Description: Measures the reduction of hazardous substances in products, such as chemicals listed under the EU's REACH regulation or the US EPA's Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). This KPI assesses the company's progress in eliminating hazardous substances from its products.
Calculation: ((Total weight of hazardous substances reduced / Total weight of hazardous substances in products) × 100) compared to a baseline year
Relevance: Essential for managing chemical risks, regulatory compliance, and enhancing brand reputation
Financial Impact: Reduced regulatory compliance costs, lower risk of product recalls, and potential cost savings from substituting hazardous substances
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value the reduction of hazardous substances in products

Description: Measures the percentage of chemicals in products that are disclosed to downstream users, such as consumers, retailers, or other stakeholders. This KPI assesses the company's transparency regarding chemical usage.
Calculation: (Total number of chemicals disclosed / Total number of chemicals used in products) × 100
Relevance: Critical for building trust with stakeholders, managing chemical risks, and complying with regulations like the EU's REACH regulation
Financial Impact: Enhanced brand reputation, reduced risk of non-compliance, and potential market benefits from transparency
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and NGOs value transparency regarding chemical usage

Description: Measures the percentage of materials sourced from sustainable suppliers, such as those certified by the Sustainable Apparel Coalition (SAC) or the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC). This KPI assesses the company's commitment to sustainable material sourcing.
Calculation: (Total weight of sustainable materials sourced / Total weight of materials sourced) × 100
Relevance: Essential for reducing environmental impacts, managing supply chain risks, and enhancing brand reputation
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from sustainable sourcing, reduced supply chain risks, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value sustainable material sourcing practices

Description: Measures the percentage of products collected and recycled through take-back programs or other recycling initiatives. This KPI assesses the company's efforts to manage product waste.
Calculation: (Total weight of products collected and recycled / Total weight of products sold) × 100
Relevance: Critical for reducing waste, managing environmental impacts, and complying with extended producer responsibility (EPR) regulations
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from recycling, reduced waste management costs, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value product take-back and recycling initiatives

Description: Measures the percentage of chemicals used in products that have undergone a risk assessment to identify potential hazards. This KPI assesses the company's proactive approach to managing chemical risks.
Calculation: (Total number of chemicals assessed / Total number of chemicals used in products) × 100
Relevance: Essential for managing chemical risks, regulatory compliance, and enhancing brand reputation
Financial Impact: Reduced risk of product recalls, lower regulatory compliance costs, and potential cost savings from substituting hazardous substances
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value proactive chemical risk management

Description: Measures the company's performance in managing chemical risks in its supply chain, based on a rating system that assesses supplier performance, audit results, and corrective actions. This KPI assesses the company's ability to influence its supply chain.
Calculation: Average rating of suppliers based on a standardized rating system
Relevance: Critical for managing supply chain risks, ensuring regulatory compliance, and enhancing brand reputation
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, potential cost savings from improved supplier performance, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value effective supply chain chemical management

Description: Measures the percentage of products designed with recyclability in mind, using design-for-recyclability principles and guidelines. This KPI assesses the company's efforts to enable product recycling.
Calculation: (Total number of products designed for recyclability / Total number of products designed) × 100
Relevance: Essential for reducing waste, managing environmental impacts, and complying with EPR regulations
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from design-for-recyclability, reduced waste management costs, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value product design for recyclability

Description: Measures the percentage of hazardous substances substituted with safer alternatives in products. This KPI assesses the company's proactive approach to eliminating hazardous substances.
Calculation: (Total number of hazardous substances substituted / Total number of hazardous substances identified) × 100
Relevance: Critical for managing chemical risks, regulatory compliance, and enhancing brand reputation
Financial Impact: Reduced risk of product recalls, lower regulatory compliance costs, and potential cost savings from substituting hazardous substances
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value proactive chemical substitution

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Metric Name: Supply Chain Carbon Footprint per Unit Procured
Description: Measures the greenhouse gas emissions associated with the production and transportation of raw materials and components procured from suppliers, normalized by the number of units procured.
Calculation: Total supply chain carbon footprint (kg CO2e) / Total units procured
Relevance: Helps identify opportunities to reduce emissions and mitigate climate-related risks in the supply chain.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and reputational risks associated with climate change.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value supply chain transparency and climate action.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Measures the proportion of sustainable materials (e.g., organic cotton, recycled polyester) sourced from suppliers, relative to total materials sourced.
Calculation: (Sustainable materials sourced / Total materials sourced) × 100
Relevance: Indicates progress toward reducing environmental impacts associated with raw material extraction and processing.
Financial Impact: Can reduce costs associated with resource extraction, processing, and waste management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainable material sourcing practices.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Measures the level of water risk exposure in the supply chain, based on factors such as water scarcity, regulatory requirements, and supplier water management practices.
Calculation: Weighted average of water risk exposure scores for each supplier
Relevance: Helps identify and mitigate water-related risks in the supply chain.
Financial Impact: Reduces water-related costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value supply chain water risk management.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Metric Name: Percentage of Suppliers Engaged in Capacity Building Programs
Description: Measures the proportion of suppliers that participate in capacity building programs focused on environmental sustainability, social responsibility, and business ethics.
Calculation: (Suppliers engaged in capacity building programs / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Enhances supplier performance, reduces risks, and improves brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Can reduce costs associated with supplier non-compliance, reputational risks, and supply chain disruptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value supplier engagement and capacity building.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Measures the reduction in waste generated throughout the supply chain, relative to a baseline year.
Calculation: ((Baseline waste - Current waste) / Baseline waste) × 100
Relevance: Indicates progress toward reducing waste and improving resource efficiency in the supply chain.
Financial Impact: Can reduce waste disposal costs, improve operational efficiency, and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value supply chain waste reduction efforts.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Measures the average time it takes for materials to move through the supply chain, from procurement to delivery.
Calculation: Total lead time / Number of shipments
Relevance: Helps optimize inventory management, reduce supply chain disruptions, and improve responsiveness to customer demand.
Financial Impact: Can reduce inventory holding costs, improve cash flow, and enhance customer satisfaction.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and logistics partners value efficient supply chain operations.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Measures the level of transparency and disclosure in the supply chain, based on factors such as supplier list publication, audit reports, and sustainability performance data.
Calculation: Weighted average of transparency and disclosure scores for each supplier
Relevance: Enhances brand reputation, builds trust with stakeholders, and supports informed decision-making.
Financial Impact: Can reduce reputational risks, improve stakeholder engagement, and support business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, NGOs, and regulators value supply chain transparency and disclosure.

Disclosure Title: Environmental Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Estimates the potential impact of supply chain disruptions on business operations, based on factors such as supplier risk assessments, natural disaster scenarios, and economic shocks.
Calculation: Modeled probability of supply chain disruptions × Potential financial impact
Relevance: Helps anticipate and prepare for potential supply chain disruptions, ensuring business continuity and minimizing financial impacts.
Financial Impact: Can reduce costs associated with supply chain disruptions, reputational risks, and business continuity planning.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and business leaders value proactive supply chain risk management and resilience planning.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage of suppliers audited for labour conditions in the past 12 months, covering at least 80% of total supplier spend.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers audited / Total number of suppliers) × 100, weighted by supplier spend.
Relevance: Ensures robust monitoring of labour conditions across the supply chain, identifying potential risks and areas for improvement.
Financial Impact: Reduces reputational risk, potential fines, and remediation costs associated with non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers expect transparency and proactive management of supply chain labour risks.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage of high-risk suppliers (identified through audits or risk assessments) that have implemented corrective actions within a specified timeframe (e.g., 6 months).
Calculation: (Number of high-risk suppliers remediated / Total number of high-risk suppliers) × 100.
Relevance: Tracks effectiveness of supplier remediation efforts, ensuring timely mitigation of labour risks.
Financial Impact: Avoids potential costs associated with non-compliance, reputational damage, and supply chain disruptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and NGOs expect companies to address labour risks proactively.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Description: Total number of supply chain workers trained on labour rights, working conditions, and company expectations in the past 12 months.
Calculation: Cumulative number of workers trained through company-led or third-party programs.
Relevance: Enhances worker awareness, skills, and capacity to identify and report labour concerns.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of non-compliance, improves worker productivity, and reduces turnover.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value proactive efforts to promote worker well-being.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Description: Total number of labour standards non-compliance incidents reported or detected in the supply chain over the past 12 months.
Calculation: Cumulative number of incidents, categorized by severity and root cause.
Relevance: Identifies potential risks, tracks incident frequency, and informs corrective actions.
Financial Impact: Avoids costs associated with remediation, fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and customers expect transparency on labour risks and incidents.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Description: Assessment of supply chain transparency, based on factors such as supplier disclosure, audit reports, and worker feedback mechanisms.
Calculation: Weighted index score, combining multiple metrics (e.g., supplier disclosure rate, audit coverage, worker feedback).
Relevance: Evaluates overall supply chain transparency, facilitating stakeholder trust and informed decision-making.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces reputational risk, and attracts sustainability-conscious investors.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value transparency and accountability in supply chain management.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage of suppliers certified to recognized fair labour standards (e.g., Fair Labour Association, Social Accountability 8000).
Calculation: (Number of certified suppliers / Total number of suppliers) × 100, weighted by supplier spend.
Relevance: Verifies suppliers' adherence to fair labour practices, reducing risk and promoting responsible sourcing.
Financial Impact: Reduces reputational risk, potential fines, and remediation costs associated with non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs expect companies to promote fair labour practices.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Metric Name: Worker Feedback and Grievance Mechanism Coverage
Description: Percentage of supply chain workers with access to functional feedback and grievance mechanisms.
Calculation: (Number of workers with access to mechanisms / Total number of supply chain workers) × 100.
Relevance: Ensures workers have a voice and can report concerns, promoting a safe and respectful work environment.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of non-compliance, improves worker satisfaction, and reduces turnover.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value proactive efforts to promote worker well-being.

Disclosure Title: Labour Conditions in the Supply Chain
Metric Name: Supply Chain Labour Risk Assessment Coverage
Description: Percentage of suppliers assessed for labour risks using a recognized risk assessment methodology.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers assessed / Total number of suppliers) × 100, weighted by supplier spend.
Relevance: Identifies potential labour risks, informing proactive mitigation and remediation efforts.
Financial Impact: Reduces reputational risk, potential fines, and remediation costs associated with non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and NGOs expect companies to proactively manage supply chain labour risks.

Description: Percentage of total raw materials sourced from certified sustainable suppliers, demonstrating commitment to responsible sourcing practices and environmental stewardship.
Calculation: (Total weight of sustainably sourced raw materials / Total weight of raw materials sourced) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to manage environmental and social risks associated with raw material sourcing, ensuring long-term supply chain resilience.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, improved brand reputation, and potential cost savings through more efficient sourcing practices.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value sustainable sourcing practices, recognizing their impact on long-term business performance and environmental sustainability.

Description: Total weight of recycled materials used in production, indicating efforts to reduce waste and promote circular economy practices.
Calculation: Total weight of recycled materials used in production (MT)
Relevance: This metric highlights the company's commitment to reducing waste, conserving natural resources, and promoting sustainable materials management.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs, lower raw material procurement costs, and potential revenue benefits from products made with recycled materials.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, customers, and investors value companies that prioritize waste reduction and circular economy practices.

Description: Average score of supplier engagement assessments, evaluating the effectiveness of supplier sustainability programs and responsible sourcing practices.
Calculation: Average score of supplier engagement assessments (1-10)
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to influence supplier behavior, ensuring responsible sourcing practices and reducing supply chain risks.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, improved supplier performance, and potential cost savings through more efficient supplier management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and sustainability-focused stakeholders value companies that prioritize supplier engagement and responsible sourcing practices.

Description: Percentage reduction in raw material waste generated during production, indicating efforts to improve resource efficiency and reduce environmental impacts.
Calculation: ((Total raw material waste generated in previous year - Total raw material waste generated in current year) / Total raw material waste generated in previous year) × 100
Relevance: This metric highlights the company's commitment to reducing waste, conserving natural resources, and promoting sustainable production practices.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs, lower raw material procurement costs, and potential revenue benefits from improved resource efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, customers, and investors value companies that prioritize waste reduction and resource efficiency.

Description: Percentage of total fibers sourced from certified sustainable sources (e.g., organic cotton, recycled polyester), demonstrating commitment to responsible materials sourcing.
Calculation: (Total weight of certified sustainable fibers / Total weight of fibers sourced) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to manage environmental and social risks associated with fiber sourcing, ensuring long-term supply chain resilience.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, improved brand reputation, and potential cost savings through more efficient sourcing practices.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value sustainable fiber sourcing practices, recognizing their impact on long-term business performance and environmental sustainability.

Description: Average score of supply chain transparency assessments, evaluating the company's ability to track and disclose supply chain information.
Calculation: Average score of supply chain transparency assessments (1-10)
Relevance: This metric highlights the company's commitment to supply chain transparency, enabling stakeholders to assess supply chain risks and opportunities.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, improved brand reputation, and potential revenue benefits from transparent supply chain practices.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and sustainability-focused stakeholders value companies that prioritize supply chain transparency and disclosure.

Description: Percentage of total raw materials sourced from local suppliers, supporting local economies and reducing transportation-related environmental impacts.
Calculation: (Total weight of locally sourced raw materials / Total weight of raw materials sourced) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's commitment to supporting local communities and reducing environmental impacts associated with transportation.
Financial Impact: Reduced transportation costs, improved supply chain resilience, and potential revenue benefits from supporting local economies.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and customers value companies that prioritize local sourcing and community development.

Description: Percentage of total products with completed LCAs, evaluating environmental impacts across the product lifecycle and informing sustainable product design.
Calculation: (Total number of products with completed LCAs / Total number of products) × 100
Relevance: This metric highlights the company's commitment to understanding and managing environmental impacts across the product lifecycle.
Financial Impact: Improved product design, reduced environmental impacts, and potential revenue benefits from sustainable products.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies that prioritize sustainable product design and lifecycle management.

Description: Measures the frequency of product recalls due to safety concerns, indicating the effectiveness of product safety controls and quality assurance processes.
Calculation: (Number of product recalls / Total units sold) x 100,000
Relevance: High recall rates can damage brand reputation, lead to financial losses, and indicate inadequate product safety measures.
Financial Impact: Product recalls can result in significant costs, including repair or replacement expenses, legal fees, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies are concerned about product safety and recall rates, as they impact brand trust and financial performance.

Description: Tracks the proportion of products that meet or exceed safety certification standards, such as UL (Underwriters Laboratories) or CE (Conformité Européene) markings.
Calculation: (Number of products with safety certifications / Total products manufactured) x 100
Relevance: Compliance with safety certifications is essential for regulatory compliance, risk management, and customer trust.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can lead to fines, product seizures, and reputational damage, while compliance can reduce liability and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, customers, and investors value safety certification compliance as a indicator of product safety and risk management.

Description: Measures the frequency of customer-reported injuries related to product use, indicating potential product safety issues.
Calculation: (Number of customer-reported injuries / Total units sold) x 100,000
Relevance: High injury rates can indicate inadequate product design, testing, or safety features, impacting customer trust and brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Customer-reported injuries can lead to liability claims, reputational damage, and decreased sales.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies are concerned about customer-reported injuries, as they impact product safety and brand reputation.

Description: Tracks the proportion of products subjected to rigorous safety testing, including testing for electrical, mechanical, and thermal hazards.
Calculation: (Number of products tested / Total products manufactured) x 100
Relevance: Comprehensive safety testing is essential for identifying potential product safety issues and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Inadequate testing can lead to product recalls, liability claims, and reputational damage, while thorough testing can reduce these risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and customers value product safety testing coverage as an indicator of product safety and risk management.

Description: Measures the proportion of suppliers and sub-suppliers assessed for product safety risks, including material quality, manufacturing processes, and compliance with safety standards.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers assessed / Total suppliers) x 100
Relevance: Supply chain risk assessments are crucial for identifying potential product safety risks and ensuring compliance with safety standards.
Financial Impact: Inadequate supply chain risk assessments can lead to product safety issues, recalls, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and customers value supply chain risk assessment coverage as an indicator of product safety and risk management.

Description: Tracks the amount of product safety training and awareness programs provided to employees, including training on safety protocols, testing procedures, and regulatory requirements.
Calculation: Total hours of training / Total number of employees
Relevance: Employee training and awareness are essential for ensuring product safety and compliance with safety standards.
Financial Impact: Inadequate employee training can lead to product safety issues, recalls, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and customers value product safety training and awareness as an indicator of product safety and risk management.

Description: Measures the frequency of field corrective actions, including repairs, replacements, or upgrades, to address product safety issues.
Calculation: (Number of field corrective actions / Total units sold) x 100,000
Relevance: High field corrective action rates can indicate inadequate product design, testing, or safety features, impacting customer trust and brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Field corrective actions can result in significant costs, including repair or replacement expenses, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies are concerned about field corrective action rates, as they impact product safety and brand reputation.

Description: Tracks the proportion of products and processes subjected to predictive risk modeling, including analysis of historical data, testing results, and safety metrics.
Calculation: (Number of products and processes modeled / Total products and processes) x 100
Relevance: Predictive risk modeling is essential for identifying potential product safety risks and proactively implementing controls to mitigate those risks.
Financial Impact: Predictive risk modeling can help reduce product safety issues, recalls, and reputational damage, resulting in cost savings and improved brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and customers value predictive risk modeling coverage as an indicator of product safety and risk management.

Description: Measures the proportion of products designed with eco-friendly features, such as energy efficiency, recyclability, and reduced material usage. This metric assesses the company's commitment to sustainable product design.
Calculation: (Number of products with eco-friendly features / Total number of products) × 100
Relevance: Encourages sustainable product design, reduces environmental impacts, and meets customer demand for eco-friendly products.
Financial Impact: Drives revenue growth through premium pricing, reduces regulatory compliance costs, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value eco-friendly products and sustainable design practices.

Description: Measures the average greenhouse gas emissions associated with each product unit, from raw material extraction to end-of-life disposal or recycling. This metric assesses the company's progress in reducing product carbon footprint.
Calculation: Total product carbon footprint (kg CO2e) / Total units produced
Relevance: Helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions, manage climate-related risks, and comply with regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, mitigates climate-related risks, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers increasingly focus on climate change mitigation and carbon footprint reduction.

Description: Measures the proportion of recycled materials used in product manufacturing, reducing waste and conserving natural resources. This metric assesses the company's commitment to circular economy practices.
Calculation: (Weight of recycled materials used / Total weight of materials used) × 100
Relevance: Encourages waste reduction, conserves natural resources, and supports circular economy practices.
Financial Impact: Reduces material costs, mitigates supply chain risks, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, customers, and investors value companies that adopt circular economy practices.

Description: Measures the proportion of products collected and recycled or reused at the end of their life cycle, reducing waste and promoting circular economy practices. This metric assesses the company's commitment to responsible product end-of-life management.
Calculation: (Number of products collected and recycled or reused / Total number of products sold) × 100
Relevance: Encourages responsible product end-of-life management, reduces waste, and supports circular economy practices.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal costs, generates revenue from recycled materials, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, customers, and investors value companies that adopt responsible product end-of-life management practices.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Material Sourcing Risk Index
Description: Measures the risk associated with sourcing materials from suppliers that may have environmental or social impacts, such as deforestation, water pollution, or human rights abuses. This metric assesses the company's supply chain risk management practices.
Calculation: Weighted score based on supplier risk assessments, materiality, and mitigation measures
Relevance: Helps mitigate supply chain risks, ensures compliance with regulations, and maintains brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces supply chain risks, avoids reputational damage, and ensures long-term material sourcing.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers increasingly focus on supply chain risk management and responsible material sourcing.

Description: Measures the average lifespan of products, assessing their durability and reliability. This metric encourages product design and manufacturing practices that prioritize longevity.
Calculation: Average lifespan of products (years)
Relevance: Encourages product design and manufacturing practices that prioritize longevity, reducing waste and supporting sustainable consumption.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces warranty and maintenance costs, and generates revenue through product longevity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value durable products that reduce waste and support sustainable consumption.

Description: Measures the proportion of customers participating in take-back programs, which collect and recycle or reuse products at the end of their life cycle. This metric assesses the company's commitment to responsible product end-of-life management.
Calculation: (Number of customers participating in take-back programs / Total number of customers) × 100
Relevance: Encourages responsible product end-of-life management, reduces waste, and supports circular economy practices.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal costs, generates revenue from recycled materials, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, customers, and investors value companies that adopt responsible product end-of-life management practices.

Description: Measures the proportion of products designed for disassembly, recyclability, and reuse, reducing waste and supporting circular economy practices. This metric assesses the company's commitment to sustainable product design.
Calculation: (Number of products designed for disassembly / Total number of products) × 100
Relevance: Encourages sustainable product design, reduces waste, and supports circular economy practices.
Financial Impact: Drives revenue growth through premium pricing, reduces regulatory compliance costs, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value companies that adopt sustainable product design practices.

Metric Name: Energy Consumption per Unit of Production (ECUP)
Description: Total energy consumed per unit of finished product, reflecting operational efficiency and energy intensity of manufacturing processes.
Calculation: Total energy consumption (kWh) / Total units produced
Relevance: This metric helps manufacturers optimize energy usage, reduce costs, and minimize environmental impact, which is critical for Building Products & Furnishings companies with high energy-intensive production processes.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses, energy costs, and competitiveness in the market.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors focus on operational efficiency, cost management, and sustainability performance.

Description: Total GHG emissions per unit of finished product, reflecting the carbon footprint of manufacturing processes and energy consumption.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions (t CO2e) / Total units produced
Relevance: This metric helps manufacturers assess and manage climate-related risks, comply with regulatory requirements, and capitalize on low-carbon opportunities.
Financial Impact: Potential carbon pricing and regulatory compliance costs, as well as opportunities for cost savings and revenue growth through low-carbon products and services.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators increasingly focus on climate change mitigation and carbon management.

Description: Percentage of energy-efficient equipment installed in manufacturing facilities, reflecting the company's commitment to energy management and technology innovation.
Calculation: (Number of energy-efficient equipment units / Total equipment units) × 100
Relevance: This metric indicates the company's efforts to reduce energy consumption and GHG emissions through technology upgrades and innovation.
Financial Impact: Potential energy cost savings, reduced maintenance expenses, and extended equipment lifespan.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that invest in energy-efficient technologies and sustainable practices.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption sourced from renewable energy, reflecting the company's commitment to clean energy transition and risk mitigation.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates the company's efforts to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, manage energy price volatility, and capitalize on low-carbon opportunities.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term cost stability, reduced energy price risk, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators increasingly value companies that invest in renewable energy and reduce their carbon footprint.

Description: Percentage of manufacturing facilities with an implemented EMS, reflecting the company's commitment to systematic energy management and continuous improvement.
Calculation: (Number of facilities with EMS / Total facilities) × 100
Relevance: This metric indicates the company's efforts to establish a systematic approach to energy management, identify energy-saving opportunities, and optimize energy performance.
Financial Impact: Potential energy cost savings, reduced energy waste, and improved operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that implement robust energy management systems and demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement.

Description: Total capital expenditures related to energy management, energy efficiency, and renewable energy projects, reflecting the company's investment in energy-related initiatives.
Calculation: Total energy-related CapEx
Relevance: This metric indicates the company's commitment to energy management and sustainability, as well as its willingness to invest in energy-related projects and technologies.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term cost savings, revenue growth, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that invest in energy-related initiatives and demonstrate a commitment to sustainability.

Relevance: This metric provides a comprehensive view of energy performance, enabling companies to track progress, identify areas for improvement, and optimize energy management.

Relevance: This metric demonstrates the company's commitment to energy management, sustainability, and long-term value creation.

Description: Measures the percentage of products collected and recycled through take-back programs or other recycling initiatives. This metric evaluates the company's efforts to manage product waste and promote circular economy practices.

Relevance: Critical for reducing waste, conserving resources, and mitigating environmental impacts
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced waste disposal costs, improved resource efficiency, and enhanced brand reputation

Relevance: Essential for ensuring safe handling, use, and disposal of products, as well as regulatory compliance

Description: Measures the company's performance in managing chemical risks in its supply chain, based on a rating system that evaluates supplier performance, chemical safety protocols, and risk management practices. This metric assesses the company's ability to influence its supply chain partners.
Calculation: Average rating of supply chain partners based on a standardized rating system

Description: Tracks the amount of product safety training and awareness programs provided to employees, including training on safety protocols, testing procedures, and regulatory requirements.

Description: Measures the proportion of products collected and recycled or reused at the end of their life cycle. This metric assesses the company's efforts to manage product waste and promote circular economy practices.

Description: Measures the percentage of electronic waste (e-waste) recycled or reused, minimizing environmental harm and promoting circular economy practices.
Calculation: (E-waste recycled or reused / Total e-waste generated) × 100
Relevance: E-waste management reduces environmental risks and supports regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs and potential revenue from recycled materials.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and sustainability-focused investors value responsible e-waste management.

Description: Measures energy consumption per dollar of goods sold, considering the entire supply chain, from sourcing to delivery.
Calculation: Total supply chain energy consumption (kWh) / Total goods sold ($)
Relevance: Energy-efficient supply chains reduce costs, risks, and environmental impact.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs, improved supply chain resilience, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and suppliers value sustainable supply chain practices.

Description: Measures the percentage of fulfillment centers and suppliers with completed water risk assessments, identifying potential water-related risks.
Calculation: (Number of assessments completed / Total number of fulfillment centers and suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Water risk assessments inform strategic planning, mitigate risks, and ensure business continuity.
Financial Impact: Reduced water-related risks, costs, and potential revenue losses.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and suppliers value proactive water risk management.

Description: Measures the percentage of fulfillment centers with implemented EMS, enabling data-driven energy management and optimization.
Calculation: (Number of EMS implemented / Total number of fulfillment centers) × 100
Relevance: EMS implementation supports energy efficiency, cost savings, and sustainability goals.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and sustainability-focused stakeholders value proactive energy management practices.

Metric Name: Average Time to Resolve Data Breach Incidents
Description: Evaluates the efficiency of incident response and breach resolution processes. A shorter time indicates more effective incident management.
Calculation: Average time (in days) taken to resolve personal data breach incidents
Relevance: Critical for minimizing breach impact and maintaining customer trust.
Financial Impact: Faster resolution reduces breach-related costs, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value prompt incident response.

Description: Measures the proportion of customers opting out of data collection or targeted advertising. A lower rate indicates greater customer trust and acceptance of data practices.
Calculation: (Number of customers opting out / Total customers) x 100
Relevance: Reflects customer sentiment and trust in e-commerce data practices.
Financial Impact: Impacts revenue from targeted advertising and customer engagement.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors monitor data practices and customer engagement.

Metric Name: Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) Response Rate
Description: Evaluates the effectiveness of DSAR response processes, which are critical for regulatory compliance and customer trust. A higher rate indicates better compliance and customer service.
Calculation: (Number of DSARs responded to within regulatory timeframe / Total DSARs received) x 100
Relevance: Essential for regulatory compliance and demonstrating respect for customer data rights.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can result in regulatory fines and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, customers, and investors prioritize DSAR response and regulatory compliance.

Description: Assesses the transparency and control provided to customers over targeted advertising. A higher index score indicates better transparency and control.
Calculation: Weighted average of metrics assessing ad transparency, control, and customer communication
Relevance: Critical for building customer trust and meeting regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Impacts customer engagement, ad revenue, and regulatory compliance costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulators value ad transparency and control.

Description: Measures the adequacy of data protection resources and expertise. A higher ratio indicates better data protection and regulatory compliance.
Calculation: (Number of DPOs / Total customer interactions) x 100,000
Relevance: Essential for ensuring data protection and regulatory compliance in e-commerce.
Financial Impact: Impacts regulatory compliance costs and reputational risk.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and customers prioritize data protection and DPO expertise.

Description: Evaluates the frequency of ML model audits to ensure fairness, accuracy, and data protection. A higher rate indicates better model governance and risk management.
Calculation: (Number of ML models audited / Total ML models in use) x 100
Relevance: Critical for mitigating ML model risks and ensuring data protection.
Financial Impact: Impacts regulatory compliance costs, reputational risk, and potential revenue loss.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value ML model transparency and audit.

Metric Name: Customer Data Deletion Request Fulfillment Rate
Description: Measures the effectiveness of customer data deletion processes. A higher rate indicates better data protection and customer trust.
Calculation: (Number of data deletion requests fulfilled / Total data deletion requests) x 100
Relevance: Essential for regulatory compliance and demonstrating respect for customer data rights.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can result in regulatory fines and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, customers, and investors prioritize data deletion and regulatory compliance.

Description: Evaluates the proportion of sensitive customer data encrypted, protecting against unauthorized access.
Calculation: (Encrypted data volume / Total sensitive data volume) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to data protection and security best practices.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of data breaches, associated costs, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value robust data security measures.

Metric Name: Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Respond to Incidents
Description: Measures the average time taken to detect and respond to data security incidents, influencing incident impact and containment.
Calculation: (Sum of detection and response times for all incidents / Total incidents)
Relevance: Critical for minimizing incident impact, maintaining customer trust, and reducing costs.
Financial Impact: Faster response times reduce costs associated with incident response, fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators expect prompt incident response.

Metric Name: Security Training and Awareness Participation Rate
Description: Tracks employee participation in data security training and awareness programs, enhancing security culture.
Calculation: (Number of employees participating in training / Total employees handling sensitive data) × 100
Relevance: Essential for fostering a security-conscious workforce and reducing human error risks.
Financial Impact: Enhances data security posture, reduces incident risk, and associated costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a well-trained workforce.

Description: Measures the proportion of identified vulnerabilities remediated within a specified timeframe, minimizing potential threats.
Calculation: (Number of remediated vulnerabilities / Total identified vulnerabilities) × 100
Relevance: Critical for maintaining robust data security and reducing potential attack surfaces.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of data breaches, associated costs, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators prioritize proactive vulnerability management.

Description: Evaluates the proportion of third-party vendors assessed for data security risks, ensuring supply chain security.
Calculation: (Number of assessed vendors / Total vendors handling sensitive data) × 100
Relevance: Essential for mitigating third-party risks and maintaining customer trust.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of data breaches, associated costs, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value robust vendor risk management.

Metric Name: Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) Response Rate
Description: Tracks the proportion of DSARs responded to within regulatory timeframes, demonstrating compliance and transparency.
Calculation: (Number of DSARs responded to within timeframe / Total DSARs received) × 100
Relevance: Critical for maintaining regulatory compliance, customer trust, and reputation.
Financial Impact: Ensures compliance with regulations, reducing fines and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, customers, and investors prioritize DSAR response.

Metric Name: Cybersecurity Investment as a Percentage of IT Budget
Description: Measures the proportion of IT budget allocated to cybersecurity initiatives, enhancing data security posture.
Calculation: (Cybersecurity investment / Total IT budget) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to data security and risk management.
Financial Impact: Enhances data security posture, reduces incident risk, and associated costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value proactive cybersecurity investments.

Description: Measures the representation of underrepresented groups (e.g., women, minorities) in the workforce, leadership, and succession planning.
Calculation: (Number of underrepresented employees / Total employees) × 100
Relevance: A diverse and inclusive workforce is essential for e-commerce companies to drive innovation, creativity, and customer engagement.
Financial Impact: Improved diversity and inclusion can lead to increased employee engagement, retention, and productivity, ultimately driving business performance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and employees value diversity and inclusion, which can impact employer brand, talent attraction, and regulatory compliance.

Metric Name: Employee Training and Development Hours per Employee
Description: Measures the investment in employee skills and development, essential for e-commerce companies to stay competitive and adapt to changing market conditions.
Calculation: Total training and development hours / Total employees
Relevance: Regular training and development opportunities are crucial for employee growth, engagement, and retention in the e-commerce sector.
Financial Impact: Improved employee skills and productivity can lead to increased revenue, reduced turnover costs, and improved customer satisfaction.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, employees, and customers value a company that invests in its employees' growth and development.

Metric Name: Employee Engagement and Feedback Response Rate
Description: Measures the percentage of employees who participate in engagement surveys and provide feedback, indicating a culture of openness and transparency.
Calculation: (Number of employees who responded / Total employees surveyed) × 100
Relevance: Regular feedback and engagement are essential for e-commerce companies to understand employee concerns, ideas, and suggestions.
Financial Impact: Improved employee engagement and feedback can lead to increased productivity, retention, and customer satisfaction.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, employees, and customers value a company that listens to its employees and acts on their feedback.

Description: Measures the time it takes to fill open positions with underrepresented groups, indicating the effectiveness of diversity and inclusion strategies.
Calculation: Average time-to-hire for underrepresented groups
Relevance: E-commerce companies must prioritize diversity and inclusion in their hiring practices to build a representative workforce.
Financial Impact: Improved diversity and inclusion in hiring can lead to increased innovation, creativity, and customer engagement.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and employees value a company that prioritizes diversity and inclusion in its hiring practices.

Description: Measures the percentage of employees who remain with the company over a certain period, indicating employee satisfaction and engagement.
Calculation: (Number of employees retained / Total employees) × 100
Relevance: High employee retention rates are crucial for e-commerce companies, which rely on skilled and experienced employees to drive business performance.
Financial Impact: Improved employee retention can lead to reduced turnover costs, increased productivity, and improved customer satisfaction.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and employees value a company that prioritizes employee retention and satisfaction.

Description: Measures the pay gap between different employee groups, indicating a company's commitment to fair and equal compensation practices.
Calculation: Average pay for underrepresented groups / Average pay for majority groups
Relevance: E-commerce companies must prioritize pay equity to ensure fairness and equality in the workplace.
Financial Impact: Improved pay equity can lead to increased employee satisfaction, retention, and productivity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, employees, and customers value a company that prioritizes pay equity and fairness.

Description: Measures the number of employee-generated ideas implemented by the company, indicating a culture of innovation and employee empowerment.
Calculation: Number of employee-generated ideas implemented
Relevance: E-commerce companies must encourage employee innovation and creativity to stay competitive and adapt to changing market conditions.
Financial Impact: Improved employee-generated ideas can lead to increased innovation, productivity, and customer satisfaction.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, employees, and customers value a company that encourages employee innovation and creativity.

Description: Average weight of packaging waste reduced per shipment through optimized packaging design and material selection, reflecting operational efficiency and waste management practices.
Calculation: Total packaging waste reduced (kg or lbs) / Total shipments
Relevance: This metric measures the effectiveness of packaging optimization efforts, reducing waste and costs while improving operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Decreases packaging waste disposal costs, reduces material usage, and enhances supply chain efficiency, leading to cost savings and improved profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value efficient packaging practices, driving business performance and competitiveness.

Description: Energy consumption per square foot of distribution center space, reflecting operational efficiency and energy management practices.
Calculation: Total energy consumption (kWh) / Total distribution center square footage
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to manage energy usage and reduce environmental impact, aligning with investor expectations and regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, mitigates regulatory risks, and enhances operational efficiency, leading to improved profitability and competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value energy-efficient operations, driving business performance and long-term growth.

Description: Percentage of on-time deliveries and rate of damaged shipments, reflecting operational efficiency and product quality.
Calculation: (On-time deliveries / Total shipments) × 100 and (Damaged shipments / Total shipments) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to deliver products efficiently and effectively, meeting customer expectations and driving business performance.
Financial Impact: Enhances customer satisfaction, reduces damage-related costs, and improves operational efficiency, leading to increased revenue and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value reliable and efficient delivery practices, driving business performance and competitiveness.

Metric Name: Return Rate due to Packaging Damage
Description: Percentage of returns due to packaging damage, reflecting product protection and packaging effectiveness.
Calculation: (Returns due to packaging damage / Total returns) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to protect products during shipping, reducing returns and improving customer satisfaction.
Financial Impact: Reduces return-related costs, enhances product quality, and improves customer satisfaction, leading to increased revenue and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value effective packaging practices, driving business performance and competitiveness.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Partner Engagement and Training
Unit: Number of partners engaged and trained
Description: Number of supply chain partners engaged and trained on sustainable packaging practices, reflecting commitment to responsible sourcing and supply chain management.
Calculation: Number of partners engaged and trained
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's efforts to promote sustainable practices throughout its supply chain, aligning with customer values and regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Enhances supply chain resilience, reduces regulatory risks, and improves brand reputation, leading to increased customer loyalty and revenue.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value responsible supply chain practices, driving business performance and long-term growth.

Metric Name: Customer Feedback and Satisfaction on Packaging
Unit: Net Promoter Score (NPS) or Satisfaction Rating
Description: Customer feedback and satisfaction ratings on packaging, reflecting customer expectations and preferences.
Calculation: NPS or satisfaction rating calculation
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to meet customer expectations and preferences on packaging, driving business performance and customer loyalty.
Financial Impact: Enhances customer satisfaction, drives customer loyalty, and improves brand reputation, leading to increased revenue and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value customer-centric practices, driving business performance and competitiveness.

Description: Investment in packaging innovation and R&D, reflecting commitment to sustainable packaging solutions and long-term growth.
Calculation: Packaging R&D investment ($) or (Packaging R&D investment / Total revenue) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's efforts to develop innovative and sustainable packaging solutions, driving business performance and long-term growth.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces regulatory risks, and drives long-term growth, leading to increased revenue and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value innovative and sustainable practices, driving business performance and long-term growth.

Description: Measures the percentage of water recycled or reused in manufacturing processes, reducing freshwater intake and wastewater generation. This metric indicates progress toward circular economy goals.
Calculation: (Recycled water volume / Total water consumption) × 100
Relevance: Highlights water conservation efforts, reduces water procurement costs, and mitigates wastewater treatment expenses.
Financial Impact: Reduces water costs, lowers wastewater treatment expenses, and enhances regulatory compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, sustainability-focused investors, and customers value water recycling and reuse.

Description: Assesses the number of suppliers in high-risk water basins, considering factors like water scarcity, regulatory environment, and supplier engagement. This metric helps identify potential supply chain disruptions.
Calculation: Number of suppliers in high-risk water basins / Total suppliers
Relevance: Essential for managing supply chain water-related risks, ensuring business continuity, and maintaining stakeholder trust.
Financial Impact: Potential supply chain disruptions, increased costs, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and risk management teams focus on supply chain resilience and water risk management.

Description: Measures capital expenditures related to water management, including investments in water-saving technologies, recycling infrastructure, and wastewater treatment. This metric indicates commitment to water stewardship.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures for water management
Relevance: Demonstrates investment in water management infrastructure, reducing water-related risks and costs.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational expenses, capital expenditures, and long-term cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, financial analysts, and stakeholders interested in water management performance.

Description: Measures progress toward reducing freshwater withdrawals, considering both direct and indirect water usage. This metric indicates commitment to water conservation.
Calculation: (Freshwater withdrawal reduction target - Current freshwater withdrawal) / Current freshwater withdrawal × 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating progress toward water conservation goals, reducing water-related risks, and enhancing sustainability performance.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced water procurement, lower wastewater treatment expenses, and enhanced regulatory compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, environmental groups, and stakeholders interested in sustainability performance.

Description: Assesses the maturity of water management practices, including policies, procedures, and performance metrics. This metric helps identify areas for improvement.
Calculation: Evaluation of water management practices against a maturity model (e.g., 1-5 scale)
Relevance: Essential for evaluating water management performance, identifying areas for improvement, and enhancing sustainability performance.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from improved water management, reduced water-related risks, and enhanced stakeholder trust.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and stakeholders interested in sustainability performance and water stewardship.

Description: Measures the effectiveness of wastewater treatment processes, considering factors like treatment capacity, efficiency, and regulatory compliance. This metric indicates environmental performance.
Calculation: (Treated wastewater volume / Total wastewater generated) × 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating environmental performance, reducing wastewater-related risks, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects wastewater treatment expenses, regulatory compliance costs, and potential environmental liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders interested in environmental performance.

Description: Measures the total water footprint of a product, considering both direct and indirect water usage throughout the value chain. This metric helps assess product-level water efficiency.
Calculation: Total water footprint (liters) / Total products produced
Relevance: Essential for evaluating product-level water efficiency, identifying areas for improvement, and enhancing sustainability performance.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced water usage, lower wastewater treatment expenses, and enhanced product competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and stakeholders interested in product sustainability and water efficiency.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Description: Evaluates the environmental impact of products based on eco-toxicity assessments, considering factors such as biodegradability, aquatic toxicity, and bioaccumulation. This metric helps identify areas for product formulation improvement.
Calculation: Weighted average eco-toxicity score based on product portfolio
Relevance: Supports strategic decision-making on product sustainability and environmental stewardship.
Financial Impact: Eco-friendly products can command premium prices, drive market share gains, and reduce regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental organizations, customers, and investors increasingly value eco-friendly products and sustainable practices.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Description: Measures the proportion of suppliers assessed for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks, ensuring that suppliers adhere to the company's sustainability standards.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers assessed / Total suppliers) x 100
Relevance: Critical for managing supply chain risks, ensuring compliance with sustainability standards, and mitigating reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Supply chain disruptions and reputational damage can result from unmanaged ESG risks, impacting business continuity and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs expect companies to ensure responsible supply chain practices.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Unit: Percentage of products collected and recycled (%)
Description: Tracks the rate of product take-back and recycling, measuring the effectiveness of closed-loop product management and circular economy strategies.
Calculation: (Total products collected and recycled / Total products sold) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating product end-of-life management, waste reduction, and resource conservation.
Financial Impact: Closed-loop product management can generate revenue from recycled materials, reduce waste disposal costs, and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental organizations value companies' efforts to minimize waste and promote circular economy practices.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Description: Measures the effectiveness of customer complaint resolution processes, ensuring timely and satisfactory responses to customer concerns.
Calculation: (Number of complaints resolved / Total complaints received) x 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating customer satisfaction, product quality, and responsiveness to customer concerns.
Financial Impact: Effective complaint resolution can enhance customer loyalty, reduce churn, and maintain market share.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers expect prompt and satisfactory resolution of complaints, influencing brand reputation and loyalty.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Description: Evaluates product sustainability performance based on a comprehensive index considering factors such as energy efficiency, water usage, and material selection.
Calculation: Weighted average index score based on product portfolio
Relevance: Supports strategic decision-making on product development, sustainability performance, and market differentiation.
Financial Impact: Sustainable products can command premium prices, drive market share gains, and reduce regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs increasingly value sustainable products and practices.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Description: Tracks the rate of regulatory compliance for products, ensuring adherence to relevant safety, environmental, and labeling standards.
Calculation: (Number of compliant products / Total products) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating regulatory risk management, product safety, and compliance with industry standards.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can result in costly fines, product recalls, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, investors, and customers expect companies to ensure compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

Disclosure Title: Product Environmental, Health and Safety Performance
Description: Measures the time required to develop new products or reformulate existing ones, influencing the company's ability to innovate and respond to market trends.
Calculation: Average product development cycle time
Relevance: Critical for evaluating innovation capacity, responsiveness to market trends, and competitiveness.
Financial Impact: Shorter product development cycle times can drive market share gains, revenue growth, and competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and competitors value companies' ability to innovate and respond to changing market conditions.

Description: This metric measures the proportion of recycled content in packaging materials, indicating progress toward a circular economy. It reflects the company's commitment to sustainable packaging practices.
Calculation: (Recycled content in packaging materials / Total packaging materials) × 100
Relevance: Recycled content in packaging reduces waste, conserves natural resources, and supports regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduces packaging material costs, minimizes waste disposal expenses, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value companies with sustainable packaging practices.

Description: This metric measures the reduction in packaging waste generated per unit of product sold, reflecting the company's efforts to minimize environmental impact.
Calculation: ((Packaging waste generated in previous year - Packaging waste generated in current year) / Packaging waste generated in previous year) × 100
Relevance: Packaging waste reduction is essential for minimizing environmental impact, reducing waste disposal costs, and enhancing brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal expenses, minimizes regulatory risks, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with effective packaging waste reduction strategies.

Unit: Kilograms of biodegradable packaging material used (kg)
Description: This metric measures the use of biodegradable packaging materials, which can reduce environmental impact and support a circular economy.
Calculation: Total biodegradable packaging material used (kg)
Relevance: Biodegradable packaging materials can reduce environmental impact, minimize waste disposal costs, and enhance brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces packaging material costs, minimizes waste disposal expenses, and mitigates regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value companies with sustainable packaging practices.

Description: This metric measures the proportion of packaging designs that meet recyclability standards, indicating the company's commitment to sustainable packaging practices.
Calculation: (Number of packaging designs meeting recyclability standards / Total packaging designs) × 100
Relevance: Packaging design for recyclability supports a circular economy, reduces waste, and enhances brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces packaging material costs, minimizes waste disposal expenses, and mitigates regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with sustainable packaging practices.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Packaging Material Sourcing Transparency
Unit: Percentage of suppliers meeting sustainability standards (%)
Description: This metric measures the transparency of packaging material sourcing from suppliers, ensuring that they meet sustainability standards.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers meeting sustainability standards / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Supply chain transparency is essential for ensuring sustainable packaging practices, minimizing risks, and enhancing brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces supply chain risks, minimizes costs associated with non-compliance, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with transparent and sustainable supply chains.

Description: This metric measures the proportion of packaging materials collected at the end of their life cycle, indicating the company's commitment to a circular economy.
Calculation: (Amount of packaging materials collected / Total packaging materials used) × 100
Relevance: End-of-life packaging collection supports a circular economy, reduces waste, and enhances brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal expenses, minimizes regulatory risks, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with effective end-of-life packaging collection strategies.

Unit: Number of customers engaged through packaging-related initiatives
Description: This metric measures customer engagement through packaging-related initiatives, such as take-back programs or recycling campaigns.
Calculation: Number of customers engaged through packaging-related initiatives
Relevance: Customer engagement through packaging-related initiatives enhances brand reputation, supports sustainable practices, and drives business growth.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, drives customer loyalty, and supports business growth.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value companies with effective customer engagement strategies.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Quantifies the proportion of palm oil sourced from high-risk areas prone to deforestation and habitat loss, enabling proactive risk management and mitigation.
Calculation: (Palm oil volume from high-risk areas / Total palm oil volume) × 100
Relevance: Critical for identifying and addressing potential environmental risks, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, and maintaining stakeholder trust.
Financial Impact: Affects long-term supply chain resilience, regulatory compliance costs, and reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers prioritize deforestation and habitat conservation.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Measures the proportion of palm oil suppliers that have undergone a social impact assessment, ensuring that social risks are identified and addressed.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers with SIA / Total number of palm oil suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Essential for proactively managing social risks, ensuring compliance with human rights standards, and maintaining stakeholder trust.
Financial Impact: Affects supply chain resilience, regulatory compliance costs, and reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers prioritize respect for human rights and fair labor practices.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Measures the efficiency of palm oil production, enabling optimization of land use, reduction of environmental impacts, and improved resource productivity.
Calculation: Total palm oil production (tons) / Total harvested area (hectares)
Relevance: Critical for optimizing resource use, reducing environmental footprint, and improving operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Directly affects production costs, profitability, and supply chain resilience.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value efficient resource use and sustainable production practices.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Evaluates the transparency of palm oil supply chain information, including supplier disclosure, mapping, and reporting.
Calculation: Based on a weighted assessment of supplier disclosure, data quality, and reporting completeness.
Relevance: Essential for demonstrating accountability, building trust with stakeholders, and facilitating responsible sourcing practices.
Financial Impact: Affects supply chain resilience, reputational risks, and stakeholder engagement.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers prioritize transparency and accountability.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Measures the proportion of HCV areas protected and conserved within the palm oil supply chain, ensuring preservation of biodiversity and ecosystem services.
Calculation: (Protected HCV area / Total HCV area) × 100
Relevance: Critical for mitigating environmental impacts, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, and maintaining stakeholder trust.
Financial Impact: Affects long-term supply chain resilience, regulatory compliance costs, and reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers prioritize conservation of biodiversity and ecosystem services.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Measures the proportion of smallholder farmers engaged in sustainable palm oil practices, promoting inclusive and responsible sourcing.
Calculation: (Number of engaged smallholder farmers / Total number of smallholder farmers) × 100
Relevance: Essential for promoting social equity, improving livelihoods, and ensuring sustainable sourcing practices.
Financial Impact: Affects supply chain resilience, social license to operate, and long-term profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers prioritize inclusive and responsible sourcing practices.

Disclosure Title: Environmental & Social Impacts of Palm Oil Supply Chain
Description: Measures the reduction of palm oil-related waste, including effluent, biomass, and packaging waste, promoting resource efficiency and waste minimization.
Calculation: ((Initial waste volume - Final waste volume) / Initial waste volume) × 100
Relevance: Critical for reducing environmental impacts, improving operational efficiency, and minimizing waste-related costs.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, waste management expenses, and environmental compliance costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs prioritize waste reduction and resource efficiency.

Metric Name: Renewable Energy Percentage in Distribution Centers
Description: This metric measures the percentage of renewable energy used in distribution centers, indicating a company's commitment to clean energy transition and risk mitigation.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates a company's efforts to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, manage energy-related risks, and capitalize on opportunities in clean energy.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability, regulatory compliance benefits, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainability commitments and clean energy adoption.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of energy-efficient lighting adopted across retail locations, indicating progress toward reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
Calculation: (Number of energy-efficient lighting fixtures / Total lighting fixtures) × 100
Relevance: Energy-efficient lighting reduces energy consumption, maintenance costs, and environmental impact.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, improves operational efficiency, and extends equipment lifespan.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies focus on energy efficiency and sustainability performance.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of retail locations and distribution centers covered by an energy management system (EMS), indicating a company's ability to monitor, control, and optimize energy consumption.
Calculation: (Number of locations with EMS / Total locations) × 100
Relevance: EMS coverage enables data-driven decision-making, energy efficiency opportunities, and reduced energy-related risks.
