Description: Tracks the number of human rights incidents, including allegations of violence, intimidation, or discrimination, per 1,000 employees.
Calculation: (Total human rights incidents / Total employees) x 1,000
Relevance: Critical for identifying potential risks, ensuring compliance with human rights standards, and protecting reputation.
Financial Impact: Human rights incidents can result in costly investigations, litigation, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and NGOs prioritize robust human rights management.

Disclosure Title: Security, Human Rights & Rights of Indigenous Peoples
Description: Measures the proportion of total operating expenses dedicated to security-related activities, including personnel, equipment, and services.
Calculation: (Security-related expenditures / Total operating expenses) x 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's investment in maintaining a secure operating environment and mitigating security risks.
Financial Impact: Effective security management can reduce costs associated with incidents, litigation, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators monitor security-related expenditures to assess operational risks.

Disclosure Title: Security, Human Rights & Rights of Indigenous Peoples
Description: Tracks the percentage of indigenous communities that have provided FPIC for projects or operations.
Calculation: (Number of communities with FPIC / Total number of indigenous communities) x 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring respect for indigenous rights, reducing reputational risks, and maintaining social license to operate.
Financial Impact: FPIC adoption can reduce project delays, costs, and reputational damage associated with indigenous community disputes.
Stakeholder Perspective: Indigenous communities, investors, and regulators prioritize FPIC adoption.

Disclosure Title: Security, Human Rights & Rights of Indigenous Peoples
Description: Measures the proportion of total capital expenditures dedicated to community development projects, including education, healthcare, and economic empowerment initiatives.
Calculation: (Community development investments / Total capital expenditures) x 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's commitment to contributing to the well-being of host communities and fostering positive relationships.
Financial Impact: Community development investments can enhance reputation, reduce social risks, and create long-term value.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and local communities prioritize community development investments.

Disclosure Title: Security, Human Rights & Rights of Indigenous Peoples
Description: Tracks the average response time to security incidents, including response to reports of violence, intimidation, or other security threats.
Calculation: (Total response time for security incidents / Total number of incidents)
Relevance: Critical for ensuring prompt and effective response to security incidents, minimizing harm to people and assets.
Financial Impact: Effective security incident response can reduce costs associated with incidents, litigation, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and NGOs prioritize robust security incident response.

Disclosure Title: Security, Human Rights & Rights of Indigenous Peoples
Description: Measures the percentage of employees who have received human rights training, including training on company policies, procedures, and standards.
Calculation: (Number of employees trained / Total number of employees) x 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring that employees understand their roles and responsibilities in upholding human rights standards.
Financial Impact: Human rights training can reduce risks associated with non-compliance, incidents, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and NGOs prioritize human rights training and capacity building.

Disclosure Title: Security, Human Rights & Rights of Indigenous Peoples
Unit: Percentage of total employment and procurement spend
Description: Tracks the percentage of indigenous peoples employed by the company and the proportion of procurement spend with indigenous-owned businesses.
Calculation: ((Indigenous employment / Total employment) + (Indigenous procurement spend / Total procurement spend)) / 2
Relevance: Indicates the company's commitment to supporting indigenous economic development and creating shared value.
Financial Impact: Indigenous employment and procurement can enhance reputation, reduce social risks, and create long-term value.
Stakeholder Perspective: Indigenous communities, investors, and regulators prioritize indigenous employment and procurement.

Description: This metric tracks the company's effectiveness in resolving community complaints and concerns in a timely and satisfactory manner.
Calculation: (Number of complaints resolved / Total number of complaints received) × 100
Relevance: This metric is crucial for assessing the company's responsiveness to community concerns and its ability to manage social risks.
Financial Impact: Effective complaint resolution can reduce reputational risks, litigation costs, and regulatory penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities and investors value transparent and effective complaint resolution processes.

Description: This metric measures the proportion of local workers in the company's workforce, reflecting its commitment to supporting local economic development.
Calculation: (Number of local workers / Total workforce) × 100
Relevance: This metric is important for demonstrating the company's efforts to contribute to local economic growth and create jobs.
Financial Impact: A local workforce can lead to improved community relations, reduced transportation costs, and enhanced operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulatory bodies value companies that support local economic development.

Metric Name: Community Health and Safety Incident Rate
Description: This metric tracks the company's performance in ensuring the health and safety of local communities, particularly in areas surrounding its operations.
Calculation: (Number of community health and safety incidents / Total workforce) × 100
Relevance: This metric is essential for assessing the company's commitment to protecting local communities from health and safety risks.
Financial Impact: Community health and safety incidents can lead to reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and litigation costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulatory bodies prioritize community health and safety.

Description: This metric measures the company's progress in rehabilitating land affected by its operations, reflecting its commitment to environmental stewardship.
Calculation: (Area of rehabilitated land / Total area affected) × 100
Relevance: This metric is crucial for demonstrating the company's efforts to mitigate environmental impacts and restore ecosystems.
Financial Impact: Land rehabilitation can reduce environmental liabilities, regulatory risks, and costs associated with land restoration.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and regulatory bodies value companies that prioritize land rehabilitation.

Description: This metric tracks the company's frequency of engagement with local communities, reflecting its commitment to transparency and communication.
Calculation: Total number of community engagement activities per year
Relevance: This metric is essential for demonstrating the company's efforts to build trust and foster positive relationships with local communities.
Financial Impact: Regular community engagement can lead to improved social license to operate, reduced reputational risks, and enhanced stakeholder relationships.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulatory bodies value transparent and regular communication.

Description: This metric measures the company's spending on local goods and services, reflecting its commitment to supporting local economic development.
Calculation: Total local procurement spend
Relevance: This metric is important for demonstrating the company's efforts to contribute to local economic growth and create jobs.
Financial Impact: Local procurement can lead to improved community relations, reduced costs, and enhanced operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulatory bodies value companies that support local economic development.

Unit: Number of beneficiaries or program metrics (e.g., education, healthcare)
Description: This metric assesses the impact of the company's community development programs, reflecting its commitment to creating positive social outcomes.
Calculation: Program-specific metrics (e.g., number of students educated, patients treated)
Relevance: This metric is essential for demonstrating the company's efforts to create lasting social value and improve community well-being.
Financial Impact: Effective community development programs can lead to improved social license to operate, enhanced reputation, and reduced regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulatory bodies value companies that prioritize community development and social responsibility.

Description: Tracks the total number of recordable work-related injuries, including those that result in lost time, restricted work, or medical treatment, to assess the overall effectiveness of health and safety programs.
Calculation: (Number of recordable injuries / Total hours worked) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Provides a comprehensive view of workplace safety performance, enabling targeted interventions to reduce incidents.
Financial Impact: Influences operational costs, insurance premiums, and reputational risk.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulators rely on TRIR to evaluate a company's commitment to workplace safety.

Metric Name: Workforce Health and Safety Training Coverage
Description: Measures the proportion of employees who have received health and safety training, ensuring they are equipped to perform their jobs safely.
Calculation: (Number of employees trained / Total workforce) x 100
Relevance: Essential for maintaining a safe working environment, reducing risk, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential fines or penalties for non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a well-trained workforce, and high training coverage rates indicate a company's commitment to health and safety.

Description: Tracks the frequency of work-related fatalities and critical injuries, providing insight into the most severe health and safety incidents.
Calculation: (Number of fatalities and critical injuries / Total hours worked) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Critical for monitoring and improving workplace safety, reducing risk, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential fines or penalties for non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a safe working environment, and low FCIR rates indicate a company's commitment to health and safety.

Description: Measures employee perceptions of their health, wellbeing, and job satisfaction, providing insight into the effectiveness of health and wellbeing programs.
Calculation: Aggregate score from employee surveys and feedback
Relevance: Essential for maintaining a healthy and engaged workforce, reducing turnover, and improving productivity.
Financial Impact: Influences operational costs, employee retention, and reputational risk.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulators value a healthy and engaged workforce, and high EHWI scores indicate a company's commitment to employee wellbeing.

Metric Name: Compliance with Health and Safety Regulations
Description: Tracks compliance with relevant health and safety regulations, ensuring the company meets or exceeds regulatory requirements.
Calculation: (Number of compliant sites / Total sites) x 100
Relevance: Critical for maintaining regulatory compliance, reducing risk, and avoiding fines or penalties.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential fines or penalties for non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value regulatory compliance, and high compliance rates indicate a company's commitment to health and safety.

Description: Measures the proportion of employees who return to work after a work-related injury or illness, providing insight into the effectiveness of return-to-work programs.
Calculation: (Number of employees returned to work / Total employees on leave) x 100
Relevance: Essential for maintaining a healthy and engaged workforce, reducing turnover, and improving productivity.
Financial Impact: Influences operational costs, employee retention, and reputational risk.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulators value a supportive work environment, and high RTW rates indicate a company's commitment to employee wellbeing.

Metric Name: Health and Safety Management System Maturity
Description: Assesses the maturity and effectiveness of health and safety management systems, including policies, procedures, and training programs.
Calculation: Aggregate score from internal audits and assessments
Relevance: Critical for maintaining a safe working environment, reducing risk, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential fines or penalties for non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a robust health and safety management system, and high maturity levels indicate a company's commitment to health and safety.

Metric Name: Capital Expenditures per Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE) Added
Description: Measures the efficiency of capital expenditures in adding new reserves, providing insight into the company's capital allocation effectiveness.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures for exploration and production / Total BOE added to 2P reserves
Relevance: Helps evaluate the company's capital efficiency and ability to generate returns on investments.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's profitability and return on investment (ROI) for shareholders.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and analysts use this metric to assess the company's capital discipline and efficiency.

Description: Measures the number of years a company's 2P reserves will last at current production rates, indicating the sustainability of its production profile.
Calculation: Total 2P reserves / Annual production
Relevance: Provides insight into the company's ability to maintain production levels and meet future demand.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's long-term valuation and ability to secure future cash flows.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, analysts, and regulators focus on this metric to assess the company's ability to sustain production.

Description: Measures the percentage of successful exploration wells drilled, indicating the company's ability to discover new reserves.
Calculation: (Number of successful exploration wells / Total exploration wells drilled) × 100
Relevance: Provides insight into the company's exploration effectiveness and ability to replace produced reserves.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's future cash flows and valuation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and analysts focus on this metric to assess the company's exploration performance.

Metric Name: Capital Expenditures as a Percentage of Operating Cash Flow
Description: Measures the company's ability to fund its capital expenditures from operating cash flows, indicating its financial resilience.
Calculation: (Capital expenditures / Operating cash flow) × 100
Relevance: Provides insight into the company's financial flexibility and ability to invest in its business while maintaining financial stability.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's ability to maintain its dividend, reduce debt, or invest in growth opportunities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and analysts focus on this metric to assess the company's financial discipline and sustainability.

Description: Measures the company's operational efficiency and productivity, indicating its ability to generate production per employee.
Calculation: Total BOE produced / Total number of employees
Relevance: Provides insight into the company's operational performance and ability to optimize its workforce.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's profitability and competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and analysts use this metric to assess the company's operational efficiency.

Metric Name: Forward-Looking Capital Allocation to Low-Carbon Initiatives
Description: Measures the company's commitment to transitioning to a lower-carbon business model, indicating its long-term resilience.
Calculation: (Capital allocated to low-carbon initiatives / Total capital expenditures) × 100
Relevance: Provides insight into the company's strategic planning and commitment to reducing its carbon footprint.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's long-term valuation and ability to adapt to changing market conditions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, analysts, and regulators focus on this metric to assess the company's commitment to sustainability.

Metric Name: Impairment Charges as a Percentage of Total Assets
Description: Measures the company's asset quality and impairment risk, indicating potential future write-downs.
Calculation: (Impairment charges / Total assets) × 100
Relevance: Provides insight into the company's asset valuation and potential future losses.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's profitability and valuation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and analysts focus on this metric to assess the company's asset quality and potential risks.

Description: Tracks the organization's responsiveness to whistleblower reports, ensuring that concerns are addressed promptly and effectively, and that a culture of openness and accountability is fostered.
Calculation: (Number of whistleblower incidents responded to within established timelines / Total number of whistleblower incidents) × 100
Relevance: Critical for demonstrating a commitment to transparency, accountability, and business ethics in the face of potential misconduct.
Financial Impact: Effective incident response can mitigate reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and financial losses.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a strong whistleblower response process as an indicator of a company's commitment to business ethics.

Description: Measures the transparency and accuracy of payments made to governments, ensuring compliance with relevant regulations, such as the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI).
Calculation: Total payments made to governments, disclosed by country and project, as a percentage of total revenue
Relevance: Vital for demonstrating accountability and transparency in dealings with governments, reducing the risk of corruption and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Transparent payments can help build trust with stakeholders, reduce reputational risks, and ensure compliance with regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and civil society organizations value transparency in payments to governments as a key indicator of business ethics.

Description: Tracks the proportion of business partners (e.g., suppliers, contractors) assessed for risks related to business ethics, corruption, and human rights.
Calculation: (Number of business partners assessed for risk / Total number of business partners) × 100
Relevance: Essential for managing risks associated with business partners, ensuring that they adhere to similar standards of business ethics and integrity.
Financial Impact: Effective risk assessment can mitigate reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and financial losses associated with business partner misconduct.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to manage business partner risks effectively.

Description: Measures the investment in employee training on business ethics, ensuring that employees understand the importance of integrity, compliance, and responsible business practices.
Calculation: Total hours of business ethics training provided to employees / Total number of employees
Relevance: Critical for fostering a culture of business ethics and integrity within the organization, reducing the risk of misconduct.
Financial Impact: Effective employee training can mitigate reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and financial losses associated with misconduct.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a strong business ethics training program as an indicator of a company's commitment to responsible business practices.

Description: Tracks the effectiveness of grievance mechanisms in place for stakeholders (e.g., employees, communities) to report concerns or complaints related to business ethics.
Calculation: (Number of grievances resolved within established timelines / Total number of grievances received) × 100
Relevance: Essential for demonstrating a commitment to accountability, transparency, and stakeholder engagement.
Financial Impact: Effective grievance mechanisms can mitigate reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and financial losses associated with unresolved grievances.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and stakeholders value a robust grievance mechanism as an indicator of a company's commitment to business ethics.

Description: Measures the company's compliance with anti-bribery laws and regulations, ensuring that adequate controls are in place to prevent bribery and corruption.
Calculation: (Number of anti-bribery law compliance assessments completed / Total number of required assessments) × 100
Relevance: Critical for managing regulatory risks, maintaining a strong reputation, and ensuring business integrity.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can result in significant fines, reputational damage, and loss of business opportunities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to maintain high standards of anti-bribery compliance.

Description: Tracks the level of engagement with stakeholders (e.g., investors, communities, NGOs) on business ethics issues, ensuring that the company is responsive to stakeholder concerns and expectations.
Calculation: Total number of stakeholder engagements on business ethics issues
Relevance: Essential for demonstrating a commitment to transparency, accountability, and stakeholder engagement on business ethics issues.
Financial Impact: Effective stakeholder engagement can mitigate reputational damage, regulatory penalties, and financial losses associated with business ethics issues.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and stakeholders value a company's engagement on business ethics issues as an indicator of its commitment to responsible business practices.

Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's commitment to compliance and risk management.

Metric Name: Lobbying and Political Contribution Transparency Index
Description: Measures the transparency of the company's lobbying and political contributions, including disclosure of activities, expenditures, and recipients. Relevance: Essential for evaluating the company's commitment to transparency and accountability in its interactions with governments and regulatory bodies.
Financial Impact: Transparency in lobbying and political contributions can mitigate reputational risks and support long-term business relationships.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, civil society organizations, and regulators focus on transparency and accountability in corporate interactions with governments.
