Description: Measures the percentage of operating assets with established environmental regulatory contingency plans in place, including procedures for spills, leaks, or other environmental incidents. This metric assesses the company's preparedness for environmental incidents and regulatory compliance.
Calculation: (Number of assets with contingency plans / Total number of operating assets) × 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's preparedness for environmental incidents and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Effective contingency planning can reduce costs associated with environmental incidents, fines, and penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and local communities focus on the company's ability to manage environmental risks and respond to incidents.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Measures the company's engagement with local communities and disclosure of community-related activities, including community investment, employment, and benefit sharing. This metric assesses the company's social license to operate and community relationships.
Calculation: Based on a weighted score of metrics, including: (1) community engagement activities, (2) disclosure of community investment, and (3) benefit sharing arrangements.
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the company's social license to operate and community relationships.
Financial Impact: Strong community relationships can support long-term business viability and access to resources.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and civil society organizations focus on the company's social responsibility and community engagement.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Measures the average lead time for implementing changes to regulatory requirements, including updates to policies, procedures, and practices. This metric assesses the company's ability to adapt to changing regulatory environments.
Calculation: Average lead time for implementing regulatory changes
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's ability to adapt to changing regulatory environments and manage compliance risks.
Financial Impact: Effective regulatory change management can reduce costs associated with non-compliance and support business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers focus on the company's ability to manage regulatory risks and adapt to changing environments.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Measures the percentage of operating assets subject to compliance-related audits and assurance activities, including internal and external audits. This metric assesses the company's commitment to independent assurance and compliance verification.
Calculation: (Number of assets audited / Total number of operating assets) × 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the company's commitment to independent assurance and compliance verification.
Financial Impact: Effective audit and assurance activities can identify and mitigate compliance risks, reducing costs associated with non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers focus on the company's commitment to transparency and independent assurance.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Measures the percentage of operating assets subject to regulatory risk assessments, including identification of potential regulatory risks and opportunities. This metric assesses the company's proactive approach to regulatory risk management.
Calculation: (Number of assets assessed / Total number of operating assets) × 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's proactive approach to regulatory risk management and identification of opportunities.
Financial Impact: Effective regulatory risk assessment can identify and mitigate potential risks, reducing costs associated with non-compliance and supporting business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Important for investors, regulators, and sustainability-focused stakeholders

Description: Tracks the volume of spills and the percentage of spills contained within a specified timeframe. This metric assesses the effectiveness of spill response and containment procedures.
Calculation: Total volume of spills (barrels or liters) and (Number of spills contained / Total number of spills) x 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating environmental impact and emergency response preparedness.
Financial Impact: Affects environmental remediation costs, regulatory fines, and reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors focus on spill management and containment.

Description: Measures the percentage of assets meeting or exceeding industry-recognized integrity standards. This metric evaluates the effectiveness of asset maintenance and inspection programs.
Calculation: (Number of assets meeting integrity standards / Total number of assets) x 100
Relevance: Essential for assessing asset reliability, maintenance effectiveness, and risk of asset failure.
Financial Impact: Directly affects maintenance costs, asset lifespan, and potential downtime.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on asset integrity as a key indicator of operational reliability.

Description: Tracks the average time to respond to and contain cybersecurity incidents. This metric evaluates the effectiveness of cybersecurity incident response plans.
Calculation: Average time (hours) to respond to and contain cybersecurity incidents
Relevance: Critical for evaluating cybersecurity risk management and incident response preparedness.
Financial Impact: Affects potential losses from cyber incidents, data breaches, and regulatory fines.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers focus on cybersecurity incident response and data protection.

Description: Evaluates the maturity of risk management practices, including risk assessment, mitigation, and monitoring. This metric assesses the effectiveness of risk management frameworks.
Calculation: (Number of risk management practices meeting maturity standards / Total number of risk management practices) x 100
Relevance: Essential for assessing risk management effectiveness and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects risk exposure, insurance premiums, and potential liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and senior management focus on risk management maturity.

Description: Tracks the frequency of near-misses reported, which can indicate potential risks and areas for improvement in safety procedures.
Calculation: (Total number of near-misses reported / Total hours worked) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Important for proactive risk management, safety culture, and continuous improvement.
Financial Impact: Indirectly affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulators focus on near-miss reporting as an indicator of safety culture.

Metric Name: Emergency Response Drill Frequency and Effectiveness
Description: Evaluates the frequency and effectiveness of emergency response drills, including evacuation procedures and spill response.
Calculation: Number of drills conducted per year and (Number of effective drills / Total number of drills) x 100
Relevance: Critical for assessing emergency preparedness and response effectiveness.
Financial Impact: Affects potential losses from unprepared responses to emergencies.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and employees focus on emergency preparedness and response.

Description: Tracks the completeness, accuracy, and timeliness of critical incident data collection and reporting.
Calculation: (Number of complete and accurate data records / Total number of data records) x 100
Relevance: Essential for reliable risk management decision-making and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Affects data management costs, regulatory fines, and potential liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and senior management focus on data quality and availability.

Description: This metric measures the rate of methane leaks from midstream oil & gas operations, which is a critical component of GHG emissions. It helps to identify areas for improvement and prioritize leak detection and repair efforts.
Calculation: (Total methane emissions / Total emissions) × 100
Relevance: Methane leaks are a significant contributor to GHG emissions in the oil & gas sector. This metric helps companies prioritize leak detection and repair efforts, reducing emissions and associated risks.
Financial Impact: Reduces emissions, energy losses, and regulatory compliance expenses associated with methane leaks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors focus on methane leak rates as an indicator of operational efficiency and environmental performance.

Metric Name: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) Utilization Rate
Description: This metric measures the utilization rate of CCS technologies in midstream oil & gas operations, providing insight into the company's commitment to reducing emissions. It helps to track progress towards emission reduction targets.
Calculation: (Total CO2 captured and stored / Total CO2 emissions) × 100
Relevance: CCS technologies are critical for reducing GHG emissions in the oil & gas sector. This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to emission reduction and low-carbon transition.
Financial Impact: Reduces emissions, regulatory compliance expenses, and reputational risks associated with high emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value CCS utilization rates as they indicate a company's commitment to low-carbon transition and emission reduction.

Metric Name: GHG Emissions Reduction Target Achievement Rate
Description: This metric measures the achievement rate of GHG emissions reduction targets set by the company, providing insight into its progress towards a low-carbon future. It helps to track progress over time and demonstrate commitment to emission reduction.
Calculation: (Actual emissions reduction / Target emissions reduction) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to emission reduction and low-carbon transition. It helps to track progress over time and demonstrate accountability.
Financial Impact: Reduces emissions, regulatory compliance expenses, and reputational risks associated with high emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value emission reduction target achievement rates as they indicate a company's commitment to low-carbon transition and environmental performance.

Description: This metric measures the improvement rate in energy efficiency of midstream oil & gas operations, providing insight into operational efficiency and emission reduction efforts. It helps to track progress over time and identify areas for improvement.
Calculation: (Energy efficiency improvement / Baseline energy efficiency) × 100
Relevance: Energy efficiency improvements are critical for reducing emissions and energy costs in midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps companies track progress and identify areas for improvement.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and reputational risks associated with high emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value energy efficiency improvement rates as they indicate operational efficiency and environmental performance.

Metric Name: Fugitive Emissions Detection and Repair Rate
Description: This metric measures the rate of detection and repair of fugitive emissions from midstream oil & gas operations, providing insight into emission reduction efforts. It helps to prioritize leak detection and repair efforts.
Calculation: (Total fugitive emissions detected and repaired / Total fugitive emissions) × 100
Relevance: Fugitive emissions are a significant contributor to GHG emissions in the oil & gas sector. This metric helps companies prioritize leak detection and repair efforts, reducing emissions and associated risks.
Financial Impact: Reduces emissions, energy losses, and regulatory compliance expenses associated with fugitive emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors focus on fugitive emissions detection and repair rates as an indicator of operational efficiency and environmental performance.

Description: This metric measures the accuracy of GHG emissions forecasts for midstream oil & gas operations, providing insight into the company's ability to predict and manage emissions. It helps to identify areas for improvement in emission forecasting and management.
Calculation: (Actual emissions / Forecasted emissions) × 100
Relevance: Accurate GHG emissions forecasts are critical for effective emission management and reduction strategies. This metric helps companies evaluate their forecasting capabilities and identify areas for improvement.
Financial Impact: Improves emission management, reduces regulatory compliance expenses, and enhances investor confidence.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value GHG emissions forecast accuracy as it indicates a company's ability to manage and reduce emissions.

Description: This metric measures the ratio of low-carbon investments to total investments in midstream oil & gas operations, providing insight into a company's commitment to low-carbon transition. It helps to track progress towards a low-carbon future.
Calculation: (Low-carbon investments / Total investments) × 100
Relevance: Low-carbon investments are critical for reducing GHG emissions and transitioning to a low-carbon economy. This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to emission reduction and low-carbon transition.
Financial Impact: Enhances long-term financial sustainability, reduces regulatory compliance expenses, and improves investor confidence.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value low-carbon investment ratios as they indicate a company's commitment to low-carbon transition and environmental performance.

Description: Measures the effectiveness of methane leak detection programs in midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps identify areas for improvement in emission management.
Calculation: (Number of detected leaks / Total number of surveyed sites) × 100
Relevance: Critical for managing greenhouse gas emissions, regulatory compliance, and reducing climate change risks
Financial Impact: Reduction in methane leaks can lead to cost savings, improved regulatory compliance, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on emission management and climate change mitigation

Unit: kg VOC/ barrel of oil processed
Description: Measures the intensity of volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps identify areas for improvement in emission management.
Calculation: (Total VOC emissions / Total barrels of oil processed)
Relevance: Essential for managing air quality, regulatory compliance, and reducing health risks
Financial Impact: Reduction in VOC emissions can lead to cost savings, improved regulatory compliance, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, environmental groups, and local communities focus on air quality management and health protection

Description: Measures the proportion of midstream oil & gas operations covered by air quality monitoring systems. This metric helps ensure effective monitoring and management of air quality risks.
Calculation: (Number of monitored sites / Total number of operating sites) × 100
Relevance: Critical for managing air quality risks, regulatory compliance, and ensuring community health protection
Financial Impact: Effective monitoring can lead to cost savings, improved regulatory compliance, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, environmental groups, and local communities focus on air quality management and health protection

Description: Measures the capital expenditures invested in emission reduction projects and technologies in midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps assess the company's commitment to emission management.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures on emission reduction projects
Relevance: Essential for managing greenhouse gas emissions, regulatory compliance, and reducing climate change risks
Financial Impact: Strategic investments in emission reduction can lead to long-term cost savings and improved regulatory compliance
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors focus on strategic investments in emission management and climate change mitigation

Description: Measures the efficiency of emission abatement efforts in midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps assess the effectiveness of emission management strategies.
Calculation: (Total emissions abated / Total revenue)
Relevance: Critical for managing greenhouse gas emissions, regulatory compliance, and reducing climate change risks
Financial Impact: Improved emission abatement efficiency can lead to cost savings, improved regulatory compliance, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on emission management and climate change mitigation

Description: Measures the company's near-term emission reduction targets for midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps assess the company's commitment to emission management and climate change mitigation.
Calculation: Specific percentage reduction targets
Relevance: Essential for managing greenhouse gas emissions, regulatory compliance, and reducing climate change risks
Financial Impact: Achieving emission reduction targets can lead to cost savings, improved regulatory compliance, and enhanced brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on emission management and climate change mitigation

Description: Measures the community air quality index near midstream oil & gas operations. This metric helps assess the impact of operations on local air quality and community health.
Calculation: Average air quality index score from monitoring stations near operating sites
Relevance: Critical for managing air quality risks, regulatory compliance, and ensuring community health protection
Financial Impact: Maintaining good community air quality can lead to improved social license to operate and reduced regulatory risks
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, regulators, and environmental groups focus on air quality management and health protection

Metric Name: Water Withdrawal per Unit of Throughput
Description: Tracks water usage efficiency in midstream operations, which is essential for minimizing ecological impacts on local water resources.
Calculation: Total water withdrawal / Total energy throughput
Relevance: Important for optimizing water management, reducing costs, and mitigating water-related risks.
Financial Impact: Efficient water use can lead to cost savings, reduced regulatory risks, and improved social license to operate.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, regulators, and investors care about water usage and management practices.

Description: Measures the percentage of pipelines that meet or exceed integrity standards, which is crucial for preventing ecological damage from leaks or ruptures.
Calculation: (Number of pipelines meeting integrity standards / Total number of pipelines) × 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring safe and reliable operations, minimizing environmental harm, and complying with regulations.
Financial Impact: Maintaining pipeline integrity can prevent costly leaks, reduce regulatory penalties, and protect reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and local communities prioritize pipeline integrity due to environmental and safety concerns.

Unit: Number of incidents/million miles of pipeline
Description: Tracks the frequency of spills and leaks from midstream operations, which can have significant ecological impacts.
Calculation: Total number of spills and leaks / Total miles of pipeline
Relevance: Critical for understanding and managing operational risks, ensuring safe and reliable operations, and minimizing environmental harm.
Financial Impact: Reducing spills and leaks can prevent costly cleanups, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and environmental groups focus on spill and leak frequency due to environmental concerns.

Description: Measures the extent of conservation areas protected by the company, which helps mitigate ecological impacts on local ecosystems.
Calculation: Total acres of conservation areas
Relevance: Important for preserving biodiversity, ensuring ecosystem services, and demonstrating environmental stewardship.
Financial Impact: Conservation efforts can lead to long-term cost savings, enhanced reputation, and regulatory benefits.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and local communities prioritize biodiversity conservation.

Description: Tracks progress in improving energy efficiency in midstream operations, which reduces greenhouse gas emissions and energy consumption.
Calculation: ((Current energy consumption / Baseline energy consumption) - 1) × 100
Relevance: Essential for reducing energy costs, minimizing climate-related risks, and demonstrating operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Energy efficiency improvements can lead to cost savings, reduced regulatory risks, and enhanced reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on energy efficiency due to its climate and cost implications.

Description: Measures the percentage of land rehabilitated after use, which helps mitigate ecological impacts on local ecosystems.
Calculation: (Total acres rehabilitated / Total acres disturbed) × 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring responsible land use, minimizing environmental harm, and demonstrating environmental stewardship.
Financial Impact: Land rehabilitation can lead to long-term cost savings, enhanced reputation, and regulatory benefits.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and local communities prioritize land rehabilitation.

Description: Tracks the percentage of fugitive emissions detected and quantified, which helps mitigate climate-related risks and ensure operational efficiency.
Calculation: (Number of fugitive emissions detected / Total number of potential fugitive emissions sources) × 100
Relevance: Essential for understanding and managing climate-related risks, ensuring operational efficiency, and demonstrating environmental responsibility.
Financial Impact: Detecting and quantifying fugitive emissions can lead to cost savings, reduced regulatory risks, and enhanced reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on fugitive emissions due to their climate implications.

Description: Tracks the number of antitrust litigation cases and associated costs, reflecting the company's compliance with competition laws and potential risks.
Calculation: Number of ongoing cases and total costs incurred (or accrued) for antitrust litigation
Relevance: Critical for assessing the company's competitive behaviour, regulatory compliance, and potential financial risks.
Financial Impact: Significant costs associated with litigation, fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers closely monitor antitrust litigation exposure to evaluate the company's compliance and risk profile.

Description: Evaluates the effectiveness of the company's engagement with business partners, suppliers, and contractors to ensure alignment with its competitive behaviour standards.
Calculation: Average score from surveys or assessments of business partners, suppliers, and contractors
Relevance: Important for ensuring that business partners and suppliers adhere to the company's competitive behaviour standards.
Financial Impact: Affects relationships with key business partners, suppliers, and contractors, influencing operational efficiency and costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and business partners value strong relationships and alignment with competitive behaviour standards.

Description: Measures the number of whistleblower reports related to competitive behaviour, indicating the effectiveness of the company's reporting mechanisms and employee awareness.
Calculation: Total whistleblower reports / Total number of employees × 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the company's culture, internal controls, and responsiveness to competitive behaviour concerns.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's reputation, regulatory compliance, and potential financial risks associated with non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees closely monitor whistleblower report rates to assess the company's commitment to competitive behaviour and ethics.

Unit: Number of intelligence reports per quarter
Description: Tracks the company's ability to gather and analyze competitive intelligence, informing strategic decision-making and competitive behaviour.
Calculation: Total number of competitive intelligence reports generated per quarter
Relevance: Critical for supporting informed decision-making, market analysis, and competitive strategy development.
Financial Impact: Directly affects the company's ability to respond to market changes, anticipate competitor actions, and make informed strategic decisions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, executive management, and strategy teams value competitive intelligence gathering rates to assess the company's market awareness and responsiveness.

Description: Evaluates the company's transparency in market pricing, reflecting its commitment to fair competition and anti-price-fixing practices.
Calculation: Average score from assessments or surveys of market participants, customers, or investors
Relevance: Essential for demonstrating the company's adherence to fair market practices and anti-competitive behaviour standards.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's reputation, regulatory compliance, and potential financial risks associated with non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators closely monitor market pricing transparency to assess the company's commitment to fair competition.

Description: Measures the company's effectiveness in resolving customer complaints related to competitive behaviour, such as unfair business practices or anticompetitive actions.
Calculation: (Resolved complaints / Total complaints) × 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's responsiveness to customer concerns and commitment to fair business practices.
Financial Impact: Directly affects customer satisfaction, loyalty, and retention, influencing revenue growth and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulators closely monitor customer complaint resolution rates to assess the company's commitment to fair competition and customer satisfaction.

Metric Name: Economic Value Generated through Pro-Competitive Initiatives
Description: Tracks the economic value generated through pro-competitive initiatives, such as investments in innovation, research and development, or collaborative projects that promote fair competition.
Calculation: Total economic value generated through pro-competitive initiatives
Relevance: Essential for demonstrating the company's commitment to promoting fair competition and contributing to economic growth.
Financial Impact: Affects the company's long-term sustainability, profitability, and reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value pro-competitive initiatives as a reflection of the company's commitment to fair competition and economic growth.

Description: Tracks the frequency of updates to emergency response plans, ensuring they remain relevant and effective in addressing potential critical incidents.
Calculation: Time elapsed since last ERP update (in months)
Relevance: Reflects the company's commitment to preparedness and responsiveness to potential critical incidents.
Financial Impact: Regular updates can minimize potential losses and regulatory non-compliance costs associated with inadequate preparedness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and local communities expect companies to have up-to-date emergency response plans.

Description: Measures the effectiveness of pipeline integrity management practices, including inspections, maintenance, and repairs.
Calculation: (Number of pipelines with documented integrity management plans / Total pipelines) × 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring safe and reliable pipeline operations, minimizing risk of incidents and associated costs.
Financial Impact: Directly affects costs related to pipeline maintenance, repairs, and potential incident response.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and local communities value robust pipeline integrity management practices.

Metric Name: Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) for Critical Infrastructure
Description: Tracks the average time to repair critical infrastructure (e.g., pipelines, processing facilities) after an incident or scheduled maintenance.
Calculation: Total downtime hours / Number of repairs
Relevance: Essential for evaluating operational efficiency, minimizing downtime, and ensuring business continuity.
Financial Impact: Affects revenue and profitability due to potential production losses and repair costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators monitor MTTR as an indicator of operational effectiveness.

Description: Measures the proportion of critical equipment and infrastructure subject to risk-based inspections, ensuring proactive identification and mitigation of potential risks.
Calculation: (Number of equipment/assets inspected using RBI / Total critical equipment/assets) × 100
Relevance: Reflects the company's proactive approach to risk management and asset integrity.
Financial Impact: Can minimize costs associated with unplanned downtime, repairs, and potential incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a robust RBI program as a demonstration of risk management effectiveness.

Description: Tracks the proportion of workforce personnel with completed training and competency assessments related to critical incident risk management.
Calculation: (Number of personnel with completed training and competency assessments / Total workforce) × 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring that personnel are equipped to respond effectively to critical incidents.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational efficiency, safety performance, and potential regulatory compliance costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a well-trained workforce as a critical component of risk management.

Unit: Number of near-misses reported and investigated per million hours worked
Description: Tracks the frequency of near-miss reporting and investigation, reflecting a proactive approach to incident prevention and risk management.
Calculation: (Total near-misses reported and investigated / Total hours worked) × 1,000,000
Relevance: Encourages a culture of safety and transparency, allowing for identification and mitigation of potential risks.
Financial Impact: Can minimize costs associated with potential incidents, regulatory fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a strong safety culture and proactive risk management practices.

Description: Tracks the frequency of BCP exercises, ensuring that the company is prepared to respond effectively to critical incidents and maintain business continuity.
Calculation: Time elapsed since last BCP exercise (in months)
Relevance: Essential for ensuring that the company can respond effectively to critical incidents and minimize potential losses.
Financial Impact: Regular exercises can minimize potential losses and regulatory non-compliance costs associated with inadequate preparedness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value a robust BCP as a demonstration of risk management effectiveness and business resilience.

Description: This metric measures the rate of fugitive emissions from equipment and infrastructure, highlighting the effectiveness of leak detection and repair programs.
Calculation: (Fugitive emissions / Total GHG emissions) × 100
Relevance: Fugitive emissions are a significant contributor to GHG emissions in the oil & gas sector; reducing them can minimize emissions and associated risks.
Financial Impact: Reduces GHG emissions, regulatory compliance costs, and potential liabilities from emissions-related incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and environmental groups focus on fugitive emissions management and reduction.

Description: This metric measures the energy efficiency of the refining process, comparing energy output to energy input.
Calculation: Energy output (BTU) / Energy input (BTU)
Relevance: A higher ratio indicates better energy efficiency, reducing energy costs and GHG emissions.
Financial Impact: Improves operational efficiency, reduces energy costs, and enhances competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value energy efficiency and GHG emissions performance.

Unit: kg CH4 / barrel of refined product
Description: This metric measures methane emissions intensity, a potent GHG, per unit of refined product.
Calculation: Total methane emissions (kg CH4) / Total barrels of refined product
Relevance: Methane has a significant global warming potential; reducing emissions can minimize climate impact and associated risks.
Financial Impact: Reduces GHG emissions, regulatory compliance costs, and potential liabilities from emissions-related incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and environmental groups focus on methane emissions management and reduction.

Description: This metric tracks progress toward GHG emissions reduction targets, demonstrating commitment to sustainability and climate action.
Calculation: (GHG emissions reduction achieved / GHG emissions reduction target) × 100
Relevance: This metric helps to assess progress toward emissions reduction goals and associated strategic planning.
Financial Impact: Supports long-term business strategy, reduces regulatory risks, and enhances reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value progress toward emissions reduction targets.

Description: This metric measures the utilization rate of CCS technologies, highlighting the effectiveness of emissions reduction strategies.
Calculation: (CO2 captured and stored / Total CO2 emissions) × 100
Relevance: CCS is a critical technology for reducing GHG emissions; a higher utilization rate indicates effective deployment.
Financial Impact: Reduces GHG emissions, regulatory compliance costs, and potential liabilities from emissions-related incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and environmental groups focus on CCS deployment and utilization.

Description: This metric measures GHG emissions per unit of energy input, providing insight into the carbon intensity of energy consumption.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions (kg CO2e) / Total energy input (MMBTU)
Relevance: A lower ratio indicates better carbon performance and reduced emissions.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs and GHG emissions-related risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on carbon performance and energy efficiency.

Description: This metric estimates the potential for future GHG emissions reductions through planned initiatives and technologies.
Calculation: (Potential GHG emissions reductions / Current GHG emissions) × 100
Relevance: This metric provides insight into the company's strategic planning and commitment to future emissions reductions.
Financial Impact: Supports long-term business strategy, reduces regulatory risks, and enhances reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value forward-looking emissions reduction potential and strategic planning.

Description: Measures the efficiency of SO2 removal processes in refineries, which is critical for minimizing air pollution and complying with regulatory standards.
Calculation: (SO2 removed / SO2 input) × 100
Relevance: Effective SO2 removal is essential for reducing air pollution, complying with regulations, and minimizing environmental impact.
Financial Impact: Improving SO2 removal efficiency can reduce regulatory compliance costs, minimize environmental liabilities, and enhance operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and local communities focus on SO2 removal efficiency as a key indicator of environmental performance and regulatory compliance.

Metric Name: Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) Emissions per Unit of Production
Description: Measures the intensity of VOC emissions from refining operations, which contribute to air pollution and smog formation.
Calculation: Total VOC emissions (kg) / Total barrels refined (million)
Relevance: Reducing VOC emissions can minimize environmental impact, improve air quality, and reduce regulatory risks.
Financial Impact: Reduction in VOC emissions can lead to cost savings from reduced regulatory penalties, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on VOC emissions as a key indicator of operational efficiency and environmental stewardship.

Description: Measures the reduction in PM emissions from refineries, which contribute to air pollution and negative health impacts.
Calculation: Total PM emissions reduced (tons) compared to a baseline year
Relevance: Reducing PM emissions can improve air quality, minimize environmental impact, and reduce regulatory risks.
Financial Impact: Reduction in PM emissions can lead to cost savings from reduced regulatory penalties, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and local communities focus on PM emissions reduction as a key indicator of environmental performance and public health protection.

Description: Measures the percentage of refinery operations covered by air quality monitoring systems, which provide critical data for emissions management and regulatory compliance.
Calculation: (Number of monitored operations / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: Comprehensive air quality monitoring is essential for identifying areas for improvement, minimizing regulatory risks, and ensuring environmental stewardship.
Financial Impact: Effective air quality monitoring can reduce regulatory compliance costs, minimize environmental liabilities, and enhance operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and environmental groups focus on air quality monitoring coverage as a key indicator of environmental performance and regulatory compliance.

Metric Name: Capital Expenditures for Air Quality Improvements
Description: Measures the capital expenditures invested in air quality improvement projects, such as emissions reduction technologies and monitoring systems.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures for air quality improvements ($ million)
Relevance: Investing in air quality improvements demonstrates a commitment to environmental stewardship, regulatory compliance, and long-term sustainability.
Financial Impact: Strategic investments in air quality improvements can reduce regulatory compliance costs, minimize environmental liabilities, and enhance operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on capital expenditures for air quality improvements as a key indicator of environmental commitment and long-term strategy.

Description: Measures the percentage of refinery operations with certified AQMS, which ensure systematic management of air quality risks and compliance with regulatory standards.
Calculation: (Number of certified operations / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: AQMS certification demonstrates a commitment to environmental stewardship, regulatory compliance, and operational excellence.
Financial Impact: AQMS certification can reduce regulatory compliance costs, minimize environmental liabilities, and enhance operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and environmental groups focus on AQMS certification as a key indicator of environmental performance and regulatory compliance.

Description: Measures the company's forward-looking target for reducing air emissions, such as greenhouse gases or VOCs, which demonstrates a commitment to long-term sustainability and environmental stewardship.
Calculation: Specific target for emissions reduction by [specific year] (e.g., 20% reduction by 2025)
Relevance: Forward-looking emissions reduction targets demonstrate a commitment to long-term sustainability, environmental stewardship, and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Achieving emissions reduction targets can reduce regulatory compliance costs, minimize environmental liabilities, and enhance operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on forward-looking emissions reduction targets as a key indicator of long-term strategy and environmental commitment.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of wastewater generated during refining operations that is recycled or reused, indicating the effectiveness of wastewater management practices.
Calculation: (Wastewater recycled or reused / Total wastewater generated) × 100
Relevance: Recycling wastewater reduces the volume of wastewater discharged into the environment, conserves water resources, and decreases treatment costs.
Financial Impact: Reduced wastewater discharge can lead to cost savings on wastewater treatment and disposal; improved regulatory compliance and reduced risk of fines or penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors value wastewater recycling and reuse practices as a demonstration of environmental stewardship.

Description: This metric measures the capital expenditures related to water management, including investments in water conservation, recycling, and treatment infrastructure.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures on water-related projects
Relevance: Water-related capital expenditures demonstrate a company's commitment to water management and its impact on operational efficiency and environmental sustainability.
Financial Impact: Investments in water management can lead to long-term cost savings, improved regulatory compliance, and reduced risk of water-related disruptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on capital expenditures related to water management as an indicator of a company's strategic priorities and commitment to sustainability.

Metric Name: Freshwater Consumption per Unit of Production
Description: This metric measures the volume of freshwater consumed per unit of production (e.g., per barrel refined), providing insight into the water efficiency of refining operations.
Calculation: Total freshwater consumption (liters) / Total units produced
Relevance: Freshwater conservation is essential for oil refining, as it reduces the risk of water scarcity, supports regulatory compliance, and decreases operational costs.
Financial Impact: Reduced freshwater consumption can lead to cost savings on water procurement, treatment, and discharge; improved regulatory compliance and reduced risk of fines or penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on freshwater conservation practices and their impact on operational efficiency and environmental sustainability.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of the company's operations that have undergone a water risk assessment, indicating the effectiveness of water risk management practices.
Calculation: (Operations with completed water risk assessments / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: Water risk assessments help identify potential water-related risks and opportunities, enabling informed decision-making and strategic planning.
Financial Impact: Effective water risk management can lead to reduced risk of water-related disruptions, improved regulatory compliance, and cost savings on water management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups value water risk assessments as a demonstration of a company's proactive approach to water management.

Description: This metric measures the quality of effluent discharged from refining operations, taking into account various water quality parameters (e.g., pH, TSS, BOD).
Calculation: Weighted average of water quality parameters, normalized to an index value
Relevance: Effluent quality is a critical aspect of environmental sustainability, as it affects aquatic ecosystems and human health.
Financial Impact: Improved effluent quality can lead to reduced costs on wastewater treatment and discharge, improved regulatory compliance, and reduced risk of fines or penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors focus on effluent quality as an indicator of a company's environmental performance and commitment to sustainability.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of the company's operations that are covered by a water management policy, indicating the effectiveness of water management practices.
Calculation: (Operations with water management policies / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: Water management policies demonstrate a company's commitment to water sustainability and provide a framework for water management decision-making.
Financial Impact: Effective water management policies can lead to improved regulatory compliance, reduced risk of water-related disruptions, and cost savings on water management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups value water management policies as a demonstration of a company's proactive approach to water sustainability.

Description: This metric measures the company's target for reducing water use in refining operations over a specified period, indicating its commitment to water conservation and sustainability.
Calculation: Specified reduction target (e.g., percentage or absolute reduction)
Relevance: Future water use reduction targets demonstrate a company's commitment to water sustainability, operational efficiency, and environmental stewardship.
Financial Impact: Achieving water use reduction targets can lead to cost savings on water procurement, treatment, and discharge; improved regulatory compliance and reduced risk of fines or penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on future water use reduction targets as an indicator of a company's strategic priorities and commitment to sustainability.

Description: Tracks the frequency of safety incidents related to chemical storage, handling, and transportation, reflecting operational safety and risk management.
Calculation: Total chemical storage safety incidents / Total hours worked (in millions)
Relevance: Indicates operational safety performance, risk management effectiveness, and potential impacts on employees and the environment.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential liability for environmental damage or employee injuries.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees focus on operational safety performance and risk management.

Metric Name: Spill Response Time and Containment Rate
Description: Measures the effectiveness of spill response procedures, including response time and containment rate, reflecting operational preparedness and environmental protection.
Calculation: Average response time (hours) and percentage of spills contained within 24 hours
Relevance: Indicates operational preparedness, environmental protection, and potential impacts on ecosystems and human health.
Financial Impact: Affects environmental liability, regulatory compliance expenses, and potential costs for cleanup and restoration.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on operational preparedness and environmental protection.

Description: Tracks the frequency of hazardous materials inventory turnover, reflecting operational efficiency and waste reduction efforts.
Calculation: Total hazardous materials used / Average hazardous materials inventory
Relevance: Indicates operational efficiency, waste reduction performance, and potential cost savings.
Financial Impact: Affects inventory management costs, waste disposal expenses, and potential environmental liability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on operational efficiency and waste reduction performance.

Metric Name: Employee Training Hours on Hazardous Materials Handling
Description: Measures employee training and competence on hazardous materials handling, reflecting operational safety and risk management.
Calculation: Total training hours on hazardous materials handling / Total employees handling hazardous materials
Relevance: Indicates operational safety performance, risk management effectiveness, and potential impacts on employees and the environment.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential liability for environmental damage or employee injuries.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees focus on operational safety performance and risk management.

Metric Name: Regulatory Compliance Rate for Hazardous Materials Management
Description: Tracks the rate of regulatory compliance for hazardous materials management, reflecting operational performance and risk management.
Calculation: (Number of compliant incidents / Total incidents) × 100
Relevance: Indicates operational performance, risk management effectiveness, and potential regulatory penalties or fines.
Financial Impact: Affects regulatory compliance expenses, potential fines or penalties, and environmental liability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on regulatory compliance performance and risk management.

Description: Measures the rate of reduction in hazardous materials usage, reflecting operational efficiency and sustainability performance.
Calculation: ((Initial hazardous materials usage - Final hazardous materials usage) / Initial hazardous materials usage) × 100
Relevance: Indicates operational efficiency, sustainability performance, and potential cost savings.
Financial Impact: Affects inventory management costs, waste disposal expenses, and potential environmental liability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on sustainability performance and operational efficiency.

Metric Name: Investment in Hazardous Materials Management Technologies
Description: Tracks investment in new technologies or processes aimed at improving hazardous materials management, reflecting strategic planning and innovation.
Calculation: Total investment in hazardous materials management technologies
Relevance: Indicates strategic planning, innovation, and potential long-term cost savings or environmental benefits.
Financial Impact: Affects future operational costs, potential environmental liability, and competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on strategic planning, innovation, and long-term sustainability performance.

Description: Tracks the rate of process safety incidents (PSIs) per 1,000,000 barrels processed, which helps to evaluate the effectiveness of process safety management systems.
Calculation: (Number of PSIs / Total barrels processed) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Critical for ensuring the safe operation of refining and marketing processes, minimizing environmental impact, and preventing asset damage.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, potential environmental fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and local communities expect companies to manage process safety risks effectively.

Metric Name: Employee Training Hours per Job Category
Description: Measures the average number of training hours provided to employees per job category, which helps to assess the effectiveness of employee training programs in ensuring a safe and healthy work environment.
Calculation: Total training hours / Total number of employees per job category
Relevance: Essential for ensuring employees have the necessary skills and knowledge to perform their jobs safely and efficiently.
Financial Impact: Directly affects employee productivity, retention, and potential errors or accidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a well-trained workforce, and this metric demonstrates a company's commitment to employee development.

Description: Tracks the percentage of the workforce covered by occupational health risk assessments, which helps to identify potential health risks and implement mitigation measures.
Calculation: (Number of employees covered by risk assessments / Total workforce) x 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring a healthy work environment, reducing absenteeism, and minimizing occupational health risks.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, workers' compensation claims, and potential fines or penalties for non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a healthy work environment, and this metric demonstrates a company's commitment to occupational health.

Description: Measures the rate of near miss reports per 100 employees per year, which helps to assess the effectiveness of safety reporting and incident prevention systems.
Calculation: (Number of near miss reports / Total workforce) x 100
Relevance: Essential for identifying potential safety risks and implementing corrective actions to prevent incidents.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, potential accidents, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a proactive approach to safety management, and this metric demonstrates a company's commitment to continuous improvement.

Description: Tracks the percentage of employees engaged in health and safety activities, such as training, risk assessments, and incident reporting, which helps to assess the effectiveness of employee engagement in health and safety management.
Calculation: (Number of employees engaged / Total workforce) x 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring a safe and healthy work environment, improving employee morale, and reducing turnover.
Financial Impact: Directly affects employee productivity, retention, and potential errors or accidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a well-engaged workforce, and this metric demonstrates a company's commitment to employee involvement in health and safety.

Metric Name: Health & Safety Management System Audit Coverage
Unit: Percentage of management system elements audited
Description: Tracks the percentage of health and safety management system elements audited, which helps to assess the effectiveness of the management system and identify areas for improvement.
Calculation: (Number of audited elements / Total management system elements) x 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring the effectiveness of health and safety management systems, identifying areas for improvement, and maintaining regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, potential fines or penalties, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a robust health and safety management system, and this metric demonstrates a company's commitment to continuous improvement.

Description: Measures the average time-to-recovery (TTR) after incidents, which helps to assess the effectiveness of incident response and business continuity planning.
Calculation: Total recovery time / Number of incidents
Relevance: Critical for minimizing downtime, ensuring business continuity, and reducing reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, revenue, and potential fines or penalties for non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value a company's ability to respond effectively to incidents and maintain business continuity.

Description: Measures the percentage of clean fuel blends (e.g., low-sulfur fuels) in total fuel production, reflecting commitment to environmental sustainability.
Calculation: (Clean fuel blends / Total fuel production) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates progress toward reducing environmental impact and meeting regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Supports long-term sustainability and compliance with environmental regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and sustainability-focused investors value clean fuel production.

Description: Measures the carbon intensity of refined products, reflecting the sector's contribution to greenhouse gas emissions.
Calculation: Total CO2e emissions from refining / Total energy content of refined products
Relevance: Indicates progress toward reducing carbon footprint and managing climate-related risks.
Financial Impact: Affects costs associated with carbon pricing and regulatory compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on climate-related performance.

Description: Measures investment in research and development of low-carbon technologies, reflecting commitment to innovation and sustainability.
Calculation: Total R&D expenses allocated to low-carbon technologies
Relevance: Indicates proactive approach to managing climate-related risks and capitalizing on opportunities.
Financial Impact: Supports long-term sustainability and potential revenue growth through innovation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, executives, and sustainability-focused stakeholders value innovation and forward-looking strategies.

Description: Measures the percentage of refining capacity utilized, reflecting operational efficiency and asset management.
Calculation: (Actual refining throughput / Refining capacity) × 100
Relevance: Indicates ability to optimize refining operations and manage capacity.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, revenue, and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and executives focus on operational efficiency and asset utilization.

Description: Measures the greenhouse gas emissions associated with refined products throughout their lifecycle, from production to end-use.
Calculation: Total lifecycle GHG emissions / Total units of refined products
Relevance: Provides a comprehensive view of the sector's climate impact and opportunities for improvement.
Financial Impact: Affects costs associated with carbon pricing, regulatory compliance, and reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on climate-related performance.

Description: Measures the reduction in sulphur content of refined products, reflecting progress toward producing cleaner fuels.
Calculation: (Initial sulphur content - Final sulphur content) / Initial sulphur content
Relevance: Indicates commitment to environmental sustainability and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Supports long-term sustainability and compliance with environmental regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and sustainability-focused investors value cleaner fuel production.

Description: Measures capital expenditures on process improvements aimed at enhancing efficiency, reducing emissions, and improving product quality.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures on process improvements
Relevance: Indicates commitment to operational excellence, sustainability, and long-term competitiveness.
Financial Impact: Affects costs, revenue, and profitability through improved efficiency and product quality.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, executives, and sustainability-focused stakeholders value strategic investments in process improvements.

Description: Measures the average deviation of the company's product prices from industry benchmarks, indicating the effectiveness of pricing strategies and potential for optimization.
Calculation: Average of (Product price - Benchmark price) across a representative sample of products and time periods
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the competitiveness of pricing strategies and identifying opportunities for improvement.
Financial Impact: Impacts revenue and profitability through optimal pricing and market share management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and market analysts focus on pricing strategies and their impact on financial performance.

Description: Tracks the frequency of price changes for key products, reflecting the company's ability to adapt to market conditions while maintaining pricing integrity.
Calculation: Number of price changes per quarter for a representative sample of products
Relevance: Indicates the company's responsiveness to market dynamics and its approach to pricing strategy.
Financial Impact: Affects revenue and profitability through the balance between price adjustments and market share management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and market analysts monitor pricing dynamics and their impact on financial performance.

Metric Name: Discounting as a Percentage of Total Sales
Description: Measures the extent of discounting practices as a percentage of total sales, providing insights into pricing strategies and potential erosion of profit margins.
Calculation: (Total discounts / Total sales) × 100
Relevance: Essential for understanding the impact of discounting on profitability and pricing integrity.
Financial Impact: Directly affects revenue and profitability through the trade-off between volume growth and margin management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and management focus on maintaining healthy profit margins while managing market share.

Description: Tracks the percentage of transactions where prices charged to customers deviate from approved price lists or contracts, indicating potential pricing integrity issues.
Calculation: (Number of transactions with price discrepancies / Total transactions) × 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring compliance with pricing policies and contracts, and for mitigating revenue leakage.
Financial Impact: Impacts revenue and profitability through prevention of revenue leakage and maintenance of pricing integrity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, auditors, and compliance officers focus on internal controls and pricing integrity.

Description: Measures customer satisfaction with pricing practices through surveys or feedback mechanisms, reflecting the perceived fairness and transparency of prices.
Calculation: Average score from customer surveys or feedback, normalized to a 1-100 scale
Relevance: Essential for understanding customer perceptions of pricing practices and their impact on customer loyalty and retention.
Financial Impact: Affects revenue and profitability through customer retention and potential price elasticity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value customer satisfaction and its impact on long-term financial performance.

Description: Tracks the percentage of products or transactions that comply with regulatory pricing requirements, indicating the effectiveness of pricing governance and compliance processes.
Calculation: (Number of compliant transactions / Total transactions) × 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and avoiding potential fines or penalties.
Financial Impact: Impacts profitability through prevention of regulatory fines and penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, investors, and compliance officers focus on regulatory compliance.

Description: Measures the alignment of the company's forward price curve with market expectations, indicating the effectiveness of price risk management strategies.
Calculation: Difference between the company's forward price curve and market consensus price curve, averaged over a representative sample of products and time periods
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the company's ability to manage price risks and capitalize on market opportunities.
Financial Impact: Impacts revenue and profitability through effective price risk management and strategic decision-making.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and market analysts focus on the company's approach to price risk management and its impact on financial performance.

Description: Tracks the company's investment in regulatory lobbying and engagement activities to influence policy and regulatory outcomes.
Calculation: Total lobbying and engagement expenses
Relevance: Essential for understanding the company's efforts to shape regulatory environments and manage risks.
Financial Impact: Can impact future regulatory outcomes, operational costs, and revenue.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on transparent and effective engagement with regulatory bodies.

Metric Name: Safety and Health Regulatory Compliance Rate
Description: Measures the company's compliance rate with safety and health regulations, including OSHA standards.
Calculation: (Number of compliant safety and health regulations / Total number of applicable regulations) × 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's commitment to employee safety and health.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of accidents, injuries, and associated costs, while enhancing operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees prioritize a safe and healthy work environment.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Tracks the company's investment in community engagement and development programs, including those related to regulatory compliance and social license to operate.
Calculation: Total community engagement and development expenses
Relevance: Essential for understanding the company's efforts to build social capital and manage regulatory risks.
Financial Impact: Can impact future regulatory outcomes, operational costs, and revenue.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulators value transparent and effective community engagement.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Measures the company's response time to changes in regulatory requirements, including updates to policies, procedures, and practices.
Calculation: Average response time to regulatory changes (days)
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the company's agility and adaptability in responding to regulatory changes.
Financial Impact: Enhances operational efficiency, reduces risk of non-compliance, and supports long-term sustainability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value proactive and timely responses to regulatory changes.

Topic Category: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Disclosure Title: Management of the Legal & Regulatory Environment
Description: Evaluates the maturity and effectiveness of the company's compliance management system, including policies, procedures, and controls.
Calculation: Index score based on assessment of compliance management system components
Relevance: Essential for understanding the company's overall compliance risk profile and management effectiveness.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, risk management, and long-term sustainability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers prioritize effective compliance management systems.

Description: Tracks the rate of process safety events (PSEs), which are incidents that result in or have the potential to result in significant safety, health, or environmental impacts. This metric evaluates the effectiveness of process safety management.
Calculation: (Total number of PSEs / Total barrels processed) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Critical for assessing process safety performance and risk management in refining operations.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and potential liabilities for damages or injuries.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and industry peers focus on process safety performance.

Description: Measures the average time taken to respond to and contain cybersecurity incidents that could impact operational safety, data integrity, or business continuity. This metric evaluates the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk management.
Calculation: Average time (in hours) taken to respond to and contain cybersecurity incidents
Relevance: Essential for assessing cybersecurity risk management and incident response capabilities.
Financial Impact: Affects potential losses from cyber-attacks, data breaches, or operational disruptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers focus on cybersecurity risk management and incident response.

Description: Evaluates the maturity of risk management practices, including critical incident risk management, using a standardized framework (e.g., COSO, ISO 31000). This metric assesses the effectiveness of risk management processes.
Calculation: Based on a standardized risk management maturity assessment framework
Relevance: Important for evaluating the effectiveness of risk management practices and identifying areas for improvement.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, insurance premiums, and potential liabilities for damages or injuries.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and industry peers focus on risk management maturity.

Description: Measures the frequency of emergency response drills conducted to prepare personnel for critical incidents (e.g., fires, spills, explosions). This metric evaluates the effectiveness of emergency preparedness and response planning.
Calculation: Total number of emergency response drills conducted per year
Relevance: Essential for assessing emergency preparedness and response capabilities.
Financial Impact: Affects potential losses from operational disruptions, damages, or injuries.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and employees focus on emergency preparedness and response.

Description: Tracks the reliability of critical equipment (e.g., pumps, compressors, heat exchangers) in refining and marketing operations. This metric evaluates the effectiveness of asset integrity management.
Calculation: (Total uptime of critical equipment / Total possible uptime) x 100
Relevance: Important for assessing asset integrity management and operational reliability.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, maintenance expenses, and potential losses from equipment failures.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and industry peers focus on asset integrity management.

Description: Measures the rate of near-misses reported (i.e., incidents that did not result in significant harm but had the potential to do so). This metric evaluates the effectiveness of safety culture and incident reporting.
Calculation: (Total number of near-misses reported / Total barrels processed) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Essential for assessing safety culture and incident reporting practices.
Financial Impact: Affects potential losses from operational disruptions, damages, or injuries.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees focus on safety culture and incident reporting.

Description: Measures the percentage of critical business processes and assets covered by business continuity plans (BCPs) in the event of a critical incident. This metric evaluates the effectiveness of business continuity planning.
Calculation: (Total critical business processes and assets covered by BCPs / Total critical business processes and assets) x 100
Relevance: Important for assessing business continuity planning and resilience.
Financial Impact: Affects potential losses from operational disruptions and business interruptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers focus on business continuity planning and resilience.

Description: Rate of methane leaks from equipment and infrastructure, measured through regular monitoring and detection programs.
Calculation: (Methane leak volume / Total equipment and infrastructure volume) × 100
Relevance: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, and leak rates are critical for assessing emissions management and mitigation efforts.
Financial Impact: Reduced methane leaks can minimize emissions-related costs, regulatory penalties, and reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and investors focus on methane management as a key aspect of climate risk mitigation.

Description: Fuel consumption per service vessel, measuring operational efficiency and potential for emissions reduction.
Calculation: Total fuel consumption / Total service vessel hours
Relevance: Improving fuel efficiency can reduce emissions, lower operational costs, and enhance competitiveness.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on fuel costs, emissions-related expenses, and potential carbon pricing risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value fuel-efficient operations as a key aspect of sustainability and cost management.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources, such as wind or solar power.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: Transitioning to renewable energy sources can reduce dependence on fossil fuels, lower emissions, and mitigate climate risks.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability, reduced regulatory compliance costs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value renewable energy adoption as a key aspect of sustainability and climate leadership.

Description: Progress toward achieving GHG emissions reduction targets, measured against a baseline year.
Calculation: (Current emissions / Baseline emissions) × 100
Relevance: Tracking progress toward emissions reduction targets helps to assess the effectiveness of sustainability strategies and climate risk management.
Financial Impact: Achieving emissions reduction targets can minimize regulatory compliance costs, reduce carbon pricing risks, and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on progress toward emissions reduction targets as a key indicator of sustainability performance.

Description: Estimated potential costs associated with carbon pricing risks, including regulatory compliance and carbon taxes.
Calculation: Estimated carbon pricing costs / Total revenue
Relevance: Understanding carbon pricing risk exposure helps to assess potential financial impacts and inform strategic decision-making.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses, profitability, and competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on carbon pricing risk exposure as a key aspect of climate risk management and financial resilience.

Description: Rate of flaring per well, measuring operational efficiency and potential for emissions reduction.
Calculation: Total flared gas volume / Total wells
Relevance: Reducing flaring rates can minimize emissions, lower operational costs, and enhance sustainability performance.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses, emissions-related costs, and potential regulatory penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on flaring rates as a key indicator of sustainability performance and climate risk management.

Description: Cost of implementing emission abatement measures, such as carbon capture and storage or emissions reduction technologies.
Calculation: Total emission abatement costs / Total tons CO2e abated
Relevance: Understanding the cost-effectiveness of emission abatement measures helps to inform strategic decision-making and optimize sustainability investments.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses, capital expenditures, and potential returns on sustainability investments.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators focus on emission abatement costs as a key aspect of sustainability performance and climate risk management.

Description: This metric measures the volume of freshwater withdrawn per well, reflecting the company's operational efficiency and water stewardship in exploration and production activities.
Calculation: Total freshwater withdrawal (cubic meters) / Total number of wells
Relevance: This metric helps assess the company's ability to manage water resources effectively, minimizing environmental impact and reducing operational costs.
Financial Impact: Reduced water costs, lower risk of water scarcity-related disruptions, and potential cost savings from more efficient operations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and local communities focus on responsible water management practices in extractive industries.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of produced water (from oil & gas operations) treated to meet regulatory standards or reused, reflecting the company's wastewater management effectiveness.
Calculation: (Treated produced water volume / Total produced water volume) × 100
Relevance: This metric is essential for oil & gas services companies, as produced water management affects environmental impact, regulatory compliance, and operational costs.
Financial Impact: Reduced wastewater treatment costs, lower environmental liability, and potential revenue from water reuse or recycling.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors focus on effective wastewater management practices.

Description: This metric measures the number of water-related regulatory non-compliance incidents, reflecting the company's risk exposure and effectiveness in managing water-related regulatory requirements.
Calculation: Number of water-related regulatory non-compliance incidents reported during the period
Relevance: This metric helps assess the company's risk management and compliance practices, which are critical for maintaining social license to operate and avoiding costly fines or penalties.
Financial Impact: Potential fines, penalties, or remediation costs associated with regulatory non-compliance incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and local communities focus on the company's ability to manage regulatory risks and maintain compliance.

Description: This metric measures the volume of water conserved through efficiency measures (e.g., water-saving technologies, process optimizations), reflecting the company's proactive approach to water stewardship.
Calculation: Total water conserved through efficiency measures (cubic meters)
