Relevance: Supports ecosystem services, pollinator health, and long-term agricultural productivity, which can improve supply chain resilience.
Financial Impact: Can improve agricultural productivity, reduce costs associated with external inputs, and enhance ecosystem services.
Stakeholder Perspective: NGOs, investors, and customers value biodiversity conservation practices.

Description: Percentage reduction in ingredient waste generated during sourcing, processing, and transportation.
Calculation: ((Total ingredient waste in baseline year - Total ingredient waste in current year) / Total ingredient waste in baseline year) × 100
Relevance: Reflects efficiency in ingredient sourcing and supply chain management, which can reduce costs and environmental impacts.
Financial Impact: Can reduce waste disposal costs, improve supply chain efficiency, and mitigate environmental liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value waste reduction and efficient resource use.

Description: Volume of ingredients certified by recognized sustainability standards, such as Fairtrade, Organic, or Rainforest Alliance.
Calculation: Total certified sustainable ingredients (units or weight)
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to responsible sourcing and supply chain management, which can improve brand reputation and mitigate risks.
Financial Impact: Can command premium pricing for certified sustainable products, and may reduce costs associated with conventional sourcing practices.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value certified sustainable ingredients and responsible sourcing practices.

Metric Name: GHG Emissions Intensity from Fleet Operations
Unit: Grams of CO2e per vehicle kilometer (g CO2e/km)
Description: Quantifies the GHG emissions generated per unit of distance traveled by the fleet, providing insight into the carbon footprint of fleet operations.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions from fleet operations (in grams of CO2e) / Total vehicle kilometers traveled
Relevance: Critical for assessing and managing climate-related risks and opportunities in fleet operations.
Financial Impact: Affects regulatory compliance costs, carbon pricing impacts, and brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers increasingly value GHG emissions reductions.

Description: Measures the proportion of alternative fuels used in the fleet, reflecting progress toward reducing dependence on fossil fuels and lowering GHG emissions.
Calculation: (Alternative fuel consumption / Total fuel consumption) × 100
Relevance: Indicates commitment to sustainable fleet management and transition to low-carbon operations.
Financial Impact: Affects fuel costs, regulatory compliance, and potential access to low-carbon incentives.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value efforts to reduce carbon footprint.

Description: Measures the percentage of fleet vehicles in use versus idle or not in use, reflecting operational efficiency and asset management.
Calculation: (Total vehicle kilometers traveled / Total possible vehicle kilometers) × 100
Relevance: Essential for optimizing fleet operations, reducing waste, and improving asset utilization.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, vehicle maintenance expenses, and overall fleet management efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and stakeholders focus on operational efficiency and asset management.

Description: Measures the proportion of new vehicles acquired that meet specific fuel efficiency or low-emission standards, reflecting strategic efforts to modernize the fleet.
Calculation: (Number of fuel-efficient vehicles acquired / Total vehicles acquired) × 100
Relevance: Indicates commitment to sustainable fleet management and reducing GHG emissions from fleet operations.
Financial Impact: Affects vehicle acquisition costs, fuel savings, and potential access to low-carbon incentives.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value efforts to reduce carbon footprint.

Description: Evaluates driver behavior and performance, including factors such as fuel-efficient driving practices, to encourage sustainable fleet operations.
Calculation: Aggregate score based on driver performance metrics (e.g., fuel consumption, idling time, speeding events)
Relevance: Essential for optimizing fleet operations, reducing fuel consumption, and promoting sustainable driving practices.
Financial Impact: Affects fuel costs, vehicle maintenance expenses, and overall fleet management efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and stakeholders focus on operational efficiency and sustainable practices.

Description: Measures the proportion of electric or hybrid vehicles in the fleet, reflecting progress toward reducing dependence on fossil fuels and lowering GHG emissions.
Calculation: (Number of electric or hybrid vehicles / Total vehicles) × 100
Relevance: Indicates commitment to sustainable fleet management and transition to low-carbon operations.
Financial Impact: Affects vehicle acquisition costs, fuel savings, and potential access to low-carbon incentives.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value efforts to reduce carbon footprint.

Description: Tracks progress toward achieving specific GHG emissions reduction targets for fleet operations, reflecting commitment to climate action.
Calculation: (GHG emissions reduction achieved / GHG emissions reduction target) × 100
Relevance: Essential for assessing and managing climate-related risks and opportunities in fleet operations.
Financial Impact: Affects regulatory compliance costs, carbon pricing impacts, and brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers increasingly value GHG emissions reductions and climate action.

Description: This metric measures the rate of refrigerant leaks from refrigeration systems, indicating the effectiveness of leak detection and prevention measures.
Calculation: (Total refrigerant leaked / Total refrigerant charged) × 100
Relevance: This metric is crucial for minimizing refrigerant emissions, reducing environmental impact, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduced refrigerant replacement costs, lower energy consumption, and minimized regulatory compliance risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and regulatory bodies focus on refrigerant management and emissions reduction.

Description: This metric measures the proportion of energy-efficient refrigeration systems in use, indicating the company's commitment to reducing energy consumption and GHG emissions.
Calculation: (Number of energy-efficient refrigeration systems / Total refrigeration systems) × 100
Relevance: This metric supports strategic decision-making on capital expenditures, energy efficiency, and sustainability initiatives.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs, lower maintenance expenses, and potential incentives for sustainable investments.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that prioritize sustainability and energy efficiency.

Unit: Number of maintenance events per year
Description: This metric measures the frequency of refrigeration system maintenance, ensuring that systems operate efficiently and minimizing the risk of refrigerant leaks.
Calculation: Total number of maintenance events per year
Relevance: Regular maintenance is essential for preventing refrigerant leaks, reducing energy consumption, and extending equipment lifespan.
Financial Impact: Reduced maintenance costs, lower energy consumption, and minimized downtime.
Stakeholder Perspective: Operations teams and maintenance personnel focus on equipment reliability and performance.

Description: This metric measures the company's investments in carbon offset projects to mitigate refrigeration-related GHG emissions.
Calculation: Total tons CO2e offset through carbon purchases
Relevance: This metric demonstrates the company's commitment to reducing its carbon footprint and supporting climate change mitigation efforts.
Financial Impact: Cost of carbon offset purchases, potential cost savings through reduced emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies that take proactive steps to address climate change.

Description: This metric measures the company's refrigerant bank management practices, ensuring that refrigerant supplies are properly managed and leaks are minimized.
Calculation: (Refrigerant stored / Refrigerant used) ratio
Relevance: Effective refrigerant bank management reduces waste, minimizes leaks, and supports regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduced refrigerant replacement costs, lower waste disposal expenses.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies and environmental groups focus on responsible refrigerant management.

Description: This metric measures the frequency of refrigeration system upgrades, indicating the company's commitment to adopting energy-efficient technologies.
Calculation: Average age of refrigeration systems or upgrade cycle length (years)
Relevance: Regular upgrades support energy efficiency, reduce GHG emissions, and minimize the risk of equipment failure.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs, lower maintenance expenses, and potential incentives for sustainable investments.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that prioritize sustainability and energy efficiency.

Description: This metric provides a forward-looking estimate of refrigeration-related GHG emissions, enabling proactive decision-making and strategic planning.
Calculation: Projected GHG emissions from refrigeration systems (tons CO2e)
Relevance: This metric supports strategic decision-making on sustainability initiatives, capital expenditures, and energy efficiency projects.
Financial Impact: Informed decision-making on investments, cost savings, and potential regulatory compliance risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, executive management, and sustainability teams focus on forward-looking metrics that predict future performance.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources in distribution centers, demonstrating a commitment to clean energy transition.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100 in distribution centers
Relevance: This metric showcases a company's efforts to mitigate climate-related risks and capitalize on opportunities in renewable energy.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability and regulatory compliance benefits, enhancing financial resilience.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, sustainability-focused investors, and customers increasingly value companies' renewable energy commitments.

Description: Percentage of energy-efficient refrigeration systems adopted in retail stores and distribution centers, reflecting a company's efforts to reduce energy consumption.
Calculation: (Number of energy-efficient refrigeration systems / Total refrigeration systems) × 100
Relevance: This metric highlights a company's proactive approach to reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs and extended equipment lifespan, contributing to cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value companies' efforts to adopt energy-efficient technologies.

Description: Total energy consumed per unit of goods distributed, reflecting the efficiency of distribution operations.
Calculation: Total energy consumption (kWh) / Total units distributed
Relevance: This metric helps identify opportunities to optimize distribution operations, reduce energy consumption, and lower costs.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses and energy costs, influencing profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value efficient distribution operations, reflecting a company's ability to manage resources effectively.

Description: Percentage of retail stores and distribution centers covered by an energy management system (EMS), demonstrating a company's commitment to monitoring and optimizing energy usage.
Calculation: (Number of locations with EMS / Total locations) × 100
Relevance: This metric highlights a company's proactive approach to energy management and optimization.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs and improved operational efficiency, contributing to cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value companies' efforts to implement energy management systems.

Metric Name: GHG Intensity per Unit of Sales
Description: Total GHG emissions per unit of sales, reflecting a company's carbon footprint and climate-related risks.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions (kg CO2e) / Total units sold
Relevance: This metric helps companies manage climate-related risks and capitalize on opportunities in low-carbon products and services.
Financial Impact: Regulatory compliance costs, carbon pricing, and reputational risks associated with climate change.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies increasingly value companies' efforts to manage and disclose climate-related risks.

Description: Total energy savings achieved through energy efficiency projects, reflecting a company's proactive approach to reducing energy consumption.
Calculation: Total energy savings (kWh) from energy efficiency projects
Relevance: This metric highlights a company's commitment to reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs and improved operational efficiency, contributing to cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value companies' efforts to implement energy efficiency projects.

Description: Progress toward achieving a forward-looking energy reduction target, demonstrating a company's commitment to continuous improvement in energy management.
Calculation: (Current energy consumption / Target energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric showcases a company's proactive approach to energy management and commitment to achieving ambitious sustainability goals.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value companies' efforts to set and achieve ambitious sustainability targets.

Description: Measures the percentage of surplus food recovered and redistributed to customers, employees, or charitable organizations. This KPI evaluates the effectiveness of food recovery programs.
Calculation: (Recovered food volume / Total surplus food volume) × 100
Relevance: Critical for assessing social responsibility, community engagement, and waste reduction efforts.
Financial Impact: Potential revenue from reduced waste disposal costs, enhanced brand reputation, and tax benefits from charitable donations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and community groups value food retailers' efforts to reduce food waste and support local communities.

Description: Measures the percentage of organic waste generated during operations that is composted on-site or through third-party services. This KPI assesses waste management practices and environmental impact.
Calculation: (Composted organic waste volume / Total organic waste volume) × 100
Relevance: Important for evaluating operational efficiency, waste reduction, and environmental sustainability.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs, potential revenue from compost sales, and lower greenhouse gas emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers value efforts to minimize waste and promote sustainable practices.

Description: Measures the total food waste generated per store location. This KPI evaluates operational efficiency and waste management practices across the retail network.
Calculation: Total food waste generated / Total number of store locations
Relevance: Essential for assessing operational performance, identifying areas for improvement, and benchmarking against peers.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs, lower procurement costs for waste management, and improved operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and industry peers value insights into operational efficiency and waste management practices.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Food Waste Reduction Target
Description: Measures the company's target reduction in food waste throughout its supply chain, compared to a baseline year. This KPI assesses the effectiveness of supply chain management and sustainability initiatives.
Calculation: ((Baseline supply chain food waste - Target supply chain food waste) / Baseline supply chain food waste) × 100
Relevance: Critical for evaluating supply chain resilience, sustainability, and long-term viability.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced waste, improved supply chain efficiency, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and industry peers value efforts to address supply chain sustainability and food waste.

Description: Measures the total volume of surplus food donated to customers, employees, or charitable organizations. This KPI evaluates the company's social responsibility and community engagement efforts.
Calculation: Total volume of food donated
Relevance: Essential for assessing social impact, community engagement, and brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Potential tax benefits from charitable donations, enhanced brand reputation, and improved stakeholder relationships.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and community groups value food retailers' efforts to support local communities and reduce food waste.

Description: Measures the total cost savings achieved through waste reduction and management initiatives. This KPI evaluates the financial impact of sustainability efforts.
Calculation: Total cost savings from waste reduction and management initiatives
Relevance: Critical for assessing financial performance, operational efficiency, and sustainability ROI.
Financial Impact: Direct cost savings from reduced waste disposal, lower procurement costs for waste management, and potential revenue from waste reduction initiatives.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and executive management value insights into financial performance and sustainability ROI.

Description: Measures the accuracy of food waste forecasts compared to actual food waste generated. This KPI evaluates the effectiveness of inventory management and waste reduction strategies.
Calculation: (1 - (Absolute difference between forecasted and actual food waste) / Actual food waste) × 100
Relevance: Essential for assessing operational efficiency, inventory management, and waste reduction efforts.
Financial Impact: Improved inventory management, reduced waste disposal costs, and potential revenue from waste reduction initiatives.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and executive management value insights into operational efficiency, inventory management, and sustainability performance.

Metric Name: Cybersecurity Investment as a Percentage of IT Budget
Description: Tracks the proportion of IT budget allocated to cybersecurity initiatives, demonstrating commitment to data security and risk mitigation.
Calculation: (Cybersecurity investment / Total IT budget) × 100
Relevance: Indicates strategic prioritization of data security within IT spending.
Financial Impact: Influences long-term cost management, risk reduction, and investor confidence.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and boards focus on strategic allocation of resources to manage risks.

Description: Measures the proportion of sensitive customer data encrypted, reflecting data protection practices and security posture.
Calculation: (Encrypted data volume / Total sensitive data volume) × 100
Relevance: Critical for safeguarding customer data and meeting regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of data breaches, associated costs, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, regulators, and investors value robust data protection measures.

Description: Tracks the proportion of employees participating in data security training programs, indicating a culture of security awareness.
Calculation: (Employees trained / Total employees handling sensitive data) × 100
Relevance: Essential for mitigating insider threats and human error.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of security incidents caused by human error or lack of awareness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators emphasize the importance of a security-aware workforce.

Description: Measures the proportion of identified vulnerabilities remediated within a specified timeframe, reflecting responsiveness to security threats.
Calculation: (Remediated vulnerabilities / Total identified vulnerabilities) × 100
Relevance: Critical for maintaining robust cybersecurity posture and minimizing risk exposure.
Financial Impact: Reduces potential costs associated with breach incidents and regulatory penalties.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and cybersecurity experts prioritize proactive vulnerability management.

Description: Tracks the proportion of third-party vendors assessed for data security risks, highlighting due diligence in supply chain risk management.
Calculation: (Vendors assessed / Total vendors handling sensitive data) × 100
Relevance: Essential for mitigating risks associated with third-party data handling.
Financial Impact: Protects against potential breaches and associated costs through effective vendor risk management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value robust supply chain risk management practices.

Description: Measures the average time to respond to and contain data security incidents, reflecting operational effectiveness of incident response plans.
Calculation: Average time (in hours) to respond to and contain incidents
Relevance: Critical for minimizing impact and costs associated with data breaches.
Financial Impact: Reduces costs associated with prolonged incident response and potential regulatory fines.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators prioritize swift and effective incident response.

Description: Tracks the proportion of customer data lost or compromised due to security incidents, reflecting data security effectiveness.
Calculation: (Customer data lost / Total customer data) × 100
Relevance: Essential for assessing data security risk management and operational resilience.
Financial Impact: Directly affects costs associated with breach incidents, regulatory fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators prioritize data security and protection of sensitive information.

Description: Measures the proportion of employees and suppliers with food safety certifications, indicating the company's commitment to food safety culture and competence.
Calculation: (Number of employees and suppliers with food safety certifications / Total employees and suppliers) x 100
Relevance: A high level of certification coverage demonstrates a proactive approach to food safety and reduces the risk of non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Investing in food safety certifications can reduce the risk of costly incidents, improve operational efficiency, and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that prioritize food safety and demonstrate a strong commitment to employee and supplier competence.

Description: Measures the proportion of suppliers audited for food safety compliance, indicating the company's ability to manage supply chain risks.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers audited / Total suppliers) x 100
Relevance: Regular supplier audits help identify and mitigate food safety risks, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and company standards.
Financial Impact: Effective supplier audit programs can prevent costly incidents, reduce reputational risk, and ensure business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators expect companies to ensure their suppliers adhere to food safety standards.

Description: Measures the frequency of customer complaints related to food safety concerns, indicating product quality and safety performance.
Calculation: (Number of customer complaints / Total units sold) x 100,000
Relevance: High customer complaint rates can indicate inadequate food safety controls, product quality issues, or ineffective customer service.
Financial Impact: Customer complaints can lead to lost sales, damage brand reputation, and result in costly corrective actions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors closely monitor customer complaint rates as an indicator of food safety and product quality performance.

Description: Measures the frequency of food safety incidents, including contamination, spoilage, or other safety concerns, indicating the effectiveness of food safety controls.
Calculation: (Number of food safety incidents / Total units sold) x 100,000
Relevance: High incident rates can indicate inadequate food safety controls, ineffective risk management, and potential regulatory non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Food safety incidents can result in significant costs, including lost sales, recall-related expenses, and potential litigation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators closely monitor food safety incident rates as an indicator of food safety performance.

Description: Measures the proportion of preventive maintenance activities completed on schedule, indicating the effectiveness of equipment maintenance and food safety controls.
Calculation: (Number of preventive maintenance activities completed on schedule / Total preventive maintenance activities) x 100
Relevance: Regular preventive maintenance helps prevent equipment failures, reduces the risk of food safety incidents, and ensures compliance with regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Effective preventive maintenance programs can reduce equipment downtime, improve operational efficiency, and prevent costly incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that prioritize equipment maintenance and food safety controls.

Description: Measures the proportion of employees participating in food safety training and awareness programs, indicating the company's commitment to food safety culture and competence.
Calculation: (Number of employees participating in food safety training and awareness programs / Total employees) x 100
Relevance: A well-trained and aware workforce is essential for effective food safety management, incident prevention, and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Investing in food safety training and awareness programs can reduce the risk of costly incidents, improve operational efficiency, and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value companies that prioritize employee training and awareness programs.

Description: Measures the proportion of corrective actions implemented and verified as effective in addressing food safety incidents or concerns, indicating the company's ability to learn and improve.
Calculation: (Number of effective corrective actions / Total corrective actions) x 100
Relevance: Effective corrective actions help prevent repeat incidents, demonstrate a commitment to continuous improvement, and ensure regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Effective corrective actions can reduce the risk of costly incidents, improve operational efficiency, and enhance brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value companies that prioritize continuous improvement and effective corrective actions.

Description: Percentage of products reformulated to reduce unhealthy ingredients (e.g., sugar, sodium, saturated fats) within a specified timeframe
Calculation: (Number of reformulated products / Total products) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to improving product healthiness and reducing health risks
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces regulatory risks, and attracts health-conscious consumers
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value companies proactively improving product health

Description: Percentage of products compliant with front-of-pack labeling regulations (e.g., displaying nutritional information)
Calculation: (Number of compliant products / Total products) × 100
Relevance: Ensures transparency and compliance with regulatory requirements
Financial Impact: Reduces regulatory risks and potential fines
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, customers, and investors value transparency in product labeling

Description: Percentage of total products sourced from suppliers meeting specific health and sustainability standards
Calculation: (Value of products from healthy suppliers / Total product value) × 100
Relevance: Encourages sustainable and healthy sourcing practices throughout the supply chain
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces supply chain risks, and attracts sustainability-focused investors
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value companies promoting sustainable and healthy sourcing practices

Unit: Number of interactions (e.g., website visits, social media posts, customer inquiries)
Description: Measures customer engagement with product-related health and nutrition information
Calculation: Total number of interactions related to product health and nutrition
Relevance: Indicates customer interest in product health and nutrition, informing marketing and product strategies
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, drives sales, and informs product development
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and marketing teams value insights into customer engagement and preferences

Metric Name: Nutrition and Health Claims Substantiation Rate
Description: Percentage of nutrition and health claims substantiated by scientific evidence and regulatory approvals
Calculation: (Number of substantiated claims / Total claims) × 100
Relevance: Ensures compliance with regulatory requirements and maintains brand credibility
Financial Impact: Reduces regulatory risks, potential fines, and reputational damage
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, investors, and customers value companies substantiating health claims

Description: Composite score evaluating the healthiness of the product portfolio based on nutritional criteria (e.g., sugar, sodium, saturated fats)
Calculation: Weighted average of nutritional criteria scores
Relevance: Provides a comprehensive view of product portfolio healthiness, informing strategic decisions
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces regulatory risks, and attracts health-conscious consumers
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and health organizations value companies with healthy product portfolios

Metric Name: Supply Chain Nutrition and Health Training
Unit: Number of training sessions or participants
Description: Measures the extent of nutrition and health training provided to supply chain partners and employees
Calculation: Total number of training sessions or participants
Relevance: Enhances supply chain partners' and employees' understanding of product health and nutrition, promoting best practices
Financial Impact: Reduces regulatory risks, improves supply chain efficiency, and enhances brand reputation
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value companies investing in supply chain nutrition and health training

Description: Measures the level of transparency in product labeling, including clear information on ingredients, allergens, and nutritional content.
Calculation: Weighted average of scores for ingredient transparency, allergen labeling, and nutritional information clarity.
Relevance: Supports customer choice and trust, driving sales and loyalty.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation and premium pricing opportunities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors prioritize transparency for informed choices.

Description: Percentage of marketing claims validated through third-party audits or certifications.
Calculation: (Number of validated marketing claims / Total number of marketing claims) × 100
Relevance: Ensures compliance with advertising regulations and maintains customer trust.
Financial Impact: Avoids costly fines, reputational damage, and lost sales.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value validated marketing claims.

Unit: Number of users / Percentage of website visitors
Description: Measures the adoption and usage of online product comparison tools, enabling customers to make informed choices.
Calculation: Number of users or percentage of website visitors using the tool.
Relevance: Enhances customer engagement, satisfaction, and loyalty.
Financial Impact: Drives sales, customer retention, and positive word-of-mouth.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers value easy access to product information for informed decisions.

Description: Percentage of products with standardized labeling across regions and channels.
Calculation: (Number of products with standardized labeling / Total number of products) × 100
Relevance: Simplifies operations, reduces costs, and enhances brand consistency.
Financial Impact: Achieves economies of scale, reduces labeling errors, and improves efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value consistent branding and labeling.

Description: Percentage of customer feedback responded to and addressed within a set timeframe.
Calculation: (Number of customer feedback responses / Total number of customer feedback) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to customer satisfaction and trust.
Financial Impact: Enhances customer loyalty, retention, and positive word-of-mouth.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers value responsive and attentive customer service.

Description: Percentage of employees completing regulatory compliance training on product labeling and marketing.
Calculation: (Number of employees completing training / Total number of employees) × 100
Relevance: Ensures employees understand regulatory requirements and maintain compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of non-compliance, fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and customers value a well-trained workforce.

Unit: Number of errors / Percentage of products
Description: Measures the frequency and rate of product labeling errors, including incorrect or missing information.
Calculation: Number of labeling errors / Total number of products.
Relevance: Identifies areas for improvement in labeling processes and reduces risk of non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Avoids costly recalls, fines, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value accurate labeling for informed decision-making.

Description: Tracks the average number of training hours provided to employees, which can enhance their skills, productivity, and job satisfaction. This metric is particularly relevant for frontline workers in food retail and distribution.
Calculation: Total training hours provided to employees / Total number of employees
Relevance: Adequate training is essential for ensuring employee competence, customer satisfaction, and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Well-trained employees can lead to improved productivity, reduced errors, and enhanced customer satisfaction, ultimately driving revenue growth.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulatory bodies value comprehensive training programs as a sign of investment in human capital.

Description: Measures the rate of occupational injuries, which can impact employee well-being, productivity, and labor costs. This metric is critical for identifying workplace safety issues.
Calculation: (Number of occupational injuries / Total number of full-time equivalent employees) × 100
Relevance: A safe working environment is essential for employee well-being and operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Occupational injuries can lead to increased medical costs, workers' compensation claims, and lost productivity, negatively impacting profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulatory bodies prioritize workplace safety as a fundamental aspect of responsible business practices.

Description: Tracks the representation of underrepresented groups (e.g., women, minorities) in the workforce, which can foster innovation, employee engagement, and better decision-making.
Calculation: (Number of employees from underrepresented groups / Total number of employees) × 100
Relevance: A diverse and inclusive workforce can drive business performance, innovation, and reputation.
Financial Impact: Diverse teams can lead to improved decision-making, innovation, and employee engagement, ultimately driving revenue growth and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and employees value diversity and inclusion as essential for long-term success.

Description: Measures the rate of compliance with labor laws and regulations, such as minimum wage, overtime, and working hours. Non-compliance can result in fines, reputational damage, and operational disruptions.
Calculation: (Number of compliant labor practices / Total number of labor practices assessed) × 100
Relevance: Labour compliance is essential for avoiding regulatory risks, fines, and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can lead to significant fines, penalties, and reputational damage, negatively impacting profitability and business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and customers prioritize labour compliance as a fundamental aspect of responsible business practices.

Description: Tracks employee engagement through surveys or other assessments, which can impact productivity, employee retention, and customer satisfaction.
Calculation: Average score from employee engagement surveys
Relevance: High employee engagement is crucial for driving productivity, innovation, and customer satisfaction.
Financial Impact: Engaged employees can lead to improved productivity, reduced turnover, and enhanced customer satisfaction, ultimately driving revenue growth and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, employees, and customers value high employee engagement as a sign of a positive work culture.

Description: Evaluates the labour practices of suppliers and third-party vendors, which can impact the company's reputation, regulatory compliance, and operational continuity.
Calculation: Risk assessment score based on supplier audits, surveys, or other assessments
Relevance: Labour risks in the supply chain can have significant reputational, regulatory, and operational implications.
Financial Impact: Labour risks in the supply chain can lead to reputational damage, regulatory fines, and operational disruptions, negatively impacting profitability and business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies prioritize supply chain labour risk management as essential for responsible business practices.

Description: Tracks the percentage of employees earning a living wage, which can impact employee well-being, productivity, and retention. This metric is particularly relevant for food retail and distribution workers.
Calculation: (Number of employees earning a living wage / Total number of employees) × 100
Relevance: Paying a living wage is essential for ensuring employee well-being, productivity, and retention.
Financial Impact: Paying a living wage can lead to improved productivity, reduced turnover, and enhanced employee well-being, ultimately driving revenue growth and profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and customers value fair compensation practices as a sign of responsible business practices.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage of agricultural products sourced from suppliers adopting sustainable practices, such as organic farming, integrated pest management, or regenerative agriculture. This metric assesses the company's progress in promoting environmentally friendly agricultural practices.
Calculation: (Volume of products sourced from sustainable agriculture / Total volume of agricultural products) × 100
Relevance: Supports environmental sustainability, reduces reputational risk, and meets customer demand for sustainably sourced products.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term cost savings through improved soil health, reduced chemical usage, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups prioritize sustainable agriculture practices.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Unit: Water stress index score (e.g., WRI's Water Stress Index)
Description: Assessment of water risk exposure in the supply chain, including watersheds with high water stress. This metric helps identify potential water-related risks and opportunities for mitigation.
Calculation: Average water stress index score of suppliers' locations
Relevance: Critical for managing water-related risks, ensuring business continuity, and meeting stakeholder expectations.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings through water conservation, reduced regulatory risks, and enhanced supply chain resilience.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs focus on water stewardship and risk management.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Unit: Liters per kilometer (or miles per gallon)
Description: Average fuel efficiency of transportation fleet, including trucks, vans, and other vehicles used for product distribution. This metric evaluates the company's efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and transportation costs.
Calculation: Total fuel consumption / Total distance traveled
Relevance: Supports reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, improves operational efficiency, and reduces fuel costs.
Financial Impact: Direct cost savings through reduced fuel consumption, lower emissions-related regulatory risks, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups prioritize sustainable transportation practices.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage reduction in food waste generated during distribution, storage, and retail operations. This metric assesses the company's efforts to minimize waste and optimize food supply chains.
Calculation: ((Initial food waste - Current food waste) / Initial food waste) × 100
Relevance: Supports reduction of waste, conserves resources, and meets stakeholder expectations for sustainable food systems.
Financial Impact: Cost savings through reduced waste disposal, improved operational efficiency, and potential revenue gains from recovered food.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs focus on waste reduction and sustainable food systems.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage of suppliers complying with labor standards, including fair wages, safe working conditions, and freedom of association. This metric evaluates the company's commitment to responsible labor practices in the supply chain.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers compliant with labor standards / Total number of suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to fair labor practices, reduces reputational risk, and ensures compliance with regulations.
Financial Impact: Reduced reputational risk, improved supplier performance, and potential cost savings through early identification of issues.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs prioritize responsible labor practices.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Assessment of supply chain resilience, including factors such as supplier diversity, geographic dispersion, and business continuity planning. This metric helps evaluate the company's ability to manage supply chain disruptions.
Calculation: Composite index score based on multiple factors (e.g., supplier diversity, lead time, inventory levels)
Relevance: Critical for managing supply chain disruptions, ensuring business continuity, and meeting stakeholder expectations.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings through reduced supply chain disruptions, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs focus on supply chain resilience and risk management.

Disclosure Title: Management of Environmental & Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Description: Percentage of packaging materials that meet sustainability standards, such as recyclability, biodegradability, or reduced material usage. This metric assesses the company's efforts to reduce packaging waste and promote sustainable packaging practices.
Calculation: (Volume of sustainable packaging materials / Total volume of packaging materials) × 100
Relevance: Supports reduction of packaging waste, conserves resources, and meets stakeholder expectations for sustainable packaging practices.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings through reduced material usage, improved brand reputation, and compliance with regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs prioritize sustainable packaging practices.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources in processing facilities, reflecting efforts to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to clean energy transition, risk mitigation, and long-term cost stability.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, supports regulatory compliance, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value sustainability commitments and efforts to mitigate climate-related risks.

Description: Efficiency of feed conversion into animal weight gain, influencing both operational costs and GHG emissions from feed production.
Calculation: Total feed consumption (kg) / Total animal weight gain (kg)
Relevance: Critical for optimizing feed strategies, reducing waste, and lowering emissions associated with feed production.
Financial Impact: Affects feed costs, animal health, and overall operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Important for investors, regulators, and sustainability-focused stakeholders

Description: Percentage of manure managed through efficient practices (e.g., anaerobic digestion, composting), reducing methane emissions and environmental impact.
Calculation: (Manure managed efficiently / Total manure produced) × 100
Relevance: Essential for mitigating methane emissions, a potent GHG, from manure and enhancing environmental sustainability.
Financial Impact: Reduces environmental liabilities, supports regulatory compliance, and can generate revenue through by-products (e.g., biogas, fertilizer).
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and sustainability-focused investors emphasize efficient manure management as a critical sustainability practice.

Description: GHG emissions intensity of the supply chain, reflecting the sector's significant upstream emissions, particularly from feed and livestock production.
Calculation: Total supply chain GHG emissions (kg CO2e) / Total supply chain spend ($)
Relevance: Critical for understanding and managing the sector's largest emission source, supporting strategic decisions on supplier engagement and sourcing practices.
Financial Impact: Affects long-term supply chain resilience, costs, and the ability to meet sustainability commitments.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers increasingly focus on supply chain sustainability and transparency.

Description: Total GHG emissions offset through verified carbon offset projects, supporting efforts to achieve net-zero emissions.
Calculation: Total tons CO2e offset through verified projects
Relevance: Demonstrates proactive approach to managing and reducing GHG emissions beyond operational improvements.
Financial Impact: Supports regulatory compliance, enhances brand reputation, and can provide cost savings through avoided emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value proactive efforts to mitigate climate-related risks and achieve sustainability goals.

Description: Projected future GHG emissions based on planned operational changes, new technologies, and sustainability initiatives.
Calculation: Modeled forecast of future GHG emissions
Relevance: Essential for strategic planning, setting science-based targets, and ensuring long-term business viability in a low-carbon economy.
Financial Impact: Informs capital allocation decisions, supports regulatory compliance, and enhances resilience to climate-related risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and stakeholders focus on forward-looking metrics that predict future performance and sustainability.

Description: Assessment of the company's resilience to climate-related risks and opportunities, reflecting its ability to adapt and thrive in a changing climate.
Calculation: Composite index based on multiple factors, including climate risk assessment, business strategy alignment, and operational adaptability
Relevance: Critical for understanding and managing climate-related risks and opportunities, supporting strategic decisions on investments, operations, and product offerings.
Financial Impact: Affects long-term business viability, cost structure, and revenue streams in a climate-constrained economy.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers increasingly value companies' ability to manage climate-related risks and capitalize on opportunities.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources, such as biogas, solar, or wind power, in meat, poultry, and dairy operations.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and reliance on fossil fuels.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability and regulatory compliance benefits from reduced energy costs and potential carbon pricing.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, sustainability-focused investors, and customers value companies' efforts to transition to renewable energy.

Description: Energy consumption per tonne of product stored in refrigeration systems, which is critical for preserving meat, poultry, and dairy products.
Calculation: Total energy consumption of refrigeration systems (kWh) / Total tonnes of product stored
Relevance: This metric helps companies optimize refrigeration system efficiency and reduce energy costs.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses and energy costs, which can affect profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers focus on operational efficiency and sustainability in food storage and preservation.

Unit: Liters/100 km or miles per gallon
Description: Fuel consumption per unit of distance traveled by company-owned vehicle fleets used for transportation and distribution of meat, poultry, and dairy products.
Calculation: Total fuel consumption (liters) / Total distance traveled (km) × 100
Relevance: This metric helps companies reduce fuel consumption, lower emissions, and optimize logistics operations.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on fuel costs, operational expenses, and potential carbon pricing.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies focus on fuel efficiency and emissions reduction in logistics and transportation.

Description: Percentage of energy-efficient equipment, such as LED lighting, high-efficiency motors, and HVAC systems, adopted in meat, poultry, and dairy operations.
Calculation: (Number of energy-efficient equipment / Total equipment) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions through equipment upgrades.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost savings from reduced energy consumption and potential rebates or incentives for energy-efficient equipment.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies' efforts to adopt energy-efficient technologies.

Description: Percentage of company operations covered by an energy management system (EMS) that monitors, reports, and optimizes energy consumption.
Calculation: (Operations covered by EMS / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to systematic energy management and data-driven decision-making.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from optimized energy consumption and reduced energy waste.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies' efforts to implement robust energy management systems.

Metric Name: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions from Energy Use
Description: Total GHG emissions from energy use, including Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, in meat, poultry, and dairy operations.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions from energy use (tonnes CO2e)
Relevance: This metric helps companies measure and manage their carbon footprint from energy use.
Financial Impact: Potential carbon pricing, regulatory compliance costs, and reputational risks associated with GHG emissions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies focus on companies' GHG emissions and efforts to reduce their carbon footprint.

Metric Name: Energy Cost Savings from Efficiency Projects
Description: Total energy cost savings achieved through energy efficiency projects, such as equipment upgrades, process optimization, and behavioral changes.
Calculation: Total energy cost savings (currency)
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's ability to reduce energy costs and improve operational efficiency through targeted projects.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses and energy costs, which can affect profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies' efforts to reduce energy costs and improve sustainability performance.

Metric Name: Water Recycling Rate in Processing Plants
Description: Percentage of water recycled or reused in processing plants, including wastewater treatment and reuse.
Calculation: (Recycled water volume / Total water consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to water conservation and circular economy practices.
Financial Impact: Reduced water procurement costs, lower wastewater treatment expenses, and potential cost savings from reduced regulatory compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, sustainability-focused investors, and regulatory bodies value water recycling and reuse efforts.

Description: A composite index assessing the company's water management practices and their impact on local watersheds, including metrics such as water quality, aquatic biodiversity, and community engagement.
Calculation: Aggregate scoring of multiple indicators, including water quality monitoring data, biodiversity assessments, and stakeholder engagement metrics.
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's impact on local ecosystems and communities, supporting strategic decision-making and stakeholder engagement.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term costs associated with watershed degradation, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and local communities value watershed stewardship and responsible water management practices.

Description: Water consumption associated with feed production, including crop irrigation and feed processing.
Calculation: Total water consumption (liters) / Total kilograms of feed produced
Relevance: This metric assesses the water impact of feed production, enabling companies to engage with suppliers and optimize feed sourcing strategies.
Financial Impact: Potential costs associated with water scarcity, feed price volatility, and supply chain disruptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers increasingly value transparency and accountability in supply chain management.

Description: Percentage of water-related regulatory requirements met, including permits, monitoring, and reporting.
Calculation: (Number of compliant permits / Total permits) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's compliance with water-related regulations, minimizing risks associated with non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Potential costs associated with fines, penalties, and reputational damage from non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, investors, and customers value compliance with environmental regulations.

Description: A composite index assessing the company's preparedness and resilience to drought conditions, including metrics such as water storage capacity, water efficiency measures, and business continuity planning.
Calculation: Aggregate scoring of multiple indicators, including water storage capacity, drought contingency planning, and business continuity metrics.
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's ability to manage drought-related risks, supporting strategic decision-making and stakeholder engagement.
Financial Impact: Potential costs associated with drought-related disruptions, supply chain risks, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value drought resilience and business continuity planning.

Description: Capital expenditures invested in water management initiatives, including water efficiency projects, wastewater treatment upgrades, and water recycling infrastructure.
Calculation: Total CAPEX invested in water management initiatives
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's commitment to water management and sustainability, supporting long-term strategic decision-making.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and reduced regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value proactive investments in water management and sustainability.

Metric Name: Water Use Reduction Target Achievement Rate
Description: Percentage of water use reduction targets achieved, including targets set for specific facilities, operations, or business units.
Calculation: (Actual water reduction / Target water reduction) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's progress toward water use reduction goals, supporting strategic decision-making and stakeholder engagement.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced water consumption, lower wastewater treatment expenses, and improved operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value progress toward sustainability targets and water use reduction goals.

Unit: kg of feed per kg of live weight gain
Description: This metric measures the efficiency of feed conversion into live weight gain for livestock, indicating the sector's resource use and potential environmental impacts.
Calculation: Total feed consumption (kg) / Total live weight gain (kg)
Relevance: FCR is a key performance indicator for animal agriculture, influencing feed costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and land use.
Financial Impact: Improving FCR reduces feed costs, mitigates environmental impacts, and enhances competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators focus on efficient resource use and minimizing environmental footprint.

Metric Name: Water Usage per Kilogram of Production
Description: This metric measures the total water consumption required for production, normalized by production volume. It helps assess the sector's water efficiency and potential impacts on local water resources.
Calculation: Total water consumption (liters) / Total production volume (kg)
Relevance: Water usage is critical in the Meat, Poultry & Dairy sector, influencing operational costs, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder perceptions.
Financial Impact: Water efficiency affects operational costs, water management expenses, and reputation among stakeholders.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs focus on water stewardship and efficient resource use.

Description: This metric assesses the company's manure management practices, measuring the balance between nutrient application and crop requirements. It helps mitigate water pollution risks and optimize fertilizer use.
Calculation: (Manure nutrient application / Crop nutrient requirements) × 100
Relevance: Manure management is crucial for minimizing water pollution, maintaining soil health, and reducing environmental impacts.
Financial Impact: Effective manure management reduces fertilizer costs, mitigates environmental liabilities, and enhances regulatory compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, NGOs, and customers focus on responsible manure management practices.

Description: This metric measures the total area of land conserved or restored for biodiversity purposes, indicating the company's commitment to ecological preservation.
Calculation: Total area of conserved or restored land (hectares)
Relevance: Biodiversity conservation is essential for maintaining ecosystem services, ensuring long-term resource availability, and enhancing reputation.
Financial Impact: Biodiversity conservation affects operational costs, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder perceptions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers value companies' efforts to conserve biodiversity and promote ecological sustainability.

Metric Name: Deforestation and Land Degradation Risk Exposure
Description: This metric assesses the company's exposure to deforestation and land degradation risks in its supply chain or operations, measured as a percentage of total sourcing or operational footprint.
Calculation: (Exposed area / Total sourcing or operational footprint) × 100
Relevance: Deforestation and land degradation pose significant ecological and reputational risks to the sector.
Financial Impact: Managing deforestation and land degradation risks mitigates operational disruptions, regulatory penalties, and reputation damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers focus on companies' efforts to address deforestation and land degradation risks.

Description: This metric measures the proportion of the company's supply chain or operational area adopting regenerative agriculture practices, promoting soil health, biodiversity, and ecosystem services.
Calculation: (Regenerative agriculture area / Total supply chain or operational area) × 100
Relevance: Regenerative agriculture enhances ecological sustainability, improves soil health, and supports long-term resource availability.
Financial Impact: Regenerative agriculture adoption can reduce input costs, improve yields, and enhance reputation among stakeholders.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers value companies' efforts to promote regenerative agriculture and ecological sustainability.

Description: This metric estimates the monetary value of ecosystem services provided by the company's conservation efforts, such as carbon sequestration, pollination, or water filtration.
Calculation: Estimated monetary value of ecosystem services (e.g., using valuation methodologies like InVEST or TEV)
Relevance: Ecosystem services valuation helps companies understand the economic benefits of ecological conservation and restoration.
Financial Impact: Ecosystem services valuation informs strategic decision-making, risk management, and investment in conservation efforts.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, NGOs, and customers increasingly value companies' efforts to quantify and manage ecosystem services.

Description: Tracks the percentage of preventive controls implemented across the production process to mitigate food safety risks.
Calculation: (Number of preventive controls implemented / Total preventive controls required) x 100
Relevance: Demonstrates proactive approach to risk management and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduces likelihood of costly non-compliance events and associated financial impacts.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value proactive risk management practices.

Description: Measures the percentage of products tested for contaminants and pathogens as part of the company's quality control process.
Calculation: (Number of products tested / Total products produced) x 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring product safety and detecting potential contamination issues early.
Financial Impact: Helps prevent costly recalls and maintains customer trust, supporting revenue and market share.
Stakeholder Perspective: Important for investors, regulators, and sustainability-focused stakeholders

Description: Tracks the percentage of suppliers and third-party vendors assessed for food safety risks.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers assessed / Total suppliers) x 100
Relevance: Critical for managing food safety risks across the supply chain.
Financial Impact: Mitigates risk of supply chain disruptions and associated costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers prioritize supply chain transparency and risk management.

Metric Name: Training and Development Hours per Employee
Description: Measures the investment in employee training and development related to food safety procedures and protocols.
Calculation: Total training hours / Total number of employees
Relevance: Essential for ensuring employees are equipped to maintain high food safety standards.
Financial Impact: Enhances operational efficiency, reduces risk of non-compliance events.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value commitment to employee development and food safety.

Description: Tracks customer complaints related to food safety or product quality.
Calculation: (Number of customer complaints / Total products sold) x 1,000
Relevance: Provides insight into product safety and quality issues.
Financial Impact: Directly impacts customer satisfaction, loyalty, and ultimately, revenue.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors prioritize product safety and quality.

Description: Measures the time taken to respond to and manage a product recall.
Calculation: Time elapsed from recall initiation to completion
Relevance: Critical for minimizing financial and reputational impacts of recalls.
Financial Impact: Reduces costs associated with prolonged recalls and maintains customer trust.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value swift and effective recall management.

Description: Tracks the percentage of facilities and products certified to recognized food safety standards (e.g., HACCP, ISO 22000).
Calculation: (Number of certified facilities/products / Total facilities/products) x 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to food safety best practices and regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, supports market access, and reduces regulatory risk.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers prioritize food safety certifications.

Description: Measures the proportion of animal production that does not involve antibiotic use.
Calculation: (Antibiotic-free animal production / Total animal production) × 100
Relevance: Indicates progress toward reducing antibiotic use and promoting sustainable animal production practices.
Financial Impact: Potential premium pricing for antibiotic-free products, improved brand reputation, and reduced regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainable and responsible animal production practices.

Description: Measures the rate of veterinary antibiotic prescriptions, indicating responsible antibiotic use.
Calculation: Total veterinary antibiotic prescriptions / Total number of animal units
Relevance: Helps monitor and manage antibiotic prescriptions, reducing the risk of antibiotic resistance.
Financial Impact: Reduced antibiotic costs, lower risk of regulatory non-compliance, and improved animal health.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators focus on responsible antibiotic use and animal welfare.

Description: Measures animal health and wellness through metrics such as mortality rates, disease incidence, and lameness rates.
Calculation: Aggregate index score based on multiple animal health and wellness metrics
Relevance: Indicates the overall health and well-being of animals, reflecting responsible animal production practices.
Financial Impact: Improved animal health, reduced mortality rates, and lower veterinary costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and animal welfare organizations value animal health and well-being.

Description: Measures the rate of antibiotic resistance monitoring, indicating proactive risk management.
Calculation: Total antibiotic resistance monitoring samples / Total number of animal units
Relevance: Helps identify and manage antibiotic resistance risks, ensuring responsible antibiotic use.
Financial Impact: Reduced risk of antibiotic resistance, lower regulatory compliance costs, and improved brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and public health organizations focus on proactive risk management and responsible antibiotic use.

Description: Measures the proportion of animal production covered by sustainable animal production policies, including antibiotic use guidelines.
Calculation: (Animal production covered by sustainable policies / Total animal production) × 100
Relevance: Indicates commitment to sustainable animal production practices, including responsible antibiotic use.
Financial Impact: Improved brand reputation, potential premium pricing for sustainably produced products, and reduced regulatory risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value sustainable and responsible animal production practices.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Antibiotic Use Transparency Rate
Description: Measures the proportion of suppliers providing transparent information on antibiotic use in their operations.
Calculation: (Suppliers providing transparent antibiotic use data / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Ensures transparency and accountability throughout the supply chain, promoting responsible antibiotic use.
Financial Impact: Improved supply chain risk management, reduced reputational risks, and potential cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value transparency and accountability in supply chain practices.

Description: Measures progress toward reducing antibiotic use, relative to a baseline or target.
Calculation: ((Baseline antibiotic use - Current antibiotic use) / Baseline antibiotic use) × 100
Relevance: Indicates commitment to reducing antibiotic use and promoting sustainable animal production practices.
Financial Impact: Reduced antibiotic costs, lower regulatory compliance costs, and improved brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators value proactive efforts to reduce antibiotic use and promote sustainability.

Description: Tracks the frequency of work-related injuries that result in lost workdays, highlighting the impact on operational efficiency and employee well-being.
Calculation: (Number of lost time injuries / Total hours worked) x 1,000,000
Relevance: Indicates the effectiveness of safety protocols and employee training programs.
Financial Impact: Affects productivity, workers' compensation costs, and employee retention.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees prioritize a safe working environment.

Description: Measures the percentage of employees participating in wellness programs, reflecting the company's commitment to employee health and well-being.
Calculation: (Number of employees participating in wellness programs / Total employees) x 100
Relevance: Demonstrates the company's investment in employee health and well-being.
Financial Impact: Can lead to reduced healthcare costs, improved productivity, and employee retention.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees and investors value a healthy and engaged workforce.

Metric Name: Recordable Incident Rate for Sector-Specific Hazards
Description: Tracks recordable incidents related to sector-specific hazards, such as meat processing equipment or poultry handling.
Calculation: (Number of recordable incidents related to sector-specific hazards / Total FTE employees) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the effectiveness of sector-specific safety protocols.
Financial Impact: Directly affects workers' compensation costs, productivity, and employee retention.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees prioritize a safe working environment.

Description: Measures the average number of training hours provided to employees on health and safety procedures, reflecting the company's commitment to employee development and safety.
Calculation: Total training hours on health and safety procedures / Total employees
Relevance: Indicates the company's investment in employee safety and health education.
Financial Impact: Can lead to reduced accidents, improved productivity, and employee retention.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a well-trained and safe workforce.

Description: Tracks employee perceptions of workplace safety through regular surveys, providing insights into the effectiveness of safety protocols and employee engagement.
Calculation: (Number of employees rating workplace safety as "good" or "excellent" / Total employees surveyed) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating employee engagement and perceptions of workplace safety.
Financial Impact: Can lead to improved productivity, employee retention, and reduced turnover.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees and investors value a safe and healthy work environment.

Description: Measures the company's compliance rate with regulatory requirements related to workplace health and safety, reflecting its commitment to regulatory adherence.
Calculation: (Number of compliant facilities / Total facilities) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating regulatory compliance and risk management.
Financial Impact: Directly affects regulatory compliance costs, fines, and reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers prioritize regulatory compliance.

Description: Tracks the percentage of employees who return to work after an injury or illness, reflecting the effectiveness of return-to-work programs and employee support.
Calculation: (Number of employees returned to work / Total employees with injuries or illnesses) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the effectiveness of employee support programs and return-to-work initiatives.
Financial Impact: Can lead to reduced workers' compensation costs, improved productivity, and employee retention.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, employees, and regulators value a supportive work environment.

Unit: Grams of antibiotics used per kilogram of animal produced
Description: Measures the reduction in antibiotic usage in animal feed and care, promoting responsible antibiotic use and reducing antimicrobial resistance risks.
Calculation: Total grams of antibiotics used / Total kilograms of animal produced
Relevance: Addresses growing concerns around antimicrobial resistance and regulatory pressures to reduce antibiotic usage.
Financial Impact: Reduces costs associated with antibiotic usage, mitigates regulatory risks, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies focus on responsible antibiotic use and animal welfare.

Description: Measures the average space and density provided to animals, ensuring adequate living conditions and reducing stress.
Calculation: Total available space (square meters) / Total number of animals
Relevance: Ensures animal welfare and comfort, reducing stress and disease risks.
Financial Impact: Improves animal productivity, reduces mortality rates, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Animal welfare organizations, customers, and investors prioritize animal living conditions.

Unit: Percentage of humane handling and slaughter practices
Description: Measures the effectiveness of humane handling and slaughter practices, ensuring animal welfare during processing.
Calculation: (Number of animals humanely handled and slaughtered / Total number of animals processed) × 100
Relevance: Ensures animal welfare during processing, reducing risk of animal suffering and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces regulatory and reputational risks, and improves operational efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and animal welfare organizations prioritize humane handling and slaughter practices.

Description: Measures the quality of feed and water provided to animals, ensuring nutritional and hygienic standards.
Calculation: Weighted average of feed and water quality assessments (e.g., nutrient content, contaminant levels)
Relevance: Ensures animal health and welfare, reducing risk of disease and productivity losses.
Financial Impact: Improves animal productivity, reduces veterinary costs, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies prioritize feed and water quality.

Metric Name: Animal Care Training and Certification Rate
Unit: Percentage of animal care staff trained and certified
Description: Measures the percentage of animal care staff trained and certified in animal welfare and handling practices.
Calculation: (Number of trained and certified staff / Total animal care staff) × 100
Relevance: Ensures animal care staff are equipped to provide high-quality care and handling practices.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of animal welfare incidents, improves operational efficiency, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies value staff training and certification.

Description: Measures the reduction in animal mortality rates, indicating improved animal welfare and care practices.
Calculation: ((Previous period mortality rate - Current period mortality rate) / Previous period mortality rate) × 100
Relevance: Indicates effectiveness of animal care and welfare practices, reducing losses and improving productivity.
Financial Impact: Reduces losses due to animal mortality, improves operational efficiency, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies prioritize animal welfare and mortality rates.

Unit: Percentage of suppliers meeting animal welfare standards
Description: Measures the percentage of suppliers meeting animal welfare standards, ensuring responsible sourcing practices.
Calculation: (Number of suppliers meeting standards / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Ensures responsible sourcing practices, reducing reputational and regulatory risks.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, reduces regulatory and reputational risks, and improves supply chain resilience.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies prioritize responsible sourcing and animal welfare practices.
