Description: Tracks the company's public engagement activities on GMO-related issues, reflecting its commitment to transparency, stakeholder dialogue, and social responsibility.

Description: Measures the percentage of processes and equipment covered by formal PSM programs, reflecting the company's commitment to operational safety.

Description: Measures the number of near-misses reported per million hours worked, reflecting the effectiveness of safety reporting and learning culture.

Relevance: Important for identifying potential safety risks and evaluating the effectiveness of safety reporting and learning culture.

Description: Measures the percentage of critical business processes and functions covered by formal BCPs, reflecting the company's preparedness for disruptions.

Relevance: Essential for evaluating the company's preparedness for disruptions and ability to maintain business continuity.

Description: Measures the percentage of operations and processes subject to regular risk assessments, reflecting the company's commitment to proactive risk management.
Calculation: (Number of operations and processes subject to regular risk assessments / Total number of operations and processes) x 100
Relevance: Important for evaluating the comprehensiveness of risk management practices.
Financial Impact: Directly affects costs associated with incident prevention, regulatory compliance, and potential fines.

Description: Measures the percentage of employees and contractors with required training and competency certifications, reflecting the company's commitment to operational safety and effectiveness.
Calculation: (Number of employees and contractors with required training and competency certifications / Total number of employees and contractors) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the effectiveness of operational safety and emergency response measures.
Financial Impact: Directly affects costs associated with incident prevention, regulatory compliance, and potential fines.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a well-trained and competent workforce.

Description: Measures the percentage of incidents subject to thorough investigation and RCA, reflecting the company's commitment to learning from incidents and preventing recurrence.
Calculation: (Number of incidents subject to thorough investigation and RCA / Total number of incidents) x 100
Relevance: Important for evaluating the effectiveness of incident investigation and learning from incidents.
Financial Impact: Indirectly affects costs associated with incident prevention and operational safety.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a culture of learning from incidents and continuous improvement.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources, demonstrating the sector's commitment to clean energy transition and risk mitigation.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: Indicator of the sector's efforts to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and manage energy-related risks.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability, reduced energy costs, and potential revenue benefits from selling excess renewable energy.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainability commitments and clean energy transition efforts.

Metric Name: GHG Emissions Reduction Target Achievement Rate
Description: Progress toward achieving GHG emissions reduction targets, demonstrating the sector's commitment to climate action and risk management.
Calculation: (Actual GHG emissions reduction / Targeted GHG emissions reduction) × 100
Relevance: Indicator of the sector's ability to manage climate-related risks, achieve sustainability goals, and meet regulatory requirements.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced energy consumption, improved brand reputation, and compliance with climate regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and stakeholders value progress toward GHG emissions reduction targets and climate action plans.

Description: Rate of improvement in energy efficiency, measured as energy consumption per unit of production, demonstrating the sector's efforts to optimize operations and reduce energy waste.
Calculation: ((Current energy consumption per unit - Previous energy consumption per unit) / Previous energy consumption per unit) × 100
Relevance: Operational efficiency indicator that impacts costs, energy consumption, and GHG emissions.
Financial Impact: Direct impact on operational expenses, energy costs, and potential revenue benefits from improved efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors focus on operational efficiency, cost management, and sustainability performance.

Description: GHG emissions intensity of raw materials sourced from suppliers, providing insight into the sector's supply chain carbon footprint.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions from supply chain (Scope 3) in kg CO2e / Total units of raw materials sourced
Relevance: Indicator of the sector's supply chain risks, opportunities for collaboration with suppliers, and potential for GHG emissions reduction.
Financial Impact: Potential risks and opportunities related to supply chain disruptions, raw material costs, and sustainability performance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value transparency and management of supply chain sustainability risks.

Description: Estimated potential costs associated with carbon pricing risks, providing insight into the sector's exposure to climate-related financial risks.
Calculation: Total potential carbon pricing costs / Total GHG emissions (Scope 1 & 2) in tons CO2e
Relevance: Indicator of the sector's climate-related financial risks, potential costs, and need for strategic planning.
Financial Impact: Potential costs associated with carbon pricing, regulatory compliance, and climate-related risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors focus on climate-related financial risks, potential costs, and strategic planning.

Description: Assessment of the sector's resilience to climate-related risks, including physical and transition risks, providing insight into its ability to adapt to a low-carbon economy.
Calculation: Composite index score based on multiple factors, including climate-related risk assessments, business continuity planning, and supply chain resilience.
Relevance: Indicator of the sector's ability to manage climate-related risks, ensure business continuity, and adapt to a low-carbon economy.
Financial Impact: Potential costs associated with climate-related risks, business disruptions, and opportunities for climate-resilient innovation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and stakeholders value climate change resilience and adaptability in the face of climate-related risks.

Description: Rate of development and deployment of low-carbon products, services, or solutions, demonstrating the sector's innovation and commitment to a low-carbon economy.
Calculation: (Number of low-carbon products / Total products) × 100
Relevance: Indicator of the sector's innovation, commitment to sustainability, and potential for long-term growth and competitiveness.
Financial Impact: Potential revenue benefits from low-carbon products, improved brand reputation, and first-mover advantages in emerging markets.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value innovation, sustainability performance, and commitment to a low-carbon economy.

Description: Tracks the reduction in PM emissions from production processes over time, which is essential for minimizing negative impacts on human health and the environment.
Calculation: ((Baseline PM emissions - Current PM emissions) / Baseline PM emissions) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to reducing air pollution and improving environmental performance, which can lead to cost savings and enhanced brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Reduces operational costs associated with emissions control and regulatory compliance, while also mitigating reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups value efforts to reduce PM emissions and improve air quality.

Description: Measures the proportion of production facilities with implemented AQMS, which ensures systematic management of air quality risks and compliance with regulations.
Calculation: (Number of facilities with AQMS / Total number of production facilities) × 100
Relevance: Ensures systematic approach to managing air quality risks, reducing regulatory compliance costs, and enhancing operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Reduces costs associated with regulatory non-compliance, improves operational efficiency, and mitigates reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value systematic management of air quality risks and compliance with regulations.

Metric Name: Fuel Consumption per Unit of Production
Description: Tracks fuel consumption per unit of packaging material produced, which contributes to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.
Calculation: Total fuel consumption (liters) / Total tons of packaging material produced
Relevance: Helps optimize energy efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and minimize air pollution from production processes.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, lowers regulatory compliance costs, and mitigates reputational risks associated with climate change and air pollution.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value efforts to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

Description: Tracks the rate of odor complaints from nearby communities, which can indicate inadequate management of air quality risks.
Calculation: Total odor complaints / Total tons of packaging material produced
Relevance: Helps identify areas for improvement in air quality management and minimize negative impacts on local communities.
Financial Impact: Reduces reputational risks, avoids potential fines or penalties, and ensures compliance with environmental regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Local communities, investors, and regulators value efforts to minimize odor complaints and ensure adequate management of air quality risks.

Metric Name: Capital Expenditures for Air Quality Improvements
Description: Tracks capital expenditures for air quality improvements, such as installing pollution control equipment or implementing cleaner production technologies.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures for air quality improvements / Total tons of packaging material produced
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to reducing air pollution and improving environmental performance, which can lead to cost savings and enhanced brand reputation.
Financial Impact: Enhances operational efficiency, reduces regulatory compliance costs, and mitigates reputational risks associated with air pollution.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups value efforts to reduce air pollution and improve environmental performance.

Description: Measures the proportion of production facilities with air quality monitoring systems in place, which ensures systematic tracking of air quality risks.
Calculation: (Number of facilities with air quality monitoring systems / Total number of production facilities) × 100
Relevance: Ensures systematic approach to tracking air quality risks, reducing regulatory compliance costs, and enhancing operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Reduces costs associated with regulatory non-compliance, improves operational efficiency, and mitigates reputational risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value systematic tracking of air quality risks and compliance with regulations.

Metric Name: Forward-Looking Air Quality Risk Assessment Coverage
Description: Tracks the proportion of production facilities with forward-looking air quality risk assessments, which helps identify potential risks and opportunities for improvement.
Calculation: (Number of facilities with forward-looking air quality risk assessments / Total number of production facilities) × 100
Relevance: Helps identify areas for improvement in air quality management, reduce regulatory compliance costs, and enhance operational efficiency.
Financial Impact: Reduces reputational risks, avoids potential fines or penalties, and ensures compliance with environmental regulations.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers value efforts to proactively manage air quality risks and identify opportunities for improvement.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources in manufacturing processes.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to clean energy transition, risk mitigation, and sustainability.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability, regulatory compliance benefits, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainability commitments.

Description: This metric measures the energy intensity of packaging materials used, providing insight into material selection and sustainability.
Calculation: Total energy required to produce packaging materials (MJ) / Total weight of packaging materials used (kg)
Relevance: This metric helps optimize packaging material selection, reduce energy consumption, and minimize environmental impact.
Financial Impact: Reduced material costs, improved supply chain resilience, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value sustainable material selection.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of energy-efficient equipment adopted in manufacturing processes.
Calculation: (Number of energy-efficient equipment / Total equipment) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to energy efficiency, operational optimization, and sustainability.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy consumption, lower maintenance costs, and improved productivity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value energy-efficient practices.

Metric Name: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions per Unit of Packaging
Description: This metric measures the total GHG emissions per unit of packaging produced, providing insight into climate impact.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions (kg CO2e) / Total units of packaging produced
Relevance: This metric is essential for Containers & Packaging companies, as it helps reduce climate impact, comply with regulations, and manage risks.
Financial Impact: Regulatory compliance costs, carbon pricing risks, and reputation management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value climate action and GHG reduction efforts.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of operations covered by an EMS, providing insight into energy management practices.
Calculation: (Operations covered by EMS / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to systematic energy management, operational optimization, and sustainability.
Financial Impact: Improved energy efficiency, reduced costs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value systematic energy management practices.

Description: This metric measures the energy savings achieved through efficiency projects, providing insight into operational optimization.
Calculation: Total energy savings (kWh/year) from efficiency projects
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to energy efficiency, operational optimization, and sustainability.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy consumption, lower costs, and improved competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value energy efficiency efforts.

Description: This metric measures the company's forward-looking energy reduction target, providing insight into future energy management plans.
Calculation: Specific percentage reduction target (e.g., 20% by 2025)
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to long-term energy management, sustainability, and climate action.
Financial Impact: Anticipated cost savings, regulatory compliance benefits, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value forward-looking energy reduction targets and plans.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of recycled water used in manufacturing processes, indicating the company's commitment to water conservation and circular economy practices.
Calculation: (Recycled water volume / Total water consumption) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates the company's efforts to reduce freshwater intake, minimize wastewater generation, and promote sustainable water management.
Financial Impact: Reduces water procurement costs and wastewater treatment expenses, while enhancing brand reputation and stakeholder trust.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, sustainability-focused investors, and customers value water conservation and recycling efforts.

Description: This metric measures the capital expenditures related to water management, including investments in water-saving technologies, recycling facilities, and wastewater treatment infrastructure.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures related to water management
Relevance: Indicates the company's commitment to water management and its impact on financial performance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, capital expenditures, and potential returns on investment.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and analysts focus on capital allocation and ROI related to sustainability initiatives.

Description: This metric measures the rate of freshwater withdrawal per ton of packaging produced, providing insight into the company's water footprint and potential impact on local water resources.
Calculation: Total freshwater withdrawal (liters) / Total tons of packaging produced
Relevance: Essential for understanding and managing water-related risks, such as water scarcity and regulatory restrictions.
Financial Impact: Affects water procurement costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and potential business continuity risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and local communities focus on water usage and its impact on the environment.

Description: This metric measures the efficiency of wastewater treatment processes, indicating the company's ability to minimize environmental impact and comply with regulatory requirements.
Calculation: (Treated wastewater volume / Total wastewater generated) × 100
Relevance: Critical for environmental sustainability, regulatory compliance, and minimizing wastewater-related risks.
Financial Impact: Reduces wastewater treatment costs, potential regulatory fines, and environmental liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, regulators, and investors focus on wastewater management and environmental sustainability.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of operations covered by water risk assessments, indicating the company's awareness and management of water-related risks.
Calculation: (Operations covered by water risk assessments / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: Essential for identifying and mitigating water-related risks, such as water scarcity, flooding, and regulatory changes.
Financial Impact: Helps minimize potential business disruptions, regulatory fines, and environmental liabilities.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and business leaders focus on risk management and strategic planning.

Description: This metric measures the percentage of operations covered by a water management policy, indicating the company's commitment to sustainable water practices.
Calculation: (Operations covered by water management policy / Total operations) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates the company's commitment to water sustainability and its integration into business operations.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, stakeholder trust, and potential long-term business resilience.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with robust water management policies.

Description: This metric measures the company's target for reducing water usage in the future, indicating its commitment to water conservation and sustainability.
Calculation: Specific target for water use reduction (e.g., 20% reduction in water consumption per ton of packaging produced within 5 years)
Relevance: Essential for strategic planning, goal-setting, and measuring progress toward water sustainability objectives.
Financial Impact: Can lead to cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and enhanced stakeholder trust.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with ambitious yet achievable sustainability targets.

Description: Measures the proportion of recyclable materials used in packaging production, reflecting the company's commitment to sustainable material sourcing.
Calculation: (Total recyclable materials used / Total materials used) × 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's efforts to promote recycling and reduce waste, which can contribute to cost savings and environmental benefits.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from using recyclable materials and reduced waste disposal costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and sustainability-focused investors value companies that prioritize recyclable materials.

Description: Measures the company's compliance with regulations and standards related to hazardous materials management, reflecting its commitment to safe and responsible operations.
Calculation: (Number of compliant hazardous materials management incidents / Total hazardous materials management incidents) × 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's ability to manage hazardous materials safely and mitigate potential risks to human health and the environment.
Financial Impact: Reduced risk of fines, penalties, and reputational damage from non-compliance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and customers value companies that prioritize safe and responsible hazardous materials management.

Description: Measures the proportion of waste converted to energy, reflecting the company's efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and generate renewable energy.
Calculation: (Total waste converted to energy / Total waste generated) × 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's progress in reducing waste and generating renewable energy, which can contribute to cost savings and environmental benefits.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced waste disposal costs and revenue generated from energy sales.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and sustainability-focused investors value companies that prioritize waste-to-energy conversion.

Description: Measures the proportion of packaging designs that meet recyclability standards, reflecting the company's commitment to sustainable packaging design.
Calculation: (Number of packaging designs meeting recyclability standards / Total packaging designs) × 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's efforts to design packaging that is recyclable and sustainable, which can contribute to reduced waste and environmental benefits.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced waste disposal costs and improved brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value companies that prioritize sustainable packaging design.

Description: Measures the reduction in landfill waste generated per unit of production, reflecting the company's efforts to minimize waste sent to landfills.
Calculation: ((Total landfill waste generated in previous year - Total landfill waste generated in current year) / Total landfill waste generated in previous year) × 100
Relevance: Indicates progress in reducing waste sent to landfills and minimizing environmental impact.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs and potential savings from optimized waste management practices.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups and sustainability-focused investors value companies that prioritize landfill waste reduction.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Packaging Waste Reduction Rate
Description: Measures the reduction in packaging waste generated throughout the supply chain, reflecting the company's efforts to engage suppliers in sustainable packaging practices.
Calculation: ((Total supply chain packaging waste generated in previous year - Total supply chain packaging waste generated in current year) / Total supply chain packaging waste generated in previous year) × 100
Relevance: Indicates the company's progress in promoting sustainable packaging practices throughout its supply chain.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from reduced waste disposal costs and improved supply chain efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that engage suppliers in sustainable practices.

Description: Measures the company's innovation in developing circular economy packaging solutions, reflecting its commitment to sustainable packaging design and waste reduction.
Calculation: Based on a weighted assessment of factors such as packaging design for recyclability, use of recycled materials, and closed-loop production.
Relevance: Indicates the company's progress in developing innovative packaging solutions that support a circular economy.
Financial Impact: Potential revenue growth from innovative packaging solutions and improved brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies that prioritize circular economy innovation.

Metric Name: Compliance Rate with Packaging Safety Standards
Description: Measures the percentage of packaging products that comply with relevant safety standards and regulations, such as those related to food safety, child-resistant packaging, or hazardous materials handling.
Calculation: (Number of compliant packaging products / Total packaging products) x 100
Relevance: Ensures adherence to regulatory requirements, reducing the risk of non-compliance, fines, and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Avoids costly fines, litigation, and potential revenue loss due to product recalls or suspension of sales.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, customers, and investors expect companies to comply with safety standards, and a high compliance rate demonstrates a commitment to responsible business practices.

Metric Name: Customer Complaint Rate related to Product Safety
Description: Measures the number of customer complaints related to product safety issues, such as packaging defects, contamination, or misuse.
Calculation: (Number of customer complaints related to product safety / Total number of customers) x 1,000
Relevance: A low complaint rate indicates effective product safety measures, customer satisfaction, and reduced risk of reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Directly affects customer retention, revenue, and potential costs associated with resolving complaints.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value product safety, and a low complaint rate demonstrates a commitment to customer satisfaction and responsible business practices.

Description: Measures the safety assessment score of packaging materials used, considering factors such as toxicity, recyclability, and sustainability.
Calculation: Based on a comprehensive assessment framework, such as a weighted scoring model, considering multiple material safety criteria.
Relevance: Ensures the use of safe and sustainable packaging materials, reducing risks associated with material hazards and environmental impacts.
Financial Impact: Affects procurement costs, operational efficiency, and potential regulatory compliance costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainable and safe packaging materials, and a high score demonstrates a commitment to responsible sourcing practices.

Description: Measures the number of product recalls due to safety issues, such as packaging defects or contamination.
Calculation: (Number of product recalls / Total units sold) x 1,000,000
Relevance: A low recall rate indicates effective product safety measures, reducing the risk of reputational damage, financial losses, and regulatory penalties.
Financial Impact: Directly affects revenue, profitability, and potential costs associated with product recalls.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value product safety, and a low recall rate demonstrates a commitment to responsible business practices.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Partner Safety Compliance Rate
Description: Measures the percentage of supply chain partners that comply with the company's product safety standards and requirements.
Calculation: (Number of compliant supply chain partners / Total supply chain partners) x 100
Relevance: Ensures that supply chain partners adhere to product safety standards, reducing risks associated with non-compliance and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Affects procurement costs, operational efficiency, and potential regulatory compliance costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies value supply chain transparency and safety compliance, and a high compliance rate demonstrates a commitment to responsible sourcing practices.

Metric Name: Employee Training Hours on Product Safety
Description: Measures the number of training hours provided to employees on product safety procedures, standards, and best practices.
Calculation: Total training hours on product safety / Total number of employees
Relevance: Ensures that employees are equipped to handle product safety issues, reducing risks associated with human error and non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Affects operational efficiency, employee productivity, and potential costs associated with product safety incidents.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and employees value product safety training, and a high training rate demonstrates a commitment to employee development and responsible business practices.

Description: Measures the frequency of product safety incidents, such as accidents or near-misses, per million hours worked.
Calculation: (Number of product safety incidents / Total hours worked) x 1,000,000
Relevance: A low incident frequency rate indicates effective product safety measures, reducing risks associated with accidents and non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational costs, employee productivity, and potential regulatory compliance costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and employees value product safety, and a low incident frequency rate demonstrates a commitment to responsible business practices and employee well-being.

Description: Measures the ease of disassembly of packaging products, with higher scores indicating easier disassembly.
Calculation: Weighted average of design features (e.g., material selection, joinery, labeling) evaluated by expert assessment.
Relevance: Facilitates recycling and reduces waste by designing products for disassembly.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs, potential revenue from recycling programs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value product design innovations that support sustainability.

Description: Total weight of biodegradable materials used in product packaging.
Calculation: Sum of biodegradable materials weight used in production.
Relevance: Reduces environmental impact by using biodegradable materials that can easily decompose.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from using biodegradable materials, reduced waste disposal costs, and potential revenue from eco-friendly products.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers value sustainable packaging practices.

Description: Percentage of products returned through take-back programs or collected for recycling.
Calculation: (Products returned / Total products sold) × 100
Relevance: Encourages product recycling and reduces waste by implementing take-back programs.
Financial Impact: Potential revenue from recycling programs, reduced waste disposal costs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value closed-loop product management.

Description: Percentage of suppliers that provide transparent material sourcing information.
Calculation: (Suppliers providing transparent material sourcing / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Ensures responsible material sourcing and reduces supply chain risks.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, potential cost savings from responsible sourcing, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value transparent supply chain practices.

Description: Total cost of managing end-of-life products, including recycling, disposal, and take-back programs.
Calculation: Total end-of-life management cost / Total weight of products managed
Relevance: Measures the efficiency of end-of-life product management and potential cost savings.
Financial Impact: Direct cost impact on business operations, potential cost savings from efficient end-of-life management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and executive management value cost-efficient product lifecycle management.

Description: Percentage of new product designs that meet recyclability criteria.
Calculation: (New product designs meeting recyclability criteria / Total new product designs) × 100
Relevance: Encourages product design innovations that support recyclability and reduces waste.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from designing recyclable products, reduced waste disposal costs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value product design innovations that support sustainability.

Description: Percentage of materials recycled and reused in production.
Calculation: (Materials recycled and reused / Total materials used) × 100
Relevance: Measures progress toward a circular economy and reduces waste.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings from using recycled materials, reduced waste disposal costs, and potential revenue from eco-friendly products.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers value closed-loop recycling practices.

Description: Measures the percentage of packaging materials designed for recyclability, reflecting the company's commitment to circular economy principles and waste reduction.
Calculation: (Weight of recyclable packaging materials / Total weight of packaging materials) × 100
Relevance: Critical for reducing waste, conserving natural resources, and meeting customer expectations for sustainable packaging.
Financial Impact: Drives cost savings through material efficiency, reduces waste disposal costs, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups prioritize sustainable packaging and waste reduction.

Unit: Metric tons CO2e / unit of production
Description: Measures the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions intensity of the supply chain, from raw material extraction to finished product delivery.
Calculation: Total supply chain GHG emissions (Metric tons CO2e) / Total units of production
Relevance: Essential for understanding and managing climate-related risks, opportunities, and regulatory compliance in the supply chain.
Financial Impact: Reduces energy costs, mitigates climate-related risks, and supports low-carbon transition strategies.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and policymakers focus on climate action and GHG emissions reduction.

Description: Evaluates the diversity and inclusion performance of suppliers, including metrics such as minority-owned, women-owned, and small business participation.
Calculation: Weighted index score based on supplier diversity metrics (e.g., 30% minority-owned, 20% women-owned, 50% small business participation)
Relevance: Fosters a diverse and inclusive supply chain, promoting innovation, and community engagement.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, supports local economic development, and encourages supplier innovation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and community groups value diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives.

Metric Name: Lead Time and Inventory Turnover Ratio
Description: Measures supply chain efficiency through lead time and inventory turnover, reflecting the company's ability to respond to changing demand and manage working capital.
Calculation: Lead time (days) and inventory turnover ratio (cost of goods sold / average inventory)
Relevance: Critical for optimizing supply chain operations, reducing costs, and improving customer satisfaction.
Financial Impact: Reduces inventory holding costs, improves cash flow, and enhances supply chain resilience.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and executives prioritize efficient supply chain operations.

Description: Measures the percentage of raw materials sourced responsibly, including certified sustainable materials (e.g., FSC-certified wood, conflict-free minerals).
Calculation: (Weight of responsibly sourced raw materials / Total weight of raw materials) × 100
Relevance: Essential for mitigating environmental and social risks associated with raw material extraction and sourcing.
Financial Impact: Supports long-term supply chain resilience, reduces reputational risks, and enhances brand value.
Stakeholder Perspective: NGOs, customers, and investors prioritize responsible sourcing and sustainable materials.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Disruption and Risk Assessment
Description: Evaluates the company's ability to identify, assess, and mitigate supply chain disruptions and risks, including natural disasters, supplier insolvency, and cyber threats.
Calculation: Number of disruptions and risk score (e.g., based on likelihood and impact assessments)
Relevance: Critical for ensuring business continuity, minimizing losses, and maintaining customer satisfaction.
Financial Impact: Reduces costs associated with supply chain disruptions, maintains revenue streams, and protects brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and executives prioritize supply chain resilience and risk management.

Description: Measures the level of collaboration and innovation with suppliers to develop new products, processes, or services that drive sustainability and business value.
Calculation: Weighted index score based on collaboration metrics (e.g., joint R&D projects, supplier innovation awards)
Relevance: Fosters a culture of innovation and collaboration, driving growth, and competitive advantage.
Financial Impact: Enhances brand reputation, generates new revenue streams, and improves supply chain efficiency.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and suppliers value collaborative innovation and sustainable growth initiatives.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources, which demonstrates commitment to clean energy transition and risk mitigation.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric shows the company's progress towards reducing dependence on fossil fuels and lowering carbon footprint.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability, regulatory compliance benefits, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value sustainability commitments.

Description: Percentage of total sales from energy-efficient products, which indicates the company's contribution to reducing energy consumption.
Calculation: (Energy-efficient product sales / Total product sales) × 100
Relevance: This metric highlights the company's efforts to develop and market products that help customers reduce their energy usage.
Financial Impact: Revenue growth from energy-efficient products and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors value products that support sustainability goals.

Description: Assessment of energy management practices and performance in the supply chain, which helps to identify areas for improvement.
Calculation: Weighted average of supplier energy management scores, based on a survey or audit.
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's influence on its supply chain's energy usage and sustainability practices.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, improved supplier relationships, and cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value responsible supply chain management.

Description: Total capital expenditures related to energy management initiatives, such as energy-efficient equipment and renewable energy systems.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures for energy-related projects
Relevance: This metric shows the company's investment in energy management and its commitment to reducing energy consumption.
Financial Impact: Future cost savings, revenue growth, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors value strategic investments in energy management.

Description: Total greenhouse gas emissions per unit of electronic equipment produced, which helps to assess the company's carbon footprint.
Calculation: Total greenhouse gas emissions (t CO2e) / Total units produced
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's progress towards reducing its carbon footprint and mitigating climate change risks.
Financial Impact: Regulatory compliance costs, carbon pricing risks, and brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value greenhouse gas emissions reductions.

Description: Assessment of the company's energy management practices, including policies, procedures, and performance metrics.
Calculation: Weighted average of energy management practice scores, based on a survey or audit.
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's readiness to manage energy-related risks and opportunities.
Financial Impact: Improved operational efficiency, reduced energy costs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors value robust energy management practices.

Metric Name: Research and Development Investment in Energy Efficiency
Description: Total research and development investments in energy-efficient technologies and products.
Calculation: Total R&D expenditures for energy-efficient projects
Relevance: This metric shows the company's commitment to innovation and developing energy-efficient solutions.
Financial Impact: Future revenue growth, cost savings, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors value strategic investments in research and development.

Description: Tracks the percentage of recyclable materials recovered from hazardous waste streams, demonstrating commitment to circular economy practices.
Calculation: (Recyclable materials recovered / Total hazardous waste generated) × 100
Relevance: Highlights the effectiveness of waste recycling programs and potential for cost savings through material recovery.
Financial Impact: Impacts waste disposal costs, revenue from recyclable materials sales, and potential environmental liability reductions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers value companies with robust recycling programs.

Description: Measures the utilization rate of hazardous waste storage facilities, indicating potential risks and operational efficiency.
Calculation: (Total hazardous waste stored / Total storage capacity) × 100
Relevance: Essential for ensuring regulatory compliance, managing potential environmental risks, and optimizing storage capacity.
Financial Impact: Affects operational costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and potential liabilities associated with hazardous waste storage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulatory bodies, investors, and local communities focus on safe and compliant hazardous waste management practices.

Description: Tracks the frequency of non-compliance events related to hazardous waste management, such as spills or permit violations.
Calculation: Total non-compliance events / Total units produced (in millions)
Relevance: Critical for evaluating the effectiveness of environmental management systems and regulatory compliance programs.
Financial Impact: Directly affects regulatory compliance costs, potential fines and penalties, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and local communities prioritize compliance and risk management.

Metric Name: Hazardous Waste Disposal Cost per Unit
Description: Measures the cost of disposing of hazardous waste per unit of electronic equipment produced, providing insight into operational expenses.
Calculation: Total hazardous waste disposal costs / Total units produced
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the financial impact of hazardous waste management practices and identifying opportunities for cost reduction.
Financial Impact: Directly affects operational expenses, profitability, and competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and executive management focus on cost management and operational efficiency.

Metric Name: Employee Training Hours on Hazardous Waste Management
Description: Tracks the amount of training provided to employees on hazardous waste management practices, ensuring a competent workforce.
Calculation: Total training hours / Total employees
Relevance: Critical for ensuring regulatory compliance, minimizing risks, and promoting a culture of sustainability.
Financial Impact: Impacts operational efficiency, regulatory compliance costs, and potential liabilities associated with human error.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulatory bodies, and employees value comprehensive training programs.

Metric Name: Hazardous Waste Reduction Target Achievement Rate
Description: Measures the achievement rate of hazardous waste reduction targets, demonstrating commitment to sustainability and operational improvement.
Calculation: (Actual waste reduction / Target waste reduction) × 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating progress toward sustainability goals and identifying areas for improvement.
Financial Impact: Impacts operational costs, regulatory compliance expenses, and potential environmental liability reductions.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups value companies with ambitious and achievable sustainability targets.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Hazardous Waste Management Assessment Rate
Description: Tracks the percentage of suppliers assessed for hazardous waste management practices, ensuring responsible sourcing.
Calculation: (Suppliers assessed / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Critical for managing supply chain risks, promoting sustainability, and ensuring regulatory compliance.
Financial Impact: Impacts supply chain resilience, operational costs, and potential reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups prioritize responsible supply chain management practices.

Description: Tracks the percentage of products that meet or exceed relevant safety certifications and standards, such as UL (Underwriters Laboratories) or CE (Conformité Européene) markings.
Calculation: (Number of products with safety certifications / Total products sold) x 100
Relevance: Ensures compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards, reducing the risk of non-compliance and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can result in fines, penalties, and costly rework or product recalls. A high compliance rate reduces these risks and associated costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators and customers expect manufacturers to meet safety standards, while investors value compliance as a risk management strategy.

Description: Measures the number of customer complaints related to product safety or performance per 1,000 units sold, providing insight into potential product issues.
Calculation: (Number of customer complaints / Total units sold) x 1,000
Relevance: Helps identify potential product safety concerns and areas for improvement in product design, testing, or manufacturing processes.
Financial Impact: High complaint rates can lead to increased customer support costs, potential product recalls, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers expect prompt resolution of complaints, while investors monitor complaint rates as an indicator of product quality and safety.

Description: Tracks the percentage of products that have undergone hazard analysis, such as Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) or Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies.
Calculation: (Number of products with hazard analysis / Total products sold) x 100
Relevance: Proactive hazard analysis helps identify and mitigate potential safety risks, reducing the likelihood of product failures or recalls.
Financial Impact: Reduces the risk of costly product recalls, liability, and reputational damage. A high coverage rate indicates a robust product safety management system.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a systematic approach to product safety risk management.

Description: Measures the percentage of suppliers that have undergone risk assessments for product safety and quality, ensuring that suppliers meet safety standards.
Calculation: (Number of assessed suppliers / Total suppliers) x 100
Relevance: Critical for ensuring that suppliers adhere to safety standards, reducing the risk of non-compliant products entering the supply chain.
Financial Impact: Reduces the risk of product failures, recalls, and liability associated with non-compliant suppliers.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers expect manufacturers to ensure that their supply chains meet safety standards.

Metric Name: Product Safety Training Hours per Employee
Description: Tracks the average number of product safety training hours provided to employees per year, ensuring that personnel have the necessary knowledge and skills to ensure product safety.
Calculation: Total product safety training hours / Total employees
Relevance: Essential for maintaining a culture of product safety and ensuring that employees understand safety procedures and protocols.
Financial Impact: Well-trained employees can help prevent product failures, reduce warranty costs, and minimize liability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value a well-trained workforce as a key component of a robust product safety management system.

Description: Measures the number of product recalls per 1,000 units sold, reflecting the effectiveness of product safety management systems.
Calculation: (Number of product recalls / Total units sold) x 1,000
Relevance: A critical lagging indicator of product safety performance, providing insight into the effectiveness of safety management systems.
Financial Impact: Product recalls can result in significant financial losses, reputational damage, and liability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulators closely monitor product recall rates as an indicator of product safety performance.

Description: Tracks the percentage of revenue invested in product safety initiatives, such as research and development, testing, and safety certifications.
Calculation: (Product safety investments / Total revenue) x 100
Relevance: Demonstrates a company's commitment to product safety and proactive investment in safety management systems.
Financial Impact: A high investment ratio indicates a proactive approach to product safety, potentially reducing warranty costs, liability, and reputational damage.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors value a company's commitment to product safety as a long-term strategy for sustainable growth and profitability.

Unit: kWh (or other relevant energy unit) per product unit
Description: Average energy consumption of products sold, measured against industry benchmarks and internal targets, to assess progress in designing more energy-efficient products.
Calculation: Total energy consumption of products sold (in kWh) / Total number of products sold
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's ability to design and deliver energy-efficient products, reducing customer energy costs and environmental impacts.
Financial Impact: Reduced energy costs for customers, increased market share through competitive energy-efficient products, and potential regulatory compliance benefits.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulatory bodies focus on energy efficiency as a key aspect of sustainable product design.

Description: Percentage reduction in hazardous substances used in products, measured against a baseline, to minimize environmental and health impacts.
Calculation: (Reduction in hazardous substances used / Baseline hazardous substances used) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's efforts to eliminate hazardous substances from products, reducing environmental and health risks.
Financial Impact: Reduced regulatory compliance costs, lower liability risks, and enhanced brand reputation through responsible material management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers value companies that prioritize responsible material management and hazardous substance reduction.

Description: Percentage of products sold that are collected and recycled through company-led take-back programs or other recycling initiatives.
Calculation: (Number of products collected and recycled / Total number of products sold) × 100
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's commitment to product end-of-life management, reducing electronic waste and supporting a circular economy.
Financial Impact: Reduced waste disposal costs, potential revenue streams from recycled materials, and enhanced brand reputation through responsible product lifecycle management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers increasingly value companies that prioritize product take-back and recycling.

Metric Name: Supply Chain Material Sourcing Risk Index
Description: Assessment of supply chain risks related to material sourcing, including conflict minerals, rare earth metals, and other critical materials.
Calculation: Weighted index score based on supplier risk assessments, material criticality, and company mitigation efforts
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's ability to manage supply chain risks related to material sourcing, ensuring responsible and sustainable material procurement.
Financial Impact: Reduced supply chain risks, lower costs through responsible material sourcing, and enhanced brand reputation through sustainable supply chain management.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and regulatory bodies focus on responsible supply chain management and material sourcing.

Metric Name: Product Design and Development Cycle Time
Description: Time-to-market for new product designs and iterations, measuring the company's ability to innovate and respond to changing market needs.
Calculation: Time elapsed between initial product concept and market launch
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's ability to innovate and deliver new products, driving business growth and competitiveness.
Financial Impact: Increased revenue through faster time-to-market, improved market share through innovative products, and reduced R&D costs through efficient design and development processes.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and executive management focus on innovation and time-to-market as key drivers of business success.

Description: Customer satisfaction with product end-of-life management, including take-back programs, recycling options, and responsible disposal practices.
Calculation: (Number of customers satisfied with product end-of-life management / Total customers surveyed) × 100
Relevance: This metric evaluates the company's ability to deliver responsible product lifecycle management, enhancing customer satisfaction and loyalty.
Financial Impact: Increased customer loyalty, reduced customer churn, and potential revenue streams through customer retention and positive word-of-mouth.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value companies that prioritize responsible product end-of-life management and customer satisfaction.

Description: Percentage of recycled materials used in new products, measured against internal targets and industry benchmarks.
Calculation: (Amount of recycled materials used / Total materials used) × 100
Relevance: This metric assesses the company's commitment to a circular economy, reducing waste and promoting sustainable material management.
Financial Impact: Reduced material costs, lower waste disposal costs, and potential revenue streams through closed-loop recycling.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers increasingly value companies that prioritize closed-loop recycling and sustainable material management.

Unit: Kilograms of materials used per unit of product (kg/unit)
Description: Measures the amount of materials used per unit of product, reflecting the company's ability to optimize material usage and reduce waste.
Calculation: Total materials used (kg) / Total units produced
Relevance: Indicator of operational efficiency, waste reduction, and resource conservation.
Financial Impact: Reduces material costs, minimizes waste disposal expenses, and improves profitability.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers focus on resource efficiency and waste reduction.

Description: Percentage of recycled materials used in products, reflecting the company's commitment to circular economy practices.
Calculation: (Total recycled materials used / Total materials used) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to sustainability, waste reduction, and resource conservation.
Financial Impact: Reduces material costs, potentially leads to cost savings, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value recycled materials content.

Description: Percentage of suppliers assessed for sustainability risks, such as environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors.
Calculation: (Total suppliers assessed / Total suppliers) × 100
Relevance: Indicator of supply chain risk management, transparency, and sustainability commitment.
Financial Impact: Reduces supply chain risks, improves brand reputation, and potentially leads to cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value supply chain risk management and transparency.

Description: Percentage of products designed for recyclability, reflecting the company's commitment to circular economy practices and end-of-life product management.
Calculation: (Total products designed for recyclability / Total products) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to sustainability, waste reduction, and resource conservation.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal expenses, potentially leads to cost savings, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value design for recyclability.

Description: Percentage of e-waste generated that is recycled or reused, reflecting the company's commitment to responsible end-of-life product management.
Calculation: (Total e-waste recycled or reused / Total e-waste generated) × 100
Relevance: Indicator of responsible product lifecycle management, waste reduction, and sustainability commitment.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal expenses, potentially leads to cost savings, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value e-waste recycling and responsible product management.

Description: Percentage of conflict-free minerals sourced, reflecting the company's commitment to responsible sourcing and risk management.
Calculation: (Total conflict-free minerals sourced / Total minerals sourced) × 100
Relevance: Demonstrates commitment to responsible sourcing, risk management, and supply chain transparency.
Financial Impact: Reduces supply chain risks, improves brand reputation, and potentially leads to cost savings.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and NGOs value conflict-free minerals sourcing.

Metric Name: Product Take-Back and Recycling Program Coverage
Description: Percentage of products covered by take-back and recycling programs, reflecting the company's commitment to responsible end-of-life product management.
Calculation: (Total products covered by take-back and recycling programs / Total products sold) × 100
Relevance: Indicator of responsible product lifecycle management, waste reduction, and sustainability commitment.
Financial Impact: Reduces waste disposal expenses, potentially leads to cost savings, and enhances brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value product take-back and recycling programs.

Description: Tracks the percentage of whistleblower reports responded to within a specified timeframe (e.g., 72 hours), demonstrating the company's commitment to addressing ethics concerns.
Calculation: (Number of reports responded to within timeframe / Total number of reports) × 100
Relevance: Ensures timely and effective response to ethics concerns, promoting a culture of transparency and accountability.
Financial Impact: Encourages a culture of openness, reducing risk of reputational damage and potential financial losses.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a company's responsiveness to ethics concerns.

Description: Measures the percentage of employees, business partners, and third-party vendors covered by anti-corruption policies and procedures.
Calculation: (Number of covered parties / Total number of parties) × 100
Relevance: Ensures comprehensive coverage of anti-corruption policies, reducing risk of non-compliance and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of fines, penalties, and reputational damage, resulting in cost savings and preserved brand value.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to maintain robust anti-corruption policies.

Description: Tracks the frequency of ethics incidents (e.g., code of conduct violations, corruption allegations) per 100 employees, assessing the effectiveness of business ethics programs.
Calculation: (Number of incidents / Total number of employees) × 100
Relevance: Identifies areas for improvement in business ethics programs, enabling proactive measures to prevent future incidents.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of fines, penalties, and reputational damage, resulting in cost savings and preserved brand value.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to maintain a strong track record of business ethics.

Description: Measures the percentage of business partners and third-party vendors assessed for ethics risks, ensuring due diligence in partner selection.
Calculation: (Number of assessed partners / Total number of partners) × 100
Relevance: Ensures comprehensive risk assessment of business partners, reducing risk of reputational damage and non-compliance.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of reputational damage and potential financial losses associated with high-risk business partners.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to maintain robust due diligence processes.

Description: Tracks employee sentiment on business ethics through regular surveys, assessing perceptions of ethics culture and program effectiveness.
Calculation: Average survey response score
Relevance: Provides insights into employee perceptions of business ethics, enabling targeted improvements to ethics programs.
Financial Impact: Enhances employee engagement, reduces turnover, and promotes a positive reputation, ultimately driving business performance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and employees value a strong ethics culture, which can drive long-term success.

Description: Measures the percentage of corrective actions implemented in response to ethics incidents or risk assessments, demonstrating commitment to remediation and improvement.
Calculation: (Number of implemented actions / Total number of actions) × 100
Relevance: Ensures timely and effective implementation of corrective actions, reducing risk of repeated incidents and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Reduces risk of fines, penalties, and reputational damage, resulting in cost savings and preserved brand value.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to take proactive steps to address ethics concerns.

Description: Tracks the maturity of business ethics programs, assessing effectiveness of policies, procedures, and training initiatives.
Calculation: Weighted average score across multiple program components (e.g., policies, training, reporting)
Relevance: Provides a comprehensive assessment of business ethics program effectiveness, enabling targeted improvements and benchmarking.
Financial Impact: Enhances reputation, reduces risk of non-compliance, and promotes long-term sustainability, ultimately driving business performance.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and customers expect companies to maintain robust business ethics programs, which can drive long-term success.

Description: Annual rate of energy efficiency improvement, measured as a reduction in energy consumption per unit of production.
Calculation: ((Energy consumption per unit of production (current year) - Energy consumption per unit of production (previous year)) / Energy consumption per unit of production (previous year)) × 100
Relevance: This metric tracks progress in implementing energy-efficient technologies and practices.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings, reduced energy expenses, and improved competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that demonstrate continuous improvement in energy efficiency.

Description: Percentage of total energy consumption from renewable sources, reflecting commitment to clean energy transition and risk mitigation.
Calculation: (Renewable energy consumption / Total energy consumption) × 100
Relevance: This metric demonstrates a company's commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and mitigating climate-related risks.
Financial Impact: Long-term cost stability, potential revenue opportunities from clean energy sales, and regulatory compliance benefits.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups increasingly value sustainability commitments.

Description: Annual capital expenditures related to energy management, including investments in energy-efficient technologies and renewable energy systems.
Calculation: Total capital expenditures for energy-related projects
Relevance: This metric tracks investments in energy management and potential future cost savings.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and revenue growth.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors focus on capital allocation, growth prospects, and sustainability performance.

Description: Percentage of production facilities or operations covered by an energy management system (EMS), reflecting systematic approach to energy management.
Calculation: (Number of facilities with EMS / Total number of facilities) × 100
Relevance: This metric indicates a company's commitment to structured energy management and continuous improvement.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and reduced energy-related risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value systematic approaches to sustainability and energy management.

Metric Name: Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions per Unit of Production
Description: Total GHG emissions per unit of finished product, reflecting climate-related performance and energy intensity.
Calculation: Total GHG emissions (t CO2e) / Total units produced
Relevance: This metric tracks progress in reducing climate-related impacts and energy consumption.
Financial Impact: Potential carbon pricing risks, regulatory compliance costs, and reputational impacts.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, customers, and environmental groups focus on climate-related performance and GHG emissions reduction.

Description: Total energy storage capacity installed, reflecting ability to manage energy demand and optimize production processes.
Calculation: Total energy storage capacity installed (kWh)
Relevance: This metric indicates a company's ability to manage energy demand, optimize production, and reduce energy-related costs.
Financial Impact: Potential cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and revenue growth from energy storage services.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that demonstrate innovative approaches to energy management.

Metric Name: Energy Management Training and Development Hours
Description: Total hours of energy management training and development provided to employees, reflecting commitment to capacity building and operational excellence.
Calculation: Total hours of energy management training and development provided
Relevance: This metric indicates a company's commitment to employee development, operational excellence, and energy management best practices.
Financial Impact: Potential long-term cost savings, improved operational efficiency, and reduced energy-related risks.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and customers value companies that invest in employee development and sustainability performance.

Metric Name: Occupational Health and Safety (OH&S) Training Coverage
Description: Tracks the proportion of employees who have received OH&S training, ensuring that the workforce is equipped to identify and mitigate hazards.
Calculation: (Number of employees trained / Total number of employees) x 100
Relevance: Critical for maintaining a safe work environment and demonstrating a proactive approach to health and safety management.
Financial Impact: Reduces the risk of accidents, injuries, and associated costs, while also enhancing employee productivity and engagement.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulators expect companies to prioritize health and safety training.

Metric Name: Workforce Health and Wellness Program Participation
Description: Measures the proportion of employees participating in health and wellness programs, such as employee assistance programs (EAPs) or fitness initiatives.
Calculation: (Number of employees participating / Total number of employees) x 100
Relevance: Supports employee well-being, reduces absenteeism, and enhances productivity.
Financial Impact: Can lead to reduced healthcare costs, improved employee retention, and increased productivity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees value companies that invest in their well-being, while investors appreciate the long-term benefits of a healthy workforce.

Description: Tracks the rate of work-related incidents that require recording, providing insight into the effectiveness of health and safety programs.
Calculation: (Number of recordable incidents / Total working hours) x 200,000
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the impact of health and safety initiatives on reducing workplace incidents.
Financial Impact: Directly affects workers' compensation costs, medical expenses, and potential production downtime.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and employees expect companies to maintain a safe work environment.

Description: Measures the investments made in safety-related capital expenditures, such as equipment upgrades or safety infrastructure.
Calculation: Total safety-related CapEx
Relevance: Demonstrates a company's commitment to maintaining a safe work environment and reducing risks.
Financial Impact: Can lead to reduced accident and injury rates, lower workers' compensation costs, and improved productivity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors and regulators value companies that prioritize safety investments.

Description: Tracks employee perceptions of the company's safety culture through surveys or assessments.
Calculation: Average index score from employee surveys
Relevance: Essential for understanding the effectiveness of health and safety programs and identifying areas for improvement.
Financial Impact: A positive safety culture can lead to improved employee engagement, reduced turnover, and increased productivity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees value a safe and supportive work environment.

Metric Name: Compliance with Health and Safety Regulations
Description: Measures the company's compliance with relevant health and safety regulations and standards.
Calculation: (Number of compliant sites / Total number of sites) x 100
Relevance: Critical for avoiding regulatory fines, penalties, and reputational damage.
Financial Impact: Non-compliance can result in significant financial costs, while compliance demonstrates a commitment to responsible business practices.
Stakeholder Perspective: Regulators, investors, and customers expect companies to maintain a strong compliance record.

Description: Tracks the proportion of employees who return to work after a work-related injury or illness.
Calculation: (Number of employees returned to work / Total number of employees with work-related injuries or illnesses) x 100
Relevance: Essential for evaluating the effectiveness of return-to-work programs and supporting employee well-being.
Financial Impact: Can lead to reduced workers' compensation costs, improved employee retention, and increased productivity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Employees, investors, and regulators value companies that prioritize employee well-being and support successful return-to-work outcomes.

Unit: CO2e/ unit of output (or ton of production)
Description: A measure of the company's progress in reducing greenhouse gas emissions from its products in use-phase, relative to a baseline. This metric assesses the effectiveness of the company's emissions reduction strategies.
Calculation: (Total CO2e emissions from product fleet - Baseline CO2e emissions) / Total unit of output
Relevance: ERI helps track the company's commitment to reducing emissions and mitigating climate change risks. A decreasing ERI indicates progress toward a low-carbon economy.
Financial Impact: Reducing emissions can lead to cost savings, lower regulatory expenses, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on emissions reduction as a key indicator of a company's sustainability performance.

Description: A measure of the company's ability to design and manufacture products with extended lifespans, reducing the need for frequent replacements and minimizing waste. This metric assesses the company's product design and lifecycle management capabilities.
Calculation: (Number of products with extended lifespan / Total number of products sold) × 100
Relevance: PLER indicates the company's commitment to sustainable product design and reduced waste generation. A higher PLER suggests a more circular economy approach.
Financial Impact: Extended product lifespans can lead to increased customer satisfaction, reduced waste disposal costs, and lower production costs.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and environmental groups value product lifespan extension as a key aspect of sustainable product design.

Unit: Currency (e.g., USD) per unit of output
Description: A measure of the total fuel cost savings realized by customers through the use of the company's fuel-efficient products. This metric assesses the financial benefits of the company's products to customers.
Calculation: Total fuel cost savings = (Fuel efficiency improvement × Total distance traveled × Fuel price)
Relevance: CFCS directly impacts customers' operating costs and provides a financial incentive for purchasing fuel-efficient products.
Financial Impact: Higher CFCS values indicate greater customer value creation, potentially leading to increased sales and market share.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers and investors focus on CFCS as a key indicator of the company's ability to deliver financially material benefits.

Description: A measure of the company's potential regulatory risk exposure related to emissions from its products in use-phase. This metric assesses the company's vulnerability to changing regulatory requirements.
Calculation: ERRE = (Probability of regulatory change × Potential regulatory cost) + (Probability of non-compliance × Potential non-compliance cost)
Relevance: ERRE helps the company manage regulatory risks and anticipate potential costs associated with emissions-related regulations.
Financial Impact: Effective management of ERRE can minimize regulatory expenses, reduce compliance risks, and ensure business continuity.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and executives focus on ERRE as a key indicator of the company's risk management capabilities.

Description: A measure of the company's ability to design and manage products for recyclability and end-of-life management. This metric assesses the company's commitment to a circular economy.
Calculation: (Number of products recycled / Total number of products sold) × 100
Relevance: PELRR indicates the company's focus on sustainable product design, waste reduction, and resource conservation.
Financial Impact: Higher PELRR values can lead to reduced waste disposal costs, lower raw material costs, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Environmental groups, investors, and customers value PELRR as a key indicator of the company's sustainability performance.

Unit: kWh/unit of output (or ton of production)
Description: A measure of the average energy consumption of the company's products in use-phase. This metric assesses the company's ability to design energy-efficient products.
Calculation: Total energy consumption of product fleet / Total unit of output
Relevance: UECPU directly impacts customers' operating costs, energy efficiency, and greenhouse gas emissions.
Financial Impact: Reduced UECPU values can lead to lower energy costs, increased customer satisfaction, and enhanced competitiveness.
Stakeholder Perspective: Customers, investors, and regulators focus on UECPU as a key performance indicator for industrial machinery and goods.

Description: A measure of the company's progress toward achieving its forward-looking emissions reduction targets for products in use-phase. This metric assesses the company's commitment to long-term sustainability goals.
Calculation: (Actual emissions reduction / Target emissions reduction) × 100
Relevance: FLETA indicates the company's ability to set and achieve ambitious sustainability goals, anticipating future regulatory requirements and stakeholder expectations.
Financial Impact: Achieving emissions reduction targets can lead to cost savings, lower regulatory expenses, and enhanced brand reputation.
Stakeholder Perspective: Investors, regulators, and environmental groups focus on FLETA as a key indicator of the company's long-term sustainability strategy and commitment to reducing emissions.
